texts.isa.52.7: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that announceth glad tidings, that publisheth peace; that announceth glad tidings of good, that publisheth salvation, that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth!
texts.isa.52.8: -- The voice of thy watchmen, they lift up the voice, they sing aloud together; for they shall see eye to eye, when Jehovah shall bring again Zion.
texts.isa.52.9: Break forth, sing aloud together, waste places of Jerusalem; for Jehovah comforteth his people, he hath redeemed Jerusalem.
texts.isa.52.10: Jehovah hath made bare his holy arm in the sight of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God.
texts.isa.52.11: -- Depart, depart, go out from thence, touch not what is unclean; go out of the midst of her, be ye clean, that bear the vessels of Jehovah.
texts.isa.52.12: For ye shall not go out with haste, nor go by flight; for Jehovah will go before you, and the God of Israel will be your rear-guard.
texts.isa.52.13: Behold, my servant shall deal prudently; he shall be exalted and be lifted up, and be very high.
texts.isa.52.14: As many were astonished at thee -- his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the children of men
texts.isa.52.15: -- so shall he astonish many nations; kings shall shut their mouths at him: for what had not been told them shall they see, and what they had not heard shall they consider.
texts.isa.53.1: Who hath believed our report? and to whom hath the arm of Jehovah been revealed?
texts.isa.53.2: For he shall grow up before him as a tender sapling, and as a root out of dry ground: he hath no form nor lordliness, and when we see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him.
texts.isa.53.3: He is despised and left alone of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief, and like one from whom [men] hide their faces; -- despised, and we esteemed him not.
texts.isa.53.4: Surely *he* hath borne our griefs and carried our sorrows; and we, we did regard him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted.
texts.isa.53.5: But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities; the chastisement of our peace was upon him, and with his stripes we are healed.
texts.isa.53.6: All we like sheep have gone astray, we have turned every one to his own way; and Jehovah hath laid upon him the iniquity of us all.
texts.isa.53.7: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, but he opened not his mouth; he was led as a lamb to the slaughter, and was as a sheep dumb before her shearers, and he opened not his mouth.
texts.isa.53.8: He was taken from oppression and from judgment; and who shall declare his generation? for he was cut off out of the land of the living; for the transgression of my people was he stricken.
texts.isa.53.9: And [men] appointed his grave with the wicked, but he was with the rich in his death, because he had done no violence, neither was there guile in his mouth.
texts.isa.53.10: Yet it pleased Jehovah to bruise him; he hath subjected [him] to suffering. When thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see a seed, he shall prolong [his] days, and the pleasure of Jehovah shall prosper in his hand.
texts.isa.53.11: He shall see of [the fruit of] the travail of his soul, [and] shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant instruct many in righteousness; and *he* shall bear their iniquities.
texts.isa.53.12: Therefore will I assign him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong: because he hath poured out his soul unto death, and was reckoned with the transgressors; and he bore the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.
texts.isa.54.1: Exult, thou barren, that didst not bear; break forth into singing, and shout for joy, thou that didst not travail with child: for more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife, saith Jehovah.
texts.isa.54.2: Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thy habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes.
texts.isa.54.3: For thou shalt spread abroad on the right hand and on the left; and thy seed shall possess nations, and they shall make desolate cities to be inhabited.
texts.isa.54.4: Fear not, for thou shalt not be ashamed; neither be thou confounded, for thou shalt not be put to shame: for thou shalt forget the shame of thy youth, and shalt not remember the reproach of thy widowhood any more.
texts.isa.54.5: For thy Maker is thy husband: Jehovah of hosts is his name, and thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: the God of the whole earth shall he be called.
texts.isa.54.6: For Jehovah hath called thee as a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit, and as a wife of youth, that hath been refused, saith thy God.
texts.isa.54.7: For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee.
texts.isa.54.8: In the outpouring of wrath have I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting loving-kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith Jehovah, thy Redeemer.
texts.isa.54.9: For this is [as] the waters of Noah unto me, since I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth: so have I sworn that I will no more be wroth with thee, nor rebuke thee.
texts.isa.54.10: For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my loving-kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall my covenant of peace be removed, saith Jehovah, that hath mercy on thee.
texts.isa.54.11: [Thou] afflicted, tossed with tempest, not comforted! Behold, I will set thy stones in antimony, and lay thy foundations with sapphires;
texts.isa.54.12: and I will make thy battlements of rubies, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of precious stones.
texts.isa.54.13: And all thy children [shall be] taught of Jehovah, and great shall be the peace of thy children.
texts.isa.54.14: In righteousness shalt thou be established: thou shalt be far from oppression, for thou shalt not fear; and from terror, for it shall not come near thee.
texts.isa.54.15: Behold, they shall surely gather together, [but] not by me: whosoever gathereth together against thee shall fall because of thee.
texts.isa.54.16: Behold, it is I who have created the smith that bloweth in the fire of coal, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the destroyer to ravage.
texts.isa.54.17: No weapon that is prepared against thee shall prosper; and every tongue that riseth against thee in judgment, thou shalt condemn. This is the inheritance of the servants of Jehovah; and their righteousness is of me, saith Jehovah.
texts.isa.55.1: Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters; and he that hath no money, come ye, buy, and eat: yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price!
texts.isa.55.2: Wherefore do ye spend money for [that which is] not bread? and your labour for that which satisfieth not? Hearken diligently unto me, and eat ye [that which is] good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness.
texts.isa.55.3: Incline your ear, and come unto me; hear, and your soul shall live; and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, the sure mercies of David.
texts.isa.55.4: Behold, I have given him [for] a witness to the peoples, a prince and commander to the peoples.
texts.isa.55.5: Behold, thou shalt call a nation thou knowest not, and a nation [that] knew not thee shall run unto thee, because of Jehovah thy God, and the Holy One of Israel; for he hath glorified thee.
texts.isa.55.6: Seek ye Jehovah while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near.
texts.isa.55.7: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts; and let him return unto Jehovah, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.
texts.isa.55.8: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith Jehovah.
texts.isa.55.9: For [as] the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
texts.isa.55.10: For as the rain cometh down, and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth, and maketh it bring forth and bud, that it may give seed to the sower, and bread to the eater:
texts.isa.55.11: so shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall do that which I please, and it shall accomplish that for which I send it.
texts.isa.55.12: For ye shall go out with joy, and be led forth with peace; the mountains and the hills shall break forth before you into singing, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands.
texts.isa.55.13: Instead of the thorn shall come up the cypress, and instead of the nettle shall come up the myrtle; and it shall be to Jehovah for a name, for an everlasting sign [that] shall not be cut off.
texts.isa.56.1: Thus saith Jehovah: Keep ye judgment and do righteousness; for my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed.
texts.isa.56.2: Blessed is the man that doeth this, and the son of man that holdeth fast to it; that keepeth the sabbath from profaning it, and keepeth his hand from doing any evil.
texts.isa.56.3: And let not the son of the alien, that hath joined himself to Jehovah, speak saying, Jehovah hath entirely separated me from his people; neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree;
texts.isa.56.4: for thus saith Jehovah: Unto the eunuchs that keep my sabbaths, and choose the things that please me, and hold fast to my covenant,
texts.isa.56.5: even unto them will I give in my house and within my walls a place and a name better than of sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name, that shall not be cut off.
texts.isa.56.6: Also the sons of the alien, that join themselves to Jehovah, to minister unto him and to love the name of Jehovah, to be his servants, every one that keepeth the sabbath from profaning it, and holdeth fast to my covenant;
texts.isa.56.7: even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer; their burnt-offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar: for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all the peoples.
texts.isa.56.8: The Lord Jehovah, who gathereth the outcasts of Israel, saith: Yet will I gather [others] to him, with those of his that are gathered.
texts.isa.56.9: All ye beasts of the field, come to devour, all ye beasts in the forest.
texts.isa.56.10: His watchmen are all of them blind, they are without knowledge; they are all dumb dogs that cannot bark, dreaming, lying down, loving to slumber:
texts.isa.56.11: and the dogs are greedy, they know not to be satisfied, and these are shepherds that know not how to discern: they all turn to their own way, every one for his gain, even to the last of them:
texts.isa.56.12: Come, [say they,] I will fetch wine, and we will fill ourselves with strong drink; and to-morrow shall be as this day, [and] much more abundant.
texts.isa.57.1: The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart; and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from before the evil.
texts.isa.57.2: He entereth into peace: they rest in their beds, [each one] that hath walked in his uprightness.
texts.isa.57.3: But draw near hither, ye sons of the sorceress, the seed of the adulterer and the harlot.
texts.isa.57.4: Against whom do ye sport yourselves? Against whom do ye make a wide mouth, [and] draw out the tongue? Are ye not children of transgression, a seed of falsehood,
texts.isa.57.5: inflaming yourselves with idols under every green tree, slaying the children in the valleys under the clefts of the rocks?
texts.isa.57.6: Among the smooth [stones] of the torrent is thy portion; they, they are thy lot: even to them hast thou poured out a drink-offering, thou hast offered an oblation. Shall I be comforted myself as to these things?
texts.isa.57.7: Upon a lofty and high mountain hast thou set thy bed: even thither didst thou go up to offer sacrifice.
texts.isa.57.8: Behind the doors also and the posts hast thou set up thy remembrance: for apart from me, thou hast uncovered thyself, and art gone up; thou hast enlarged thy bed, and hast made agreement with them; thou lovedst their bed, thou sawest their nakedness.
texts.isa.57.9: And thou wentest to the king with ointment, and didst multiply thy perfumes, and didst send thy messengers afar off, and didst debase thyself unto Sheol.
texts.isa.57.10: Thou wast wearied by the multitude of thy ways; [but] thou saidst not, It is of no avail. Thou didst find a quickening of thy strength; therefore thou wast not sick [of it].
texts.isa.57.11: And of whom hast thou been afraid or feared, that thou hast lied, and hast not remembered me, nor taken it to heart? Have not I even of long time held my peace, and thou fearest me not?
texts.isa.57.12: I will declare thy righteousness, and thy works; and they shall not profit thee.
texts.isa.57.13: When thou criest, let them that are gathered by thee deliver thee! But a wind shall carry them all away, a breath shall take them; but he that putteth his trust in me shall inherit the land, and possess my holy mountain.
texts.isa.57.14: And it shall be said, Cast up, cast up, prepare the way, take up the stumbling-blocks out of the way of my people.
texts.isa.57.15: For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, and whose name is Holy: I dwell in the high and holy [place], and with him that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.
texts.isa.57.16: For I will not contend for ever, neither will I be always wroth; for the spirit would fail before me, and the souls [which] I have made.
texts.isa.57.17: For the iniquity of his covetousness was I wroth, and smote him; I hid me, and was wroth, and he went on backslidingly in the way of his heart.
texts.isa.57.18: I have seen his ways, and will heal him; and I will lead him, and will restore comforts unto him and to those of his that mourn.
texts.isa.57.19: I create the fruit of the lips: peace, peace to him [that is] afar off, and to him [that is] nigh, saith Jehovah; and I will heal him.
texts.isa.57.20: But the wicked are like the troubled sea, which cannot rest, and whose waters cast up mire and dirt.
texts.isa.57.21: There is no peace, saith my God, to the wicked.
texts.isa.58.1: Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and declare unto my people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins.
texts.isa.58.2: Yet they seek me daily, and delight to know my ways, as a nation that doeth righteousness, and hath not forsaken the ordinance of their God; they ask of me the ordinances of righteousness, they take delight in approaching to God:
texts.isa.58.3: -- Wherefore have we fasted, and thou seest not; have afflicted our soul, and thou takest no knowledge? Behold, in the day of your fast ye find what pleaseth [you], and exact all your labours.
texts.isa.58.4: Behold, ye have fasted for strife and debate, and to smite with the fist of wickedness; ye do not at present fast, to cause your voice to be heard on high.
texts.isa.58.5: Is such the fast that I have chosen, a day for a man to afflict his soul, -- that he should bow down his head as a bulrush, and spread sackcloth and ashes [under him]? Wilt thou call this a fast, and a day acceptable to Jehovah?
texts.isa.58.6: Is not this the fast which I have chosen: to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the thongs of the yoke, and to send forth free the crushed, and that ye break every yoke?
texts.isa.58.7: Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring to thy house the needy wanderers; when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?
texts.isa.58.8: Then shall thy light break forth as the dawn, and thy health shall spring forth speedily; and thy righteousness shall go before thee, the glory of Jehovah shall be thy rearguard.
texts.isa.58.9: Then shalt thou call, and Jehovah will answer; thou shalt cry, and he will say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger and the unjust speech,
texts.isa.58.10: and thou proffer thy soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul: then shall thy light rise in the darkness, and thine obscurity be as midday;
texts.isa.58.11: and Jehovah will guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and strengthen thy bones; and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a water-spring, whose waters deceive not.
texts.isa.58.12: And they [that come] of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations [that have remained] from generation to generation; and thou shalt be called, Repairer of the breaches, restorer of frequented paths.
texts.isa.58.13: If thou turn back thy foot from the sabbath, [from] doing thy pleasure on my holy day, and call the sabbath a delight, the holy [day] of Jehovah, honourable; and thou honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking [idle] words;
texts.isa.58.14: then shalt thou delight thyself in Jehovah, and I will cause thee to ride on the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of Jehovah hath spoken.
texts.isa.59.1: Behold, Jehovah's hand is not shortened that it cannot save, neither his ear heavy that it cannot hear;
texts.isa.59.2: but your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid [his] face from you, that he doth not hear.
texts.isa.59.3: For your hands are stained with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips speak lies, your tongue muttereth unrighteousness:
texts.isa.59.4: none calleth for justice, none pleadeth in truthfulness. They trust in vanity, and speak falsehood; they conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity.
texts.isa.59.5: They hatch serpents' eggs, and weave the spider's web: he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper.
texts.isa.59.6: Their webs shall not become garments, neither shall they cover themselves with their works; their works are works of iniquity, and the act of violence is in their hands.
texts.isa.59.7: Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood; their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity; wasting and destruction are in their paths;
texts.isa.59.8: the way of peace they know not, and there is no judgment in their goings; they have made their paths crooked: whoso goeth therein knoweth not peace.
texts.isa.59.9: Therefore is justice far from us, and righteousness overtaketh us not: we wait for light, and behold darkness; for brightness, [but] we walk in obscurity.
texts.isa.59.10: We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes: we stumble at midday as in the twilight; amongst the flourishing we are as the dead.
texts.isa.59.11: We roar all like bears, and mourn grievously like doves: we look for judgment, and there is none; for salvation, [but] it is far from us.
texts.isa.59.12: For our transgressions are multiplied before thee, and our sins testify against us; for our transgressions are with us; and our iniquities, we know them:
texts.isa.59.13: in transgressing and lying against Jehovah, and departing away from our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood.
texts.isa.59.14: And judgment is turned away backward, and righteousness standeth afar off; for truth stumbleth in the street, and uprightness cannot enter.
texts.isa.59.15: And truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey. And Jehovah saw [it], and it was evil in his sight that there was no judgment.
texts.isa.59.16: And he saw that there was no man, and he wondered that there was no intercessor; and his arm brought him salvation, and his righteousness, it sustained him.
texts.isa.59.17: And he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on garments of vengeance [for] clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloak.
texts.isa.59.18: According to deeds, so will he repay: fury to his adversaries, recompence to his enemies; to the islands he will repay recompence.
texts.isa.59.19: And they shall fear the name of Jehovah from the west, and from the rising of the sun, his glory. When the adversary shall come in like a flood, the Spirit of Jehovah will lift up a banner against him.
texts.isa.59.20: And the Redeemer will come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob, saith Jehovah.
texts.isa.59.21: And as for me, this is my covenant with them, saith Jehovah: My spirit that is upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed's seed, saith Jehovah, from henceforth and for ever.
texts.isa.60.1: Arise, shine! for thy light is come, and the glory of Jehovah is risen upon thee.
texts.isa.60.2: For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the peoples; but Jehovah will arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen on thee.
texts.isa.60.3: And the nations shall walk by thy light, and kings by the brightness of thy rising.
texts.isa.60.4: Lift up thine eyes round about, and see: all they gather themselves together, they come to thee: thy sons come from afar, and thy daughters are carried upon the side.
texts.isa.60.5: Then thou shalt see, and shalt be brightened, and thy heart shall throb, and be enlarged; for the abundance of the sea shall be turned unto thee, the wealth of the nations shall come unto thee.
texts.isa.60.6: A multitude of camels shall cover thee, young camels of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense; and they shall publish the praises of Jehovah.
texts.isa.60.7: All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered unto thee, the rams of Nebaioth shall serve thee: they shall come up with acceptance on mine altar, and I will beautify the house of my magnificence.
texts.isa.60.8: Who are these that come flying as a cloud, and as doves to their dove-cotes?
texts.isa.60.9: For the isles shall await me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring thy sons from afar, their silver and their gold with them, unto the name of Jehovah thy God, and to the Holy One of Israel, for he hath glorified thee.
texts.isa.60.10: And the sons of the alien shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee. For in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.
texts.isa.60.11: And thy gates shall stand open continually: (they shall not be shut day nor night,) that the wealth of the nations may be brought unto thee, and that their kings may be led [to thee].
texts.isa.60.12: For the nation and the kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; and those nations shall be utterly wasted.
texts.isa.60.13: The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the cypress, pine, and box-tree together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious.
texts.isa.60.14: And the children of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee The city of Jehovah, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
texts.isa.60.15: Instead of thy being forsaken and hated, so that no one went through [thee], I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy from generation to generation.
texts.isa.60.16: And thou shalt suck the milk of the nations, and shalt suck the breast of kings; and thou shalt know that I, Jehovah, [am] thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
texts.isa.60.17: For bronze I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood bronze, and for stones iron; and I will make thine officers peace, and thy rulers righteousness.
texts.isa.60.18: Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders; but thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise.
texts.isa.60.19: The sun shall be no more thy light by day, neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee; but Jehovah shall be thine everlasting light, and thy God thy glory.
texts.isa.60.20: Thy sun shall no more go down, neither shall thy moon withdraw itself; for Jehovah shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended.
texts.isa.60.21: Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall possess the land for ever -- the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.
texts.isa.60.22: The little one shall become a thousand, and the smallest a mighty nation: I, Jehovah, will hasten it in its time.
texts.isa.61.1: The Spirit of the Lord Jehovah is upon me, because Jehovah hath anointed me to announce glad tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the broken-hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and opening of the prison to them that are bound;
texts.isa.61.2: to proclaim the acceptable year of Jehovah, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn;
texts.isa.61.3: to appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, that beauty should be given unto them instead of ashes, the oil of joy instead of mourning, the garment of praise instead of the spirit of heaviness: that they might be called terebinths of righteousness, the planting of Jehovah, that he may be glorified.
texts.isa.61.4: And they shall build the old wastes, they shall raise up the former desolations, and they shall repair the waste cities, the places desolate from generation to generation.
texts.isa.61.5: And strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the alien shall be your ploughmen and your vinedressers.
texts.isa.61.6: But as for you, ye shall be called priests of Jehovah; it shall be said of you: Ministers of our God. Ye shall eat the wealth of the nations, and into their glory shall ye enter.
texts.isa.61.7: Instead of your shame [ye shall have] double; instead of confusion they shall celebrate with joy their portion: therefore in their land they shall possess the double; everlasting joy shall be unto them.
texts.isa.61.8: For I, Jehovah, love judgment, I hate robbery with wrong; and I will give their recompence in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.
texts.isa.61.9: And their seed shall be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are a seed that Jehovah hath blessed.
texts.isa.61.10: I will greatly rejoice in Jehovah, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with the priestly turban, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels.
texts.isa.61.11: For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as a garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth, so the Lord Jehovah will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations.
texts.isa.62.1: For Zion's sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not be still, until her righteousness go forth as brightness, and her salvation as a torch that burneth.
texts.isa.62.2: And the nations shall see thy righteousness, and all kings thy glory; and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of Jehovah will name.
texts.isa.62.3: And thou shalt be a crown of beauty in the hand of Jehovah, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God.
texts.isa.62.4: Thou shalt no more be termed, Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed, Desolate: but thou shalt be called, My delight is in her, and thy land, Married; for Jehovah delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married.
texts.isa.62.5: For [as] a young man marrieth a virgin, shall thy sons marry thee; and with the joy of the bridegroom over the bride, shall thy God rejoice over thee.
texts.isa.62.6: I have set watchmen upon thy walls, Jerusalem; all the day and all the night they shall never hold their peace: ye that put Jehovah in remembrance, keep not silence,
texts.isa.62.7: and give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.
texts.isa.62.8: Jehovah hath sworn by his right hand and by the arm of his strength, I will indeed no more give thy corn [to be] food for thine enemies; and the sons of the alien shall not drink thy new wine, for which thou hast laboured;
texts.isa.62.9: for they that have garnered it shall eat it, and praise Jehovah; and they that have gathered it shall drink it in the courts of my holiness.
texts.isa.62.10: Go through, go through the gates; prepare the way of the people; cast up, cast up the highway; gather out the stones; lift up a banner for the peoples.
texts.isa.62.11: Behold, Jehovah hath proclaimed unto the end of the earth, Say ye to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy salvation cometh; behold, his reward is with him, and his recompence before him.
texts.isa.62.12: And they shall call them, The holy people, The redeemed of Jehovah; and thou shalt be called, The sought out, The city not forsaken.
texts.isa.63.1: Who is this that cometh from Edom, with deep-red garments from Bozrah, this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? -- I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save.
texts.isa.63.2: -- Wherefore is redness in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winevat?
texts.isa.63.3: I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the peoples not a man was with me; and I have trodden them in mine anger, and trampled them in my fury; and their blood is sprinkled upon my garments, and I have stained all mine apparel.
texts.isa.63.4: For the day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redeemed had come.
texts.isa.63.5: And I looked, and there was none to help; and I wondered that there was none to uphold: and mine own arm brought salvation unto me; and my fury, it upheld me.
texts.isa.63.6: And I have trodden down the peoples in mine anger, and made them drunk in my fury; and their blood have I brought down to the earth.
texts.isa.63.7: I will record the loving-kindnesses of Jehovah, the praises of Jehovah, according to all that Jehovah hath bestowed upon us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel which he hath bestowed upon them according to his mercies, and according to the multitude of his loving-kindnesses.
texts.isa.63.8: And he said, They are indeed my people, children that will not lie; and he became their Saviour.
texts.isa.63.9: In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the Angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bore them and carried them all the days of old.
texts.isa.63.10: But they rebelled and grieved his holy Spirit: and he turned to be their enemy; himself, he fought against them.
texts.isa.63.11: But he remembered the days of old, Moses [and] his people: Where is he that brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where is he that put his holy Spirit within him,
texts.isa.63.12: his glorious arm leading them by the right hand of Moses, dividing the waters before them, to make himself an everlasting name,
texts.isa.63.13: -- who led them through the depths, like a horse in the wilderness, [and] they stumbled not?
texts.isa.63.14: As cattle go down into the valley, the Spirit of Jehovah gave them rest; so didst thou lead thy people, to make thyself a glorious name.
texts.isa.63.15: Look down from the heavens, and behold from the habitation of thy holiness and of thy glory! Where is thy zeal and thy strength, the sounding of thy bowels and of thy tender mercies? Are they restrained toward me?
texts.isa.63.16: For thou art our Father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel acknowledge us not: thou, Jehovah, art our Father; our Redeemer, from everlasting, is thy name.
texts.isa.63.17: Why, O Jehovah, hast thou made us to err from thy ways, hast hardened our heart from thy fear? Return for thy servants' sake, the tribes of thine inheritance.
texts.isa.63.18: Thy holy people have possessed [it] but a little while: our adversaries have trodden down thy sanctuary.
texts.isa.63.19: We have become [like those] over whom thou never barest rule, those not called by thy name.
texts.isa.64.1: Oh, that thou wouldest rend the heavens, that thou wouldest come down, -- that the mountains might flow down at thy presence,
texts.isa.64.2: -- as fire kindleth brushwood, as the fire causeth water to boil, to make thy name known to thine adversaries, that the nations might tremble at thy presence!
texts.isa.64.3: When thou didst terrible things [which] we looked not for, thou camest down, and the mountains flowed down at thy presence.
texts.isa.64.4: Never have [men] heard, nor perceived by the ear, nor hath eye seen a God beside thee, who acteth for him that waiteth for him.
texts.isa.64.5: Thou meetest him that rejoiceth to do righteousness, those that remember thee in thy ways: (behold, thou wast wroth, and we have sinned:) in those is perpetuity, and we shall be saved.
texts.isa.64.6: And we are all become as an unclean [thing], and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags; and we all fade as a leaf, and our iniquities, like the wind, have carried us away;
texts.isa.64.7: and there is none that calleth upon thy name, that stirreth up himself to take hold of thee; for thou hast hidden thy face from us, and hast caused us to melt away through our iniquities.
texts.isa.64.8: And now, Jehovah, thou art our Father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand.
texts.isa.64.9: Be not wroth very sore, O Jehovah, neither remember iniquity for ever. Behold, see, we beseech thee, we are all thy people.
texts.isa.64.10: Thy holy cities are become a wilderness, Zion is a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.
texts.isa.64.11: Our holy and our beautiful house, where our fathers praised thee, is burnt up with fire, and all our precious things are laid waste.
texts.isa.64.12: Wilt thou restrain thyself in presence of these things, Jehovah? Wilt thou hold thy peace, and afflict us very sore?
texts.isa.65.1: I am sought out of them that inquired not [for me], I am found of them that sought me not; I have said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name.
texts.isa.65.2: I have stretched out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, who walk in a way not good, after their own thoughts;
texts.isa.65.3: the people that provoke me to anger continually to my face, sacrificing in gardens and burning incense upon the bricks;
texts.isa.65.4: who sit down among the graves, and lodge in the secret places; who eat swine's flesh, and broth of abominable things [is in] their vessels;
texts.isa.65.5: who say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou. These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day.
texts.isa.65.6: Behold, it is written before me: I will not keep silence, but will recompense, even recompense into their bosom,
texts.isa.65.7: your iniquities, and the iniquities of your fathers together, saith Jehovah, who have burned incense upon the mountains, and outraged me upon the hills; and I will measure their former work into their bosom.
texts.isa.65.8: Thus saith Jehovah: As the new wine is found in the cluster, and it is said, Destroy it not, for a blessing is in it; so will I do for my servants' sakes, that I may not destroy [them] all.
texts.isa.65.9: And I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob, and out of Judah a possessor of my mountains; and mine elect shall possess it, and my servants shall dwell there.
texts.isa.65.10: And the Sharon shall be a fold for flocks, and the valley of Achor a couching-place of the herds, for my people that have sought me.
texts.isa.65.11: But ye who forsake Jehovah, who forget my holy mountain, who prepare a table for Gad, and fill up mixed wine unto Meni:
texts.isa.65.12: I will even assign you to the sword, and ye shall all bow down in the slaughter; because I called, and ye did not answer, I spoke, and ye did not hear; but ye did what was evil in mine eyes, and chose that wherein I delight not.
texts.isa.65.13: Therefore thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Behold, my servants shall eat, and *ye* shall be hungry; behold, my servants shall drink, and *ye* shall be thirsty; behold, my servants shall rejoice, and *ye* shall be ashamed;
texts.isa.65.14: behold, my servants shall sing aloud for gladness of heart, and *ye* shall cry out for sorrow of heart, and shall howl for vexation of spirit.
texts.isa.65.15: And ye shall leave your name for a curse unto mine elect; for the Lord Jehovah will slay thee, and will call his servants by another name:
texts.isa.65.16: so that he who blesseth himself in the land shall bless himself by the God of truth; and he that sweareth in the land shall swear by the God of truth: because the former troubles shall be forgotten, and because they shall be hidden from mine eyes.
texts.isa.65.17: For behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.
texts.isa.65.18: But be glad and rejoice for ever in that which I create. For behold, I create Jerusalem a rejoicing, and her people a joy.
texts.isa.65.19: And I will rejoice over Jerusalem, and will joy in my people; and the voice of weeping shall be no more heard in her, nor the voice of crying.
texts.isa.65.20: There shall be no more thenceforth an infant of days, nor an old man that hath not completed his days; for the youth shall die a hundred years old, and the sinner being a hundred years old shall be accursed.
texts.isa.65.21: And they shall build houses, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, and eat the fruit thereof:
texts.isa.65.22: they shall not build, and another inhabit; they shall not plant, and another eat: for as the days of a tree shall be the days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands.
texts.isa.65.23: They shall not labour in vain, nor bring forth for terror; for they are the seed of the blessed of Jehovah, and their offspring with them.
texts.isa.65.24: And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will answer; while they are yet speaking, I will hear.
texts.isa.65.25: The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the ox; and dust shall be the serpent's meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith Jehovah.
texts.isa.66.1: Thus saith Jehovah: The heavens are my throne, and the earth is my footstool: what is the house that ye will build unto me? and what is the place of my rest?
texts.isa.66.2: Even all these things hath my hand made, and all these things have been, saith Jehovah. But to this man will I look: to the afflicted and contrite in spirit, and who trembleth at my word.
texts.isa.66.3: He that slaughtereth an ox, smiteth a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb, breaketh a dog's neck; he that offereth an oblation, [it is as] swine's blood; he that presenteth a memorial of incense, [is as] he that blesseth an idol. As they have chosen their own ways, and their soul delighteth in their abominations,
texts.isa.66.4: I also will choose their calamities, and will bring their fears upon them; because I called, and none answered, I spoke, and they did not hear, but did that which was evil in mine eyes, and chose that wherein I delight not.
texts.isa.66.5: Hear the word of Jehovah, ye that tremble at his word: Your brethren that hated you, that cast you out for my name's sake, said, Let Jehovah be glorified, and let us see your joy! but they shall be ashamed.
texts.isa.66.6: A voice of tumult from the city, a voice from the temple, a voice of Jehovah that rendereth recompence to his enemies!
texts.isa.66.7: Before she travailed, she brought forth; before her pain came, she was delivered of a man-child.
texts.isa.66.8: Who hath heard such a thing? who hath seen such things? Can a land be made to bring forth in one day? shall a nation be born at once? For as soon as Zion travailed, she brought forth her sons.
texts.isa.66.9: Shall I bring to the birth, and not cause to bring forth? saith Jehovah; I who cause to bring forth, shall I shut [the womb]? saith thy God.
texts.isa.66.10: Rejoice with Jerusalem, and be glad for her, all ye that love her; rejoice for joy with her, all ye that mourn over her:
texts.isa.66.11: because ye shall suck, and be satisfied with the breasts of her consolations; because ye shall drink out, and be delighted with the abundance of her glory.
texts.isa.66.12: For thus saith Jehovah: Behold, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the nations like an overflowing torrent; and ye shall suck, ye shall be carried upon the side, and be dandled upon the knees.
texts.isa.66.13: As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you; and ye shall be comforted in Jerusalem.
texts.isa.66.14: And ye shall see [this], and your heart shall rejoice, and your bones shall flourish like the grass; and the hand of Jehovah shall be known toward his servants, and he will have indignation toward his enemies.
texts.isa.66.15: For behold, Jehovah will come with fire, and his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire.
texts.isa.66.16: For by fire and by his sword will Jehovah enter into judgment with all flesh: and the slain of Jehovah shall be many.
texts.isa.66.17: They that sanctify themselves, and purify themselves in the gardens behind one in the midst; that eat swine's flesh, and the abomination, and the mouse, shall perish together, saith Jehovah.
texts.isa.66.18: And I, -- their works and their thoughts [are before me]. ... [The time] cometh for the gathering of all nations and tongues; and they shall come, and see my glory.
texts.isa.66.19: And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those that escape of them unto the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, that draw the bow; to Tubal and Javan, to the isles afar off, that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory: and they shall declare my glory among the nations.
texts.isa.66.20: And they shall bring all your brethren out of all the nations as an oblation unto Jehovah, upon horses, and in chariots, and in covered waggons, and upon mules, and upon dromedaries, to my holy mountain, to Jerusalem, saith Jehovah, as the children of Israel bring an oblation in a clean vessel into the house of Jehovah.
texts.isa.66.21: And I will also take of them for priests [and] for Levites, saith Jehovah.
texts.isa.66.22: For as the new heavens and the new earth which I will make shall remain before me, saith Jehovah, so shall your seed and your name remain.
texts.isa.66.23: And it shall come to pass from new moon to new moon, and from sabbath to sabbath, all flesh shall come to worship before me, saith Jehovah.
texts.isa.66.24: And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorrence unto all flesh.

texts.isa.1.1: The Visions of Isaiah son of Amoz, that he hath seen concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
texts.isa.1.2: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, For Jehovah hath spoken: Sons I have nourished and brought up, And they -- they transgressed against Me.
texts.isa.1.3: An ox hath known its owner, And an ass the crib of its master, Israel hath not known, My people hath not understood.
texts.isa.1.4: Ah, sinning nation, a people heavy [with] iniquity, A seed of evil doers, sons -- corrupters! They have forsaken Jehovah, They have despised the Holy One of Israel, They have gone away backward.
texts.isa.1.5: Wherefore are ye stricken any more? Ye do add apostacy! Every head is become diseased, and every heart [is] sick.
texts.isa.1.6: From the sole of the foot -- unto the head, There is no soundness in it, Wound, and bruise, and fresh smiting! They have not been closed nor bound, Nor have they softened with ointment.
texts.isa.1.7: Your land [is] a desolation, your cities burnt with fire, Your ground, before you strangers are consuming it, And a desolation as overthrown by strangers!
texts.isa.1.8: And left hath been the daughter of Zion, As a booth in a vineyard, As a lodge in a place of cucumbers -- as a city besieged.
texts.isa.1.9: Unless Jehovah of Hosts had left to us a remnant, Shortly -- as Sodom we had been, To Gomorrah we had been like!
texts.isa.1.10: Hear the word of Jehovah, ye rulers of Sodom, Give ear to the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrah,
texts.isa.1.11: `Why to Me the abundance of your sacrifices? saith Jehovah, I have been satiated [with] burnt-offerings of rams, And fat of fatlings; And blood of bullocks, and lambs, And he-goats I have not desired.
texts.isa.1.12: When ye come in to appear before Me, Who hath required this of your hand, To trample My courts?
texts.isa.1.13: Add not to bring in a vain present, Incense -- an abomination it [is] to Me, New moon, and sabbath, calling of convocation! Rendure not iniquity -- and a restraint!
texts.isa.1.14: Your new moons and your set seasons hath My soul hated, They have been upon me for a burden, I have been weary of bearing.
texts.isa.1.15: And in your spreading forth your hands, I hide mine eyes from you, Also when ye increase prayer, I do not hear, Your hands of blood have been full.
texts.isa.1.16: Wash ye, make ye pure, Turn aside the evil of your doings, from before Mine eyes, Cease to do evil, learn to do good.
texts.isa.1.17: Seek judgment, make happy the oppressed, Judge the fatherless, strive [for] the widow.
texts.isa.1.18: Come, I pray you, and we reason, saith Jehovah, If your sins are as scarlet, as snow they shall be white, If they are red as crimson, as wool they shall be!
texts.isa.1.19: If ye are willing, and have hearkened, The good of the land ye consume,
texts.isa.1.20: And if ye refuse, and have rebelled, [By] the sword ye are consumed, For the mouth of Jehovah hath spoken.
texts.isa.1.21: How hath a faithful city become a harlot? I have filled it [with] judgment, Righteousness lodgeth in it -- now murderers.
texts.isa.1.22: Thy silver hath become dross, Thy drink polluted with water.
texts.isa.1.23: Thy princes [are] apostates, and companions of thieves, Every one loving a bribe, and pursuing rewards, The fatherless they judge not, And the plea of the widow cometh not to them.
texts.isa.1.24: Therefore -- the affirmation of the Lord -- Jehovah of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel: Ah, I am eased of Mine adversaries, And I am avenged of Mine enemies,
texts.isa.1.25: And I turn back My hand upon thee, And I refine as purity thy dross, And I turn aside all thy tin,
texts.isa.1.26: And I give back thy judges as at the first, And thy counsellors as in the beginning, After this thou art called, `A city of righteousness -- a faithful city.'
texts.isa.1.27: Zion in judgment is redeemed, And her captivity in righteousness.
texts.isa.1.28: And the destruction of transgressors and sinners [is] together, And those forsaking Jehovah are consumed.
texts.isa.1.29: For [men] are ashamed because of the oaks That ye have desired, And ye are confounded because of the gardens That ye have chosen.
texts.isa.1.30: For ye are as an oak whose leaf is fading, And as a garden that hath no water.
texts.isa.1.31: And the strong hath been for tow, And his work for a spark, And burned have both of them together, And there is none quenching!
texts.isa.2.1: The thing that Isaiah son of Amoz hath seen concerning Judah and Jerusalem:
texts.isa.2.2: And it hath come to pass, In the latter end of the days, Established is the mount of Jehovah's house, Above the top of the mounts, And it hath been lifted up above the heights, And flowed unto it have all the nations.
texts.isa.2.3: And gone have many peoples and said, `Come, and we go up unto the mount of Jehovah, Unto the house of the God of Jacob, And He doth teach us of His ways, And we walk in His paths, For from Zion goeth forth a law, And a word of Jehovah from Jerusalem.
texts.isa.2.4: And He hath judged between the nations, And hath given a decision to many peoples, And they have beat their swords to ploughshares, And their spears to pruning-hooks, Nation doth not lift up sword unto nation, Nor do they learn any more -- war.
texts.isa.2.5: O house of Jacob, come, And we walk in the light of Jehovah.'
texts.isa.2.6: For Thou hast left Thy people, the house of Jacob. For they have been filled from the east, And [are] sorcerers like the Philistines, And with the children of strangers strike hands.
texts.isa.2.7: And its land is full of silver and gold, And there is no end to its treasures, And its land is full of horses, And there is no end to its chariots,
texts.isa.2.8: And its land is full of idols, To the work of its hands it boweth itself, To that which its fingers have made,
texts.isa.2.9: And the low boweth down, and the high is humbled, And Thou acceptest them not.
texts.isa.2.10: Enter into a rock, and be hidden in dust, Because of the fear of Jehovah, And because of the honour of His excellency.
texts.isa.2.11: The haughty eyes of man have been humbled, And bowed down hath been the loftiness of men, And set on high hath Jehovah alone been in that day.
texts.isa.2.12: For a day [is] to Jehovah of Hosts, For every proud and high one, And for every lifted up and low one,
texts.isa.2.13: And for all cedars of Lebanon, The high and the exalted ones, And for all oaks of Bashan,
texts.isa.2.14: And for all the high mountains, And for all the exalted heights,
texts.isa.2.15: And for every high tower, And for every fenced wall,
texts.isa.2.16: And for all ships of Tarshish, And for all desirable pictures.
texts.isa.2.17: And bowed down hath been the haughtiness of man, And humbled the loftiness of men, And set on high hath Jehovah alone been in that day.
texts.isa.2.18: And the idols -- they completely pass away.
texts.isa.2.19: And [men] have entered into caverns of rocks, And into caves of dust, Because of the fear of Jehovah, And because of the honour of His excellency, In His rising to terrify the earth.
texts.isa.2.20: In that day doth man cast his idols of silver, And his idols of gold, That they have made for him to worship, To moles, and to bats,
texts.isa.2.21: To enter into cavities of the rocks, And into clefts of the high places, Because of the fear of Jehovah, And because of the honour of His excellency, In His rising to terrify the earth.
texts.isa.2.22: Cease for you from man, Whose breath [is] in his nostrils, For -- in what is he esteemed?
texts.isa.3.1: For, lo, the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, Is turning aside from Jerusalem, And from Judah, stay and staff, Every stay of bread, and every stay of water.
texts.isa.3.2: Hero and man of war, judge and prophet, And diviner and elder,
texts.isa.3.3: Head of fifty, and accepted of faces, And counsellor, and the wise of artificers, And the intelligent of charmers.
texts.isa.3.4: And I have made youths their heads, And sucklings rule over them.
texts.isa.3.5: And the people hath exacted -- man upon man, Even a man on his neighbour, Enlarge themselves do the youths against the aged, And the lightly esteemed against the honoured.
texts.isa.3.6: When one layeth hold on his brother, [Of] the house of his father, [by] the garment, `Come, a ruler thou art to us, And this ruin [is] under thy hand.'
texts.isa.3.7: He lifteth up, in that day, saying: `I am not a binder up, And in my house is neither bread nor garment, Ye do not make me a ruler of the people.'
texts.isa.3.8: For stumbled hath Jerusalem, and Judah hath fallen, For their tongue and their doings [are] against Jehovah, To provoke the eyes of His glory.
texts.isa.3.9: The appearance of their faces witnessed against them, And their sin, as Sodom, they declared, They have not hidden! Wo to their soul, For they have done to themselves evil.
texts.isa.3.10: Say ye to the righteous, that [it is] good, Because the fruit of their doings they eat.
texts.isa.3.11: Wo to the wicked -- evil, Because the deed of his hand is done to him.
texts.isa.3.12: My people -- its exactors [are] sucklings, And women have ruled over it. My people -- thy eulogists are causing to err, And the way of thy paths swallowed up.
texts.isa.3.13: Jehovah hath stood up to plead, And He is standing to judge the peoples.
texts.isa.3.14: Jehovah into judgment doth enter With elders of His people, and its heads: `And ye, ye have consumed the vineyard, Plunder of the poor [is] in your houses.
texts.isa.3.15: What -- to you? ye bruise My people, And the faces of the poor ye grind.' An affirmation of the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, And Jehovah saith:
texts.isa.3.16: `Because that daughters of Zion have been haughty, And they walk stretching out the neck, And deceiving [with] the eyes, Walking and mincing they go, And with their feet they make a tinkling,
texts.isa.3.17: The Lord also hath scabbed The crown of the head of daughters of Zion, And Jehovah their simplicity exposeth.
texts.isa.3.18: In that day doth the Lord turn aside The beauty of the tinkling ornaments, And of the embroidered works, And of the round tires like moons,
texts.isa.3.19: Of the drops, and the bracelets, and the mufflers,
texts.isa.3.20: Of the bonnets, and the ornaments of the legs, And of the bands, And of the perfume boxes, and the amulets,
texts.isa.3.21: Of the seals, and of the nose-rings,
texts.isa.3.22: Of the costly apparel, and of the mantles, And of the coverings, and of the purses,
texts.isa.3.23: Of the mirrors, and of the linen garments, And of the hoods, and of the vails,
texts.isa.3.24: And it hath been, instead of spice is muck, And instead of a girdle, a rope, And instead of curled work, baldness, And instead of a stomacher a girdle of sackcloth.
texts.isa.3.25: For instead of glory, thy men by sword do fall, And thy might in battle.
texts.isa.3.26: And lamented and mourned have her openings, Yea, she hath been emptied, on the earth she sitteth!
texts.isa.4.1: And taken hold have seven women on one man, In that day, saying, `Our own bread we do eat, And our own raiment we put on, Only, let thy name be called over us, Remove thou our reproach.'
texts.isa.4.2: In that day is the Shoot of Jehovah for desire and for honour, And the fruit of the earth For excellence and for beauty to the escaped of Israel.
texts.isa.4.3: And it hath been, he who is left in Zion, And he who is remaining in Jerusalem, `Holy' is said of him, Of every one who is written for life in Jerusalem.
texts.isa.4.4: If the Lord hath washed away The filth of daughters of Zion, And the blood of Jerusalem purgeth from her midst, By the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning.
texts.isa.4.5: Then hath Jehovah prepared Over every fixed place of Mount Zion, And over her convocations, A cloud by day, and smoke, And the shining of a flaming fire by night, That, over all honour a safe-guard,
texts.isa.4.6: And a covering may be, For a shadow by day from drought, And for a refuge, and for a hiding place, From inundation and from rain!
texts.isa.5.1: Let me sing, I pray you, for my beloved, A song of my beloved as to his vineyard: My beloved hath a vineyard in a fruitful hill,
texts.isa.5.2: And he fenceth it, and casteth out its stones, And planteth it [with] a choice vine, And buildeth a tower in its midst, And also a wine press hath hewn out in it, And he waiteth for the yielding of grapes, And it yieldeth bad ones!
texts.isa.5.3: And now, O inhabitant of Jerusalem, and man of Judah, Judge, I pray you, between me and my vineyard.
texts.isa.5.4: What -- to do still to my vineyard, That I have not done in it! Wherefore, I waited to the yielding of grapes, And it yieldeth bad ones!
texts.isa.5.5: And now, pray, let me cause you to know, That which I am doing to my vineyard, To turn aside its hedge, And it hath been for consumption, To break down its wall, And it hath been for a treading-place.
texts.isa.5.6: And I make it a waste, It is not pruned, nor arranged, And gone up have brier and thorn, And on the thick clouds I lay a charge, From raining upon it rain.
texts.isa.5.7: Because the vineyard of Jehovah of Hosts [Is] the house of Israel, And the man of Judah His pleasant plant, And He waiteth for judgment, and lo, oppression, For righteousness, and lo, a cry.
texts.isa.5.8: Wo [to] those joining house to house, Field to field they bring near, till there is no place, And ye have been settled by yourselves In the midst of the land!
texts.isa.5.9: By the weapons of Jehovah of Hosts Do not many houses a desolation become? Great and good without inhabitant!
texts.isa.5.10: For ten acres of vineyard do yield one bath, And an homer of seed yieldeth an ephah.
texts.isa.5.11: Wo [to] those rising early in the morning, Strong drink they pursue! Tarrying in twilight, wine inflameth them!
texts.isa.5.12: And harp, and psaltery, tabret, and pipe, And wine, have been their banquets, And the work of Jehovah they behold not, Yea, the work of His hands they have not seen.
texts.isa.5.13: Therefore my people removed without knowledge, And its honourable ones are famished, And its multitude dried up of thirst.
texts.isa.5.14: Therefore hath Sheol enlarged herself, And hath opened her mouth without limit. And gone down hath its honour, and its multitude, And its noise, and its exulting one -- into her.
texts.isa.5.15: And bowed down is the low, and humbled the high, And the eyes of the haughty become low,
texts.isa.5.16: And Jehovah of Hosts is high in judgment, And the Holy God sanctified in righteousness,
texts.isa.5.17: And fed have lambs according to their leading, And waste places of the fat ones Do sojourners consume.
texts.isa.5.18: Wo [to] those drawing out iniquity with cords of vanity, And as [with] thick ropes of the cart -- sin.
texts.isa.5.19: Who are saying, `Let Him hurry, Let Him hasten His work, that we may see, And let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel Draw near and come, and we know.'
texts.isa.5.20: Wo [to] those saying to evil `good,' And to good `evil,' Putting darkness for light, and light for darkness, Putting bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter.
texts.isa.5.21: Wo [to] the wise in their own eyes, And -- before their own faces -- intelligent!
texts.isa.5.22: Wo [to] the mighty to drink wine, And men of strength to mingle strong drink.
texts.isa.5.23: Declaring righteous the wicked for a bribe, And the righteousness of the righteous They turn aside from him.
texts.isa.5.24: Therefore, as a tongue of fire devoureth stubble, And flaming hay falleth, Their root is as muck, And their flower as dust goeth up. Because they have rejected the law of Jehovah of Hosts, And the saying of the Holy One of Israel despised.
texts.isa.5.25: Therefore hath the anger of Jehovah burned among His people, And He stretcheth out His hand against it, And smiteth it, and the mountains tremble, And their carcase is as filth in the midst of the out-places. With all this His anger did not turn back, And still His hand is stretched out!
texts.isa.5.26: And He lifted up an ensign to nations afar off, And hissed to it from the end of the earth, And lo, with haste, swift it cometh.
texts.isa.5.27: There is none weary, nor stumbling in it, It doth not slumber, nor sleep, Nor opened hath been the girdle of its loins, Nor drawn away the latchet of its sandals.
texts.isa.5.28: Whose arrows [are] sharp, and all its bows bent, Hoofs of its horses as flint have been reckoned, And its wheels as a hurricane!
texts.isa.5.29: Its roaring [is] like a lioness, It roareth like young lions, And it howleth, and seizeth prey, And carrieth away safely, and there is none delivering.
texts.isa.5.30: And it howleth against it in that day as the howling of a sea, And it hath looked attentively to the land, And lo, darkness -- distress, And light hath been darkened by its abundance!
texts.isa.6.1: In the year of the death of king Uzziah -- I see the Lord, sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and His train is filling the temple.
texts.isa.6.2: Seraphs are standing above it: six wings hath each one; with two [each] covereth its face, and with two [each] covereth its feet, and with two [each] flieth.
texts.isa.6.3: And this one hath called unto that, and hath said: `Holy, Holy, Holy, [is] Jehovah of Hosts, The fulness of all the earth [is] His glory.'
texts.isa.6.4: And the posts of the thresholds are moved by the voice of him who is calling, and the house is full of smoke.
texts.isa.6.5: And I say, `Wo to me, for I have been silent, For a man -- unclean of lips [am] I, And in midst of a people unclean of lips I am dwelling, Because the King, Jehovah of Hosts, have my eyes seen.'
texts.isa.6.6: And flee unto me doth one of the seraphs, and in his hand a burning coal, (with tongs he hath taken [it] from off the altar,)
texts.isa.6.7: and he striketh against my mouth, and saith: `Lo, this hath stricken against thy lips, And turned aside is thine iniquity, And thy sin is covered.'
texts.isa.6.8: And I hear the voice of the Lord, saying: `Whom do I send? and who doth go for Us?' And I say, `Here [am] I, send me.'
texts.isa.6.9: And He saith, `Go, and thou hast said to this people, Hear ye -- to hear, and ye do not understand, And see ye -- to see, and ye do not know.
texts.isa.6.10: Declare fat the heart of this people, And its ears declare heavy, And its eyes declare dazzled, Lest it see with its eyes, And with its ears hear, and its heart consider, And it hath turned back, and hath health.'
texts.isa.6.11: And I say, `Till when, O Lord?' And He saith, `Surely till cities have been wasted without inhabitant, And houses without man, And the ground be wasted -- a desolation,
texts.isa.6.12: And Jehovah hath put man far off, And great [is] the forsaken part in the heart of the land.
texts.isa.6.13: And yet in it a tenth, and it hath turned, And hath been for a burning, As a teil-tree, and as an oak, that in falling, Have substance in them, The holy seed [is] its substance!'
texts.isa.7.1: And it cometh to pass in the days of Ahaz, son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, gone up hath Rezin king of Aram, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, to Jerusalem, to battle against it, and he is not able to fight against it.
texts.isa.7.2: And it is declared to the house of David, saying, `Aram hath been led towards Ephraim,' And his heart and the heart of his people is moved, like the moving of trees of a forest by the presence of wind.
texts.isa.7.3: And Jehovah saith unto Isaiah, `Go forth, I pray thee, to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shear-Jashub thy son, unto the end of the conduit of the upper pool, unto the highway of the fuller's field,
texts.isa.7.4: and thou hast said unto him: `Take heed, and be quiet, fear not, And let not thy heart be timid, Because of these two tails of smoking brands, For the fierceness of the anger of Rezin and Aram, And the son of Remaliah.
texts.isa.7.5: Because that Aram counselled against thee evil, Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, saying:
texts.isa.7.6: We go up into Judah, and we vex it, And we rend it unto ourselves, And we cause a king to reign in its midst -- The son of Tabeal.
texts.isa.7.7: Thus said the Lord Jehovah: It doth not stand, nor shall it be!
texts.isa.7.8: For the head of Aram [is] Damascus, And the head of Damascus [is] Rezin, And within sixty and five years Is Ephraim broken from [being] a people.
texts.isa.7.9: And the head of Ephraim [is] Samaria, And the head of Samaria [is] the son of Remaliah. If ye do not give credence, Surely ye are not stedfast.'
texts.isa.7.10: And Jehovah addeth to speak unto Ahaz, saying:
texts.isa.7.11: `Ask for thee a sign from Jehovah thy God, Make deep the request, or make [it] high upwards.'
texts.isa.7.12: And Ahaz saith, `I do not ask nor try Jehovah.'
texts.isa.7.13: And he saith, `Hear, I pray you, O house of David, Is it a little thing for you to weary men, That ye weary also my God?
texts.isa.7.14: Therefore the Lord Himself giveth to you a sign, Lo, the Virgin is conceiving, And is bringing forth a son, And hath called his name Immanuel,
texts.isa.7.15: Butter and honey he doth eat, When he knoweth to refuse evil, and to fix on good.
texts.isa.7.16: For before the youth doth know To refuse evil, and to fix on good, Forsaken is the land thou art vexed with, because of her two kings.
texts.isa.7.17: Jehovah bringeth on thee, and on thy people, And on the house of thy father, Days that have not come, Even from the day of the turning aside of Ephraim from Judah, By the king of Asshur.
texts.isa.7.18: And it hath come to pass, in that day, Jehovah doth hiss for a fly that [is] in the extremity of the brooks of Egypt, And for a bee that [is] in the land of Asshur.
texts.isa.7.19: And they have come, and rested all of them in the desolate valleys, And in holes of the rocks, and on all the thorns, And on all the commendable things.
texts.isa.7.20: In that day doth the Lord shave, By a razor that is hired beyond the river, By the king of Asshur, The head, and the hair of the feet, Yea, also the beard it consumeth.
texts.isa.7.21: And it hath come to pass, in that day, A man keepeth alive a heifer of the herd, And two of the flock,
texts.isa.7.22: And it hath come to pass, From the abundance of the yielding of milk he eateth butter, For butter and honey doth every one eat Who is left in the heart of the land.
texts.isa.7.23: And it hath come to pass, in that day, Every place where there are a thousand vines, At a thousand silverlings, Is for briers and for thorns.
texts.isa.7.24: With arrows and with bow he cometh thither, Because all the land is brier and thorn.
texts.isa.7.25: And all the hills that with a mattock are kept in order, Thither cometh not the fear of brier and thorn, And it hath been for the sending forth of ox, And for the treading of sheep!'
texts.isa.8.1: And Jehovah saith unto me, `Take to thee a great tablet, and write upon it with a graving tool of man, To haste spoil, enjoy prey.'
texts.isa.8.2: And I cause faithful witnesses to testify to me, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah.
texts.isa.8.3: And I draw near unto the prophetess, and she conceiveth, and beareth a son; and Jehovah saith unto me, `Call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz,
texts.isa.8.4: for before the youth doth know to cry, My father, and My mother, one taketh away the wealth of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria, before the king of Asshur.'
texts.isa.8.5: And Jehovah addeth to speak unto me again, saying:
texts.isa.8.6: `Because that this people hath refused The waters of Shiloah that go softly, And is rejoicing with Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
texts.isa.8.7: Therefore, lo, the Lord is bringing up on them, The waters of the river, the mighty and the great, (The king of Asshur, and all his glory,) And it hath gone up over all its streams, And hath gone on over all its banks.
texts.isa.8.8: And it hath passed on into Judah, It hath overflown and passed over, Unto the neck it cometh, And the stretching out of its wings Hath been the fulness of the breadth of thy land, O Emmanu-El!
texts.isa.8.9: Be friends, O nations, and be broken, And give ear, all ye far off ones of earth, Gird yourselves, and be broken, Gird yourselves, and be broken.
texts.isa.8.10: Take counsel, and it is broken, Speak a word, and it doth not stand, Because of Emmanu-El!'
texts.isa.8.11: For thus hath Jehovah spoken unto me with strength of hand, and instructeth me against walking in the way of this people, saying,
texts.isa.8.12: `Ye do not say, A confederacy, To all to whom this people saith, A confederacy, And its fear ye do not fear, Nor declare fearful.
texts.isa.8.13: Jehovah of Hosts -- Him ye do sanctify, And He [is] your Fear, and He your Dread,
texts.isa.8.14: And He hath been for a sanctuary, And for a stone of stumbling, and for a rock of falling, To the two houses of Israel, For a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
texts.isa.8.15: And many among them have stumbled and fallen, And been broken, and snared, and captured.
texts.isa.8.16: Bind up the testimony, Seal the law among My disciples.
texts.isa.8.17: And I have waited for Jehovah, Who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob, And I have looked for Him.
texts.isa.8.18: Lo, I, and the children whom Jehovah hath given to me, [Are] for signs and for wonders in Israel, From Jehovah of Hosts, who is dwelling in Mount Zion.
texts.isa.8.19: And when they say unto you, `Seek unto those having familiar spirits, And unto wizards, who chatter and mutter, Doth not a people seek unto its God? -- For the living unto the dead!
texts.isa.8.20: To the law and to the testimony! If not, let them say after this manner, `That there is no dawn to it.'
texts.isa.8.21: -- And it hath passed over into it, hardened and hungry, And it hath come to pass, That it is hungry, and hath been wroth, And made light of its king, and of its God, And hath looked upwards.
texts.isa.8.22: And unto the land it looketh attentively, And lo, adversity and darkness! -- Dimness, distress, and thick darkness is driven away, But not the dimness for which she is in distress!
texts.isa.9.1: As the former time made light The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, So the latter hath honoured the way of the sea, Beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
texts.isa.9.2: The people who are walking in darkness Have seen a great light, Dwellers in a land of death-shade, Light hath shone upon them.
texts.isa.9.3: Thou hast multiplied the nation, Thou hast made great its joy, They have joyed before Thee as the joy in harvest, As [men] rejoice in their apportioning spoil.
texts.isa.9.4: Because the yoke of its burden, And the staff of its shoulder, the rod of its exactor, Thou hast broken as [in] the day of Midian.
texts.isa.9.5: For every battle of a warrior [is] with rushing, and raiment rolled in blood, And it hath been for burning -- fuel of fire.
texts.isa.9.6: For a Child hath been born to us, A Son hath been given to us, And the princely power is on his shoulder, And He doth call his name Wonderful, Counsellor, Mighty God, Father of Eternity, Prince of Peace.
texts.isa.9.7: To the increase of the princely power, And of peace, there is no end, On the throne of David, and on his kingdom, To establish it, and to support it, In judgment and in righteousness, Henceforth, even unto the age, The zeal of Jehovah of Hosts doth this.
texts.isa.9.8: A word hath the Lord sent into Jacob, And it hath fallen in Israel.
texts.isa.9.9: And the people have known -- all of it, Ephraim, and the inhabitant of Samaria, In pride and in greatness of heart, saying,
texts.isa.9.10: `Bricks have fallen, and hewn work we build, Sycamores have been cut down, and cedars we renew.'
texts.isa.9.11: And Jehovah setteth the adversaries of Rezin on high above him, And his enemies he joineth together,
texts.isa.9.12: Aram from before, and Philistia from behind, And they devour Israel with the whole mouth. With all this not turned back hath His anger, And still His hand is stretched out.
texts.isa.9.13: And the people hath not turned back unto Him who is smiting it, And Jehovah of Hosts they have not sought.
texts.isa.9.14: And Jehovah cutteth off from Israel head and tail, Branch and reed -- the same day,
texts.isa.9.15: Elder, and accepted of face, he [is] the head, Prophet, teacher of falsehood, he [is] the tail.
texts.isa.9.16: And the eulogists of this people are causing to err, And its eulogised ones are consumed.
texts.isa.9.17: Therefore, over its young men the Lord rejoiceth not, And its orphans, and its widows He pitieth not, For every one [is] profane, and an evil doer, And every mouth is speaking folly. With all this not turned back hath His anger, And still His hand is stretched out.
texts.isa.9.18: For burned as a fire hath wickedness, Brier and thorn it devoureth, And it kindleth in thickets of the forest, And they lift themselves up, an exaltation of smoke!
texts.isa.9.19: In the wrath of Jehovah of Hosts Hath the land been consumed, And the people is as fuel of fire; A man on his brother hath no pity,
texts.isa.9.20: And cutteth down on the right, and hath been hungry, And he devoureth on the left, And they have not been satisfied, Each the flesh of his own arm they devour.
texts.isa.9.21: Manasseh -- Ephraim, and Ephraim -- Manasseh, Together they [are] against Judah, With all this not turned back hath His anger. And still His hand is stretched out!
texts.isa.10.1: Wo [to] those decreeing decrees of iniquity, And writers who have prescribed perverseness.
texts.isa.10.2: To turn aside from judgment the poor, And to take violently away the judgment Of the afflicted of My people, That widows may be their prey, That the fatherless they may spoil.
texts.isa.10.3: And what do ye at a day of inspection? And at desolation? -- from afar it cometh. Near whom do ye flee for help? And where do ye leave your honour?
texts.isa.10.4: Without Me it hath bowed down In the place of a bound one, And in the place of the slain they fall. With all this not turned back hath His anger, And still His hand is stretched out.
texts.isa.10.5: Wo [to] Asshur, a rod of Mine anger, And a staff in their hand [is] Mine indignation.
texts.isa.10.6: Against a profane nation I send him, And concerning a people of My wrath I charge him, To spoil spoil, and to seize prey, And to make it a treading-place as the clay of out places.
texts.isa.10.7: And he -- he thinketh not so, And his heart reckoneth not so, For -- to destroy [is] in his heart, And to cut off nations not a few.
texts.isa.10.8: For he saith, `Are not my princes altogether kings?
texts.isa.10.9: Is not Calno as Carchemish? Is not Hamath as Arpad? Is not Samaria as Damascus?
texts.isa.10.10: As my hand hath got to the kingdoms of a worthless thing, and their graven images, [Greater] than Jerusalem and than Samaria,
texts.isa.10.11: Do I not -- as I have done to Samaria, And to her worthless things, So do to Jerusalem and to her grievous things?
texts.isa.10.12: And it hath come to pass, When the Lord doth fulfil all His work In mount Zion and in Jerusalem, I see concerning the fruit of the greatness Of the heart of the king of Asshur. And concerning the glory of the height of his eyes.
texts.isa.10.13: For he hath said, `By the power of my hand I have wrought, And by my wisdom, for I have been intelligent, And I remove borders of the peoples, And their chief ones I have spoiled, And I put down as a mighty one the inhabitants,
texts.isa.10.14: And my hand as to a nest Getteth to the wealth of the peoples, And as a gathering of forsaken eggs All the earth I -- I have gathered, And there hath not been one moving wing, Or opening mouth, or whispering.'
texts.isa.10.15: -- Doth the axe glorify itself Against him who is hewing with it? Doth the saw magnify itself Against him who is shaking it? As a rod waving those lifting it up! As a staff lifting up that which is not wood!
texts.isa.10.16: Therefore doth the Lord, the Lord of Hosts, Send among his fat ones leanness, And under his honour He kindleth a burning As the burning of a fire.
texts.isa.10.17: And the light of Israel hath been for a fire, And his Holy One for a flame, And it hath burned, and devoured his thorn And his brier in one day.
texts.isa.10.18: And the honour of his forest, and his fruitful field, From soul even unto flesh He doth consume, And it hath been as the fainting of a standard-bearer.
texts.isa.10.19: And the rest of the trees of his forest [are] few, And a youth doth write them.
texts.isa.10.20: And it hath come to pass, in that day, The remnant of Israel, And the escaped of the house of Jacob, Do not add any more to lean on its smiter, And have leant on Jehovah, The Holy One of Israel, in truth.
texts.isa.10.21: A remnant returneth -- a remnant of Jacob, Unto the Mighty God.
texts.isa.10.22: For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, A remnant doth return of it, A consumption determined, Overflowing [with] righteousness.
texts.isa.10.23: For a consumption that is determined, The Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, Is making in the midst of all the land.
texts.isa.10.24: Therefore, thus said the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, `Be not afraid, my people, inhabiting Zion, because of Asshur, With a rod he doth smite thee, And his staff lifteth up against thee, in the way of Egypt.
texts.isa.10.25: For yet a very little, And the indignation hath been completed, And Mine anger by their wearing out.
texts.isa.10.26: And awaking for him is Jehovah of Hosts, A scourge like the smiting of Midian at the rock Oreb, And his rod [is] over the sea, And he hath lifted it in the way of Egypt.
texts.isa.10.27: And it hath come to pass, in that day, Turned is his burden from off thy shoulder, And his yoke from off thy neck, And destroyed hath been the yoke, because of prosperity.
texts.isa.10.28: He hath come in against Aiath, He hath passed over into Migron, At Michmash he looketh after his vessels.
texts.isa.10.29: They have gone over the passage, Geba they have made a lodging place, Trembled hath Rama, Gibeah of Saul fled.
texts.isa.10.30: Cry aloud [with] thy voice, daughter of Gallim, Give attention, Laish! answer her, Anathoth.
texts.isa.10.31: Fled away hath Madmenah, The inhabitants of the high places have hardened themselves.
texts.isa.10.32: Yet to-day in Nob to remain, Wave its hand doth the mount of the daughter of Zion, The hill of Jerusalem.
texts.isa.10.33: Lo, the Lord, Jehovah of Hosts, Is lopping a branch with violence, And the high of stature are cut down, And the lofty are become low,
texts.isa.10.34: And He hath gone round the thickets of the forest with iron, And Lebanon by a mighty one falleth!
texts.isa.11.1: And a rod hath come out from the stock of Jesse, And a branch from his roots is fruitful.
texts.isa.11.2: Rested on him hath the Spirit of Jehovah, The spirit of wisdom and understanding, The spirit of counsel and might, The spirit of knowledge and fear of Jehovah.
texts.isa.11.3: To refresh him in the fear of Jehovah, And by the sight of his eyes he judgeth not, Nor by the hearing of his ears decideth.
texts.isa.11.4: And he hath judged in righteousness the poor, And decided in uprightness for the humble of earth, And hath smitten earth with the rod of his mouth, And with the breath of his lips he putteth the wicked to death.
texts.isa.11.5: And righteousness hath been the girdle of his loins, And faithfulness -- the girdle of his reins.
texts.isa.11.6: And a wolf hath sojourned with a lamb, And a leopard with a kid doth lie down, And calf, and young lion, and fatling [are] together, And a little youth is leader over them.
texts.isa.11.7: And cow and bear do feed, Together lie down their young ones, And a lion as an ox eateth straw.
texts.isa.11.8: And played hath a suckling by the hole of an asp, And on the den of a cockatrice Hath the weaned one put his hand.
texts.isa.11.9: Evil they do not, nor destroy in all My holy mountain, For full hath been the earth with the knowledge of Jehovah, As the waters are covering the sea.
texts.isa.11.10: And there hath been, in that day, A root of Jesse that is standing for an ensign of peoples, Unto him do nations seek, And his rest hath been -- honour!
texts.isa.11.11: And it hath come to pass, in that day, The Lord addeth a second time his power, To get the remnant of His people that is left, From Asshur, and from Egypt, And from Pathros, and from Cush, And from Elam, and from Shinar, And from Hamath, and from isles of the sea,
