texts.isa.38.4: And a word of Jehovah is unto Isaiah, saying,
texts.isa.38.5: Go, and thou hast said to Hezekiah, Thus said Jehovah, God of David thy father, `I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tear, lo, I am adding to thy days fifteen years,
texts.isa.38.6: and out of the hand of the king of Asshur I deliver thee and this city, and have covered over this city.
texts.isa.38.7: And this [is] to thee the sign from Jehovah, that Jehovah doth this thing that He hath spoken.
texts.isa.38.8: Lo, I am bringing back the shadow of the degrees that it hath gone down on the degrees of Ahaz, by the sun, backward ten degrees:' and the sun turneth back ten degrees in the degrees that it had gone down.
texts.isa.38.9: A writing of Hezekiah king of Judah concerning his being sick, when he reviveth from his sickness:
texts.isa.38.10: `I -- I said in the cutting off of my days, I go in to the gates of Sheol, I have numbered the remnant of mine years.
texts.isa.38.11: I said, I do not see Jah -- Jah! In the land of the living, I do not behold man any more, With the inhabitants of the world.
texts.isa.38.12: My sojourning hath departed, And been removed from me as a shepherd's tent, I have drawn together, as a weaver, my life, By weakness it cutteth me off, From day unto night Thou dost end me.
texts.isa.38.13: I have set [Him] till morning as a lion, So doth He break all my bones, From day unto night Thou dost end me.
texts.isa.38.14: As a crane -- a swallow -- so I chatter, I mourn as a dove, Drawn up have been mine eyes on high, O Jehovah, oppression [is] on me, be my surety.
texts.isa.38.15: -- What do I say? seeing He said to me, And He Himself hath wrought, I go softly all my years for the bitterness of my soul.
texts.isa.38.16: Lord, by these do [men] live, And by all in them [is] the life of my spirit, And Thou savest me, make me also to live,
texts.isa.38.17: Lo, to peace He changed for me bitterness, And Thou hast delighted in my soul without corruption, For Thou hast cast behind Thy back all my sins.
texts.isa.38.18: For Sheol doth not confess Thee, Death doth not praise Thee, Those going down to the pit hope not for Thy truth.
texts.isa.38.19: The living, the living, he doth confess Thee.
texts.isa.38.20: Like myself to-day -- a father to sons Doth make known of Thy faithfulness, O Jehovah -- to save me: And my songs we sing all days of our lives In the house of Jehovah.'
texts.isa.38.21: And Isaiah saith, `Let them take a bunch of figs, and plaster over the ulcer, and he liveth.'
texts.isa.38.22: And Hezekiah saith, `What [is] the sign that I go up to the house of Jehovah!'
texts.isa.39.1: At that time hath Merodach-Baladan, son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present unto Hezekiah, when he heareth that he hath been sick, and is become strong.
texts.isa.39.2: And Hezekiah rejoiceth over them, and sheweth them the house of his spices, the silver, and the gold, and the spices, and the good ointment, and all the house of his vessels, and all that hath been found in his treasures; there hath not been a thing in his house, and in all his dominion, that Hezekiah hath not shewed them.
texts.isa.39.3: And Isaiah the prophet cometh in unto king Hezekiah, and saith unto him, `What said these men? and whence come they unto thee?' And Hezekiah saith, `From a land afar off they have come unto me -- from Babylon.'
texts.isa.39.4: And he saith, `What saw they in thy house?' and Hezekiah saith, `All that [is] in my house they saw; there hath not been a thing that I have not shewed them among my treasures.'
texts.isa.39.5: And Isaiah saith unto Hezekiah, `Hear a word of Jehovah of Hosts:
texts.isa.39.6: Lo, days are coming, and borne hath been all that [is] in thy house, and that thy fathers have treasured up till this day, to Babylon; there is not left a thing, said Jehovah;
texts.isa.39.7: and of thy sons who come forth from thee, whom thou begettest, they take, and they have been eunuchs in a palace of the king of Babylon.'
texts.isa.39.8: And Hezekiah saith unto Isaiah, `Good [is] the word of Jehovah that thou hast spoken;' and he saith, `Because there is peace and truth in my days.'
texts.isa.40.1: Comfort ye, comfort ye, My people, saith your God.
texts.isa.40.2: Speak to the heart of Jerusalem, and call to her, That her warfare hath been completed, That accepted hath been her punishment, That she hath received from the hand of Jehovah Double for all her sins.
texts.isa.40.3: A voice is crying -- in a wilderness -- Prepare ye the way of Jehovah, Make straight in a desert a highway to our God.
texts.isa.40.4: Every valley is raised up, And every mountain and hill become low, And the crooked place hath become a plain, And the entangled places a valley.
texts.isa.40.5: And revealed hath been the honour of Jehovah, And seen [it] have all flesh together, For the mouth of Jehovah hath spoken.
texts.isa.40.6: A voice is saying, `Call,' And he said, `What do I call?' All flesh [is] grass, and all its goodliness [is] As a flower of the field:
texts.isa.40.7: Withered hath grass, faded the flower, For the Spirit of Jehovah blew upon it, Surely the people [is] grass;
texts.isa.40.8: Withered hath grass, faded the flower, But a word of our God riseth for ever.
texts.isa.40.9: On a high mountain get thee up, O Zion, Proclaiming tidings, Lift up with power thy voice, O Jerusalem, proclaiming tidings, Lift up, fear not, say to cities of Judah, `Lo, your God.'
texts.isa.40.10: Lo, the Lord Jehovah with strength cometh, And His arm is ruling for Him, Lo, His hire [is] with Him, and His wage before Him.
texts.isa.40.11: As a shepherd His flock He feedeth, With His arm He gathereth lambs, And in His bosom He carrieth [them]: Suckling ones He leadeth.
texts.isa.40.12: Who hath measured in the hollow of his hand the waters? And the heavens by a span hath meted out, And comprehended in a measure the dust of the earth, And hath weighed in scales the mountains, And the hills in a balance?
texts.isa.40.13: Who hath meted out the Spirit of Jehovah, And, [being] His counsellor, doth teach Him!
texts.isa.40.14: With whom consulted He, That he causeth Him to understand? And teacheth Him in the path of judgment, And teacheth Him knowledge? And the way of understanding causeth Him to know?
texts.isa.40.15: Lo, nations as a drop from a bucket, And as small dust of the balance, have been reckoned, Lo, isles as a small thing He taketh up.
texts.isa.40.16: And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, Nor its beasts sufficient for a burnt-offering.
texts.isa.40.17: All the nations [are] as nothing before Him, Less than nothing and emptiness, They have been reckoned to Him.
texts.isa.40.18: And unto whom do ye liken God, And what likeness do ye compare to Him?
texts.isa.40.19: The graven image poured out hath a artizan, And a refiner with gold spreadeth it over, And chains of silver he is refining.
texts.isa.40.20: He who is poor [by] heave-offerings, A tree not rotten doth choose, A skilful artizan he seeketh for it, To establish a graven image -- not moved.
texts.isa.40.21: Do ye not know -- do ye not hear? Hath it not been declared from the first to you? Have ye not understood [From] the foundations of the earth?
texts.isa.40.22: He who is sitting on the circle of the earth, And its inhabitants [are] as grasshoppers, He who is stretching out as a thin thing the heavens, And spreadeth them as a tent to dwell in.
texts.isa.40.23: He who is making princes become nothing, Judges of earth as emptiness hath made;
texts.isa.40.24: Yea, they have not been planted, Yea, they have not been sown, Yea, not taking root in the earth is their stock, And also He hath blown upon them, and they wither, And a whirlwind as stubble taketh them away.
texts.isa.40.25: And unto whom do ye liken Me, And [am] I equal? saith the Holy One.
texts.isa.40.26: Lift up on high your eyes, And see -- who hath prepared these? He who is bringing out by number their host, To all of them by name He calleth, By abundance of strength (And [he is] strong in power) not one is lacking.
texts.isa.40.27: Why sayest thou, O Jacob? and speakest thou, O Israel? `My way hath been hid from Jehovah, And from my God my judgment passeth over.'
texts.isa.40.28: Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard? The God of the age -- Jehovah, Preparer of the ends of the earth, Is not wearied nor fatigued, There is no searching of His understanding.
texts.isa.40.29: He is giving power to the weary, And to those not strong He increaseth might.
texts.isa.40.30: Even youths are wearied and fatigued, And young men utterly stumble,
texts.isa.40.31: But those expecting Jehovah pass [to] power, They raise up the pinion as eagles, They run and are not fatigued, They go on and do not faint!
texts.isa.41.1: Keep silent towards Me, O isles, And the peoples pass on [to] power, They come nigh, then they speak, `Together -- to judgment we draw near.'
texts.isa.41.2: Who stirred up from the east a righteous one? He calleth him to His foot, He giveth before him nations, And kings He causeth him to rule, He giveth [them] as dust [to] his sword, As driven stubble [to] his bow.
texts.isa.41.3: He pursueth them, he passeth over in safety A path with his feet he entereth not.
texts.isa.41.4: Who hath wrought and done, Calling the generations from the first? I, Jehovah, the first, and with the last I [am] He.
texts.isa.41.5: Seen have isles and fear, ends of the earth tremble, They have drawn near, yea, they come.
texts.isa.41.6: Each his neighbour they help, And to his brother he saith, `Be strong.'
texts.isa.41.7: And strengthen doth an artizan the refiner, A smoother [with] a hammer, Him who is beating [on] an anvil, Saying, `For joining it [is] good,' And he strengtheneth it with nails, it is not moved!
texts.isa.41.8: -- And thou, O Israel, My servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, Seed of Abraham, My lover,
texts.isa.41.9: Whom I have taken hold of, from the ends of the earth, And from its near places I have called thee, And I say to thee, My servant Thou [art], I have chosen thee, and not rejected thee.
texts.isa.41.10: Be not afraid, for with thee I [am], Look not around, for I [am] thy God, I have strengthened thee, Yea, I have helped thee, yea, I upheld thee, With the right hand of My righteousness.
texts.isa.41.11: Lo, all those displeased with thee, They are ashamed and blush, They are as nothing, yea, perish Do the men who strive with thee.
texts.isa.41.12: Thou seekest them, and findest them not, The men who debate with thee, They are as nothing, yea, as nothing, The men who war with thee.
texts.isa.41.13: For I, Jehovah thy God, Am strengthening thy right hand, He who is saying to thee, `Fear not, I have helped thee.'
texts.isa.41.14: Fear not, O worm Jacob, ye men of Israel, I helped thee, an affirmation of Jehovah, Even thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.
texts.isa.41.15: Lo, I have set thee for a new sharp threshing instrument, Possessing teeth, thou threshest mountains, And beatest small, and hills as chaff thou makest.
texts.isa.41.16: Thou winnowest them, and a wind lifteth them up, And a whirlwind scattereth them, And thou -- thou rejoicest in Jehovah, In the Holy One of Israel dost boast thyself.
texts.isa.41.17: The poor and the needy are seeking water, And there is none, Their tongue with thirst hath failed, I, Jehovah do answer them, The God of Israel -- I forsake them not.
texts.isa.41.18: I open on high places rivers, And in midst of valleys fountains, I make a wilderness become a pond of water, And a dry land become springs of water.
texts.isa.41.19: I give in a wilderness the cedar, Shittah, and myrtle, and oil-tree, I set in a desert the fir-pine and box-wood together.
texts.isa.41.20: So that they see, and know, And regard, and act wisely together, For the hand of Jehovah hath done this, And the Holy One of Israel hath prepared it.
texts.isa.41.21: Bring near your cause, saith Jehovah, Bring nigh your mighty ones, saith the king of Jacob.
texts.isa.41.22: They bring nigh, and declare to us that which doth happen, The first things -- what they [are] declare ye, And we set our heart, and know their latter end, Or the coming things cause us to hear.
texts.isa.41.23: Declare the things that are coming hereafter, And we know that ye [are] gods, Yea, ye may do good or do evil, And we look around and see [it] together.
texts.isa.41.24: Lo, ye [are] of nothing, and your work of nought, An abomination -- it fixeth on you.
texts.isa.41.25: I have stirred up [one] from the north, And he cometh, From the rising of the sun he calleth in My name, And he cometh in [on] prefects as [on] clay, And as a potter treadeth down mire.
texts.isa.41.26: Who hath declared from the first, and we know? And beforetime, and we say, `Righteous?' yea, there is none declaring, Yea, there is none proclaiming, Yea, there is none hearing your sayings.
texts.isa.41.27: First to Zion, Behold, behold them, And to Jerusalem one proclaiming tidings I give,
texts.isa.41.28: And I see that there is no man, Yea, of these that there is no counsellor, And I ask them, and they return word:
texts.isa.41.29: `Lo, all of them [are] vanity, Nought [are] their works, Wind and emptiness their molten images!'
texts.isa.42.1: Lo, My servant, I take hold on him, My chosen one -- My soul hath accepted, I have put My Spirit upon him, Judgment to nations he bringeth forth.
texts.isa.42.2: He doth not cry, nor lift up, Nor cause his voice to be heard, in the street.
texts.isa.42.3: A bruised reed he breaketh not, And dim flax he quencheth not, To truth he bringeth forth judgment.
texts.isa.42.4: He doth not become weak nor bruised, Till he setteth judgment in the earth, And for his law isles wait with hope.
texts.isa.42.5: Thus said God, Jehovah, preparing The heavens, and stretching them out, Spreading out the earth and its productions, Giving breath to the people on it, And spirit to those walking in it.
texts.isa.42.6: I, Jehovah, did call thee in righteousness, And I lay hold on thy hand, and keep thee, And I give thee for a covenant of a people, And a light of nations.
texts.isa.42.7: To open the eyes of the blind, To bring forth from prison the bound one, From the house of restraint those sitting in darkness.
texts.isa.42.8: I [am] Jehovah, this [is] My name, And Mine honour to another I give not, Nor My praise to graven images.
texts.isa.42.9: The former things, lo, have come, And new things I am declaring, Before they spring up I cause you to hear.
texts.isa.42.10: Sing to Jehovah a new song, His praise from the end of the earth, Ye who are going down to the sea, and its fulness, Isles, and their inhabitants.
texts.isa.42.11: The wilderness and its cities do lift up [the voice], The villages Kedar doth inhabit, Sing do the inhabitants of Sela, From the top of mountains they cry.
texts.isa.42.12: They ascribe to Jehovah honour, And His praise in the isles they declare.
texts.isa.42.13: Jehovah as a mighty one goeth forth. As a man of war He stirreth up zeal, He crieth, yea, He shrieketh, Against His enemies He showeth Himself mighty.
texts.isa.42.14: I have kept silent from of old, I keep silent, I refrain myself, As a travailing woman I cry out, I desolate and swallow up together.
texts.isa.42.15: I make waste mountains and hills, And all their herbs I dry up, And I have made rivers become isles, And ponds I dry up.
texts.isa.42.16: And I have caused the blind to go, In a way they have not known, In paths they have not known I cause them to tread, I make a dark place before them become light, And unlevelled places become a plain, These [are] the things I have done to them, And I have not forsaken them.
texts.isa.42.17: Removed backward -- utterly ashamed, Are those trusting in a graven image, Those saying to a molten image, `Ye [are] our gods.'
texts.isa.42.18: Ye deaf, hear; and ye blind, look to see.
texts.isa.42.19: Who [is] blind but My servant? And deaf as My messenger I send? Who [is] blind as he who is at peace, Yea, blind, as the servant of Jehovah?
texts.isa.42.20: Seeing many things, and thou observest not, Opening ears, and he heareth not.
texts.isa.42.21: Jehovah hath delight for the sake of His righteousness, He magnifieth law, and maketh honourable.
texts.isa.42.22: And this [is] a people seized and spoiled, Snared in holes -- all of them, And in houses of restraint they were hidden, They have been for a prey, And there is no deliverer, A spoil, and none is saying, `Restore.'
texts.isa.42.23: Who among you giveth ear [to] this? Attendeth, and heareth afterwards.
texts.isa.42.24: Who hath given Jacob for a spoil, And Israel to the spoilers? Is it not Jehovah -- He against whom we sinned? Yea, they have not been willing in His ways to walk, Nor have they hearkened to His law.
texts.isa.42.25: And He poureth on him fury, His anger, and the strength of battle, And it setteth him on fire round about, And he hath not known, And it burneth against him, and he layeth it not to heart!
texts.isa.43.1: And now, thus said Jehovah, Thy Creator, O Jacob, and thy Fashioner, O Israel, Be not afraid, for I have redeemed thee, I have called on thy name -- thou [art] Mine.
texts.isa.43.2: When thou passest into waters, I [am] with thee, And into floods, they do not overflow thee, When thou goest into fire, thou art not burnt, And a flame doth not burn against thee.
texts.isa.43.3: For I -- Jehovah thy God, The Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour, I have appointed Egypt thine atonement, Cush and Seba in thy stead.
texts.isa.43.4: Since thou wast precious in Mine eyes, Thou wast honoured, and I have loved thee, And I appoint men in thy stead, And peoples instead of thy life.
texts.isa.43.5: Be not afraid, for I [am] with thee, From the east I bring in thy seed, And from the west I gather thee.
texts.isa.43.6: I am saying to the north, `Give up,' And to the south, `Restrain not.' Bring in My sons from afar, And My daughters from the end of the earth.
texts.isa.43.7: Every one who is called by My name, Even for My honour I have created him, I have formed him, yea, I have made him.
texts.isa.43.8: He brought out a blind people who have eyes, And deaf ones who have ears.
texts.isa.43.9: All the nations have been gathered together, And the peoples are assembled, Who among them declareth this, And former things causeth us to hear? They give their witnesses, And they are declared righteous, And they hear and say, `Truth.'
texts.isa.43.10: Ye [are] My witnesses, an affirmation of Jehovah, And My servant whom I have chosen, So that ye know and give credence to Me, And understand that I [am] He, Before Me there was no God formed, And after Me there is none.
texts.isa.43.11: I -- I [am] Jehovah, And besides Me there is no saviour.
texts.isa.43.12: I -- I declared, and saved, and proclaimed, And there is no stranger with you, And ye [are] My witnesses, an affirmation of Jehovah, And I [am] God.
texts.isa.43.13: Even from the day I [am] He, And there is no deliverer from My hand, I work, and who doth turn it back?
texts.isa.43.14: Thus said Jehovah, your Redeemer, The Holy One of Israel: `For your sake I have sent to Babylon, And caused bars to descend -- all of them, And the Chaldeans, whose song [is] in the ships.
texts.isa.43.15: I [am] Jehovah, your Holy One, Creator of Israel, your King.'
texts.isa.43.16: Thus said Jehovah, Who is giving in the sea a way, And in the strong waters a path.
texts.isa.43.17: Who is bringing forth chariot and horse, A force, even a strong one: `Together they lie down -- they rise not, They have been extinguished, As flax they have been quenched.'
texts.isa.43.18: Remember not former things, And ancient things consider not.
texts.isa.43.19: Lo, I am doing a new thing, now it springeth up, Do ye not know it? Yea, I put in a wilderness a way, In a desolate place -- floods.
texts.isa.43.20: Honour me doth the beast of the field, Dragons and daughters of an ostrich, For I have given in a wilderness waters, Floods in a desolate place, To give drink to My people -- My chosen.
texts.isa.43.21: This people I have formed for Myself, My praise they recount.
texts.isa.43.22: And Me thou hast not called, O Jacob, For thou hast been wearied of me, O Israel,
texts.isa.43.23: Thou hast not brought in to Me, The lamb of thy burnt-offerings, And [with] thy sacrifices thou hast not honoured Me, I have not caused thee to serve with a present, Nor wearied thee with frankincense.
texts.isa.43.24: Thou hast not bought for Me with money sweet cane, And [with] the fat of thy sacrifices hast not filled Me, Only -- thou hast caused Me to serve with thy sins, Thou hast wearied Me with thine iniquities.
texts.isa.43.25: I -- I [am] He who is blotting out Thy transgressions for Mine own sake, And thy sins I do not remember.
texts.isa.43.26: Cause me to remember -- we are judged together, Declare thou that thou mayest be justified.
texts.isa.43.27: Thy first father sinned, And thine interpreters transgressed against me,
texts.isa.43.28: And I pollute princes of the sanctuary, And I give Jacob to destruction, and Israel to revilings!
texts.isa.44.1: And now, hear, O Jacob, My servant, And Israel, whom I have fixed on:
texts.isa.44.2: Thus said Jehovah, thy Maker, and thy Former, From the womb He doth help thee; Fear not, my servant Jacob, And Jeshurun, whom I have fixed on.
texts.isa.44.3: For I pour waters on a thirsty one, And floods on a dry land, I pour My Spirit on thy seed, And My blessing on thine offspring.
texts.isa.44.4: And they have sprung up as among grass, As willows by streams of water.
texts.isa.44.5: This [one] saith, For Jehovah I [am], And this calleth [himself] by the name of Jacob, And this [one] writeth [with] his hand, `For Jehovah,' and by the name of Israel surnameth himself.
texts.isa.44.6: Thus said Jehovah, king of Israel, And his Redeemer, Jehovah of Hosts: `I [am] the first, and I the last, And besides Me there is no God.
texts.isa.44.7: And who as I, doth call and declare it, And arrange it for Me, Since My placing the people of antiquity, And things that are coming, And those that do come, declare they to them?
texts.isa.44.8: Fear not, nor be afraid, Have I not from that time caused thee to hear, and declared? And ye [are] My witnesses, Is there a God besides Me? yea, there is none, A Rock I have not known.
texts.isa.44.9: Framers of a graven image [are] all of them emptiness, And their desirable things do not profit, And their own witnesses they [are], They see not, nor know, that they may be ashamed.
texts.isa.44.10: Who hath formed a god, And a molten image poured out -- not profitable?
texts.isa.44.11: Lo, all his companions are ashamed, As to artizans -- they [are] of men, All of them gather together, they stand up, They fear, they are ashamed together.
texts.isa.44.12: He hath wrought iron [with] an axe, And hath wrought with coals, And with hammers doth form it, And doth work it by his powerful arm, Yea, he is hungry, and there is no power, He doth not drink water, and he is wearied.
texts.isa.44.13: He hath wrought [with] wood, He hath stretched out a rule, He doth mark it out with a line, He maketh it with carving tools, And with a compass he marketh it out, And maketh it according to the form of a man, According to the beauty of a man, To remain in the house.
texts.isa.44.14: Cutting down to himself cedars, He taketh also a cypress, and an oak, And he strengtheneth [it] for himself Among the trees of a forest, He hath planted an ash, and the shower doth nourish [it].
texts.isa.44.15: And it hath been for man to burn, And he taketh of them, and becometh warm, Yea, he kindleth [it], and hath baked bread, Yea, he maketh a god, and boweth himself, He hath made it a graven image, And he falleth down to it.
texts.isa.44.16: Half of it he hath burnt in the fire, By [this] half of it he eateth flesh, He roasteth a roasting, and is satisfied, Yea, he is warm, and saith: `Aha, I have become warm, I have enjoyed the light.
texts.isa.44.17: And its remnant for a god he hath made -- For his graven image, He falleth down to it, and worshippeth, And prayeth unto it, and he saith, `Deliver me, for my god thou [art].'
texts.isa.44.18: They have not known, nor do they understand, For He hath daubed their eyes from seeing, Their heart from acting wisely.
texts.isa.44.19: And none doth turn [it] back unto his heart, Nor hath knowledge nor understanding to say, `Half of it I have burned in the fire, Yea, also, I have baked bread over its coals, I roast flesh and I eat, And its remnant for an abomination I make, To the stock of a tree I fall down.'
texts.isa.44.20: Feeding on ashes, the heart is deceived, It hath turned him aside, And he delivereth not his soul, nor saith: `Is there not a lie in my right hand?'
texts.isa.44.21: Remember these, O Jacob, and Israel, For My servant thou [art], I formed thee, a servant to Me thou [art], O Israel, thou dost not forget Me.
texts.isa.44.22: I have blotted out, as [by] a thick cloud, Thy transgressions, And as [by] a cloud thy sins, Return unto Me, for I have redeemed thee.
texts.isa.44.23: Sing, O heavens, for Jehovah hath wrought, Shout, O lower parts of earth, Break forth, O mountains, with singing, Forest, and every tree in it, For Jehovah hath redeemed Jacob, And in Israel He doth beautify Himself.
texts.isa.44.24: Thus said Jehovah, thy redeemer, And thy framer from the womb: `I [am] Jehovah, doing all things, Stretching out the heavens by Myself, Spreading out the earth -- who [is] with Me?
texts.isa.44.25: Making void the tokens of devisers, And diviners it maketh mad, Turning the wise backward, And their knowledge it maketh foolish.
texts.isa.44.26: Confirming the word of His servant, The counsel of His messengers it perfecteth, Who is saying of Jerusalem, She is inhabited, And of cities of Judah, They shall be built, and her wastes I raise up,
texts.isa.44.27: Who is saying to the deep, Be dry, and thy rivers I cause to dry up,
texts.isa.44.28: Who is saying of Cyrus, My shepherd, And all my delight He doth perfect, So as to say of Jerusalem, Thou art built, And of the temple, Thou art founded.
texts.isa.45.1: Thus said Jehovah, To His anointed, to Cyrus, Whose right hand I have laid hold on, To subdue nations before him, Yea, loins of kings I loose, To open before him two-leaved doors, Yea, gates are not shut:
texts.isa.45.2: `I go before thee, and crooked places make straight, Two-leaved doors of brass I shiver, And bars of iron I cut asunder,
texts.isa.45.3: And have given to thee treasures of darkness, Even treasures of secret places, So that thou knowest that I, Jehovah, Who am calling on thy name -- [am] the God of Israel.
texts.isa.45.4: For the sake of my servant Jacob, And of Israel My chosen, I call also thee by thy name, I surname thee, And thou hast not known Me.
texts.isa.45.5: I [am] Jehovah, and there is none else, Except Me there is no God, I gird thee, and thou hast not known Me.
texts.isa.45.6: So that they know from the rising of the sun, And from the west, that there is none besides Me, I [am] Jehovah, and there is none else,
texts.isa.45.7: Forming light, and preparing darkness, Making peace, and preparing evil, I [am] Jehovah, doing all these things.'
texts.isa.45.8: Drop, ye heavens, from above, And clouds do cause righteousness to flow, Earth openeth, and they are fruitful, Salvation and righteousness spring up together, I, Jehovah, have prepared it.
texts.isa.45.9: Wo [to] him who is striving with his Former, (A potsherd with potsherds of the ground!) Doth clay say to its Framer, `What dost thou?' And thy work, `He hath no hands?'
texts.isa.45.10: Wo [to] him who is saying to a father, `What dost thou beget?' Or to a wife, `What dost thou bring forth?
texts.isa.45.11: Thus said Jehovah, The Holy One of Israel, and his Former: Ask Me of the things coming concerning My sons, Yea, concerning the work of My hands, ye command Me.'
texts.isa.45.12: I made earth, and man on it prepared, I -- My hands stretched out the heavens, And all their host I have commanded.
texts.isa.45.13: I have stirred him up in righteousness, And all his ways I make straight, He doth build My city, and My captivity doth send out, Not for price, nor for bribe, said Jehovah of Hosts.
texts.isa.45.14: Thus said Jehovah, `The labour of Egypt, And the merchandise of Cush, And of the Sebaim -- men of measure, Unto thee pass over, and thine they are, After thee they go, in fetters they pass over, And unto thee they bow themselves, Unto thee they pray: Only in thee [is] God, And there is none else, no [other] God.
texts.isa.45.15: Surely Thou [art] a God hiding Thyself, God of Israel -- Saviour!
texts.isa.45.16: They have been ashamed, And they have even blushed -- all of them, Together gone in confusion have those carving images.
texts.isa.45.17: Israel hath been saved in Jehovah, A salvation age-during! Ye are not ashamed nor confounded Unto the ages of eternity!
texts.isa.45.18: For thus said Jehovah, Creator of heaven, He is God, Former of earth, and its Maker, He established it -- not empty He prepared it, For inhabiting He formed it: `I [am] Jehovah, and there is none else.
texts.isa.45.19: Not in secret have I spoken, in a dark place of the earth, I have not said to the seed of Jacob, In vain seek ye Me, I [am] Jehovah, speaking righteousness, Declaring uprightness.
texts.isa.45.20: Be gathered, and come in, Come nigh together, ye escaped of the nations, They have not known, Who are lifting up the wood of their graven image, And praying unto a god [that] saveth not.
texts.isa.45.21: Declare ye, and bring near, Yea, they take counsel together, Who hath proclaimed this from of old? From that time hath declared it? Is it not I -- Jehovah? And there is no other god besides Me, A God righteous and saving, there is none save Me.
texts.isa.45.22: Turn to Me, and be saved, all ends of the earth, For I [am] God, and there is none else.
texts.isa.45.23: By Myself I have sworn, Gone out from my mouth in righteousness hath a word, And it turneth not back, That to Me, bow doth every knee, every tongue swear.
texts.isa.45.24: Only in Jehovah, said hath one, Have I righteousness and strength, Unto Him he cometh in, And ashamed are all those displeased with Him.
texts.isa.45.25: In Jehovah are all the seed of Israel justified, And they boast themselves.'
texts.isa.46.1: Bowed down hath Bel, stooping is Nebo, Their idols have been for the beast and for cattle, Your burdens are loaded, a burden to the weary.
texts.isa.46.2: They have stooped, they have bowed together, They have not been able to deliver the burden, And themselves into captivity have gone.
texts.isa.46.3: Hearken unto Me, O house of Jacob, And all the remnant of Israel, Who are borne from the belly, Who are carried from the womb,
texts.isa.46.4: Even to old age I [am] He, and to grey hairs I carry, I made, and I bear, yea, I carry and deliver.
texts.isa.46.5: To whom do ye liken Me, and make equal? And compare Me, that we may be like?
texts.isa.46.6: -- They are pouring out gold from a bag, And silver on the beam they weigh, They hire a refiner, and he maketh it a god, They fall down, yea, they bow themselves.
texts.isa.46.7: They lift him up on the shoulder, They carry him, and cause him to rest in his place, And he standeth, from his place he moveth not, Yea, one crieth unto him, and he answereth not, From his adversity he saveth him not.
texts.isa.46.8: Remember this, and shew yourselves men, Turn [it] back, O transgressors, to the heart.
texts.isa.46.9: Remember former things of old, For I [am] Mighty, and there is none else, God -- and there is none like Me.
texts.isa.46.10: Declaring from the beginning the latter end, And from of old that which hath not been done, Saying, `My counsel doth stand, And all My delight I do.'
texts.isa.46.11: Calling from the east a ravenous bird, From a far land the man of My counsel, Yea, I have spoken, yea, I bring it in, I have formed [it], yea, I do it.
texts.isa.46.12: Hearken unto Me, ye mighty in heart, Who are far from righteousness.
texts.isa.46.13: I have brought near My righteousness, It is not far off, And My salvation -- it doth not tarry, And I have given in Zion salvation, To Israel My glory!
texts.isa.47.1: Come down, and sit on the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, Sit on the earth, there is no throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans, For no more do they cry to thee, `O tender and delicate one.'
texts.isa.47.2: Take millstones, and grind flour, Remove thy veil, draw up the skirt, Uncover the leg, pass over the floods.
texts.isa.47.3: Revealed is thy nakedness, yea, seen is thy reproach, Vengeance I take, and I meet not a man.
texts.isa.47.4: Our redeemer [is] Jehovah of Hosts, His name [is] the Holy One of Israel.
texts.isa.47.5: Sit silent, and go into darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans, For no more do they cry to thee, `Mistress of kingdoms.'
texts.isa.47.6: I have been wroth against My people, I have polluted Mine inheritance And I give them into thy hand, Thou hast not appointed for them mercies, On the aged thou hast made thy yoke very heavy,
texts.isa.47.7: And thou sayest, `To the age I am mistress,' While thou hast not laid these things to thy heart, Thou hast not remembered the latter end of it.
texts.isa.47.8: And now, hear this, O luxurious one, Who is sitting confidently -- Who is saying in her heart, `I [am], and none else, I sit not a widow, nor know bereavement.'
texts.isa.47.9: And come in to thee do these two things, In a moment, in one day, childlessness and widowhood, According to their perfection they have come upon thee, In the multitude of thy sorceries, In the exceeding might of thy charms.
texts.isa.47.10: And thou art confident in thy wickedness, Thou hast said, `There is none seeing me,' Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, It is turning thee back, And thou sayest in thy heart, `I [am], and none else.'
texts.isa.47.11: And come in on thee hath evil, Thou knowest not its rising, And fall on thee doth mischief, Thou art not able to pacify it, And come on thee suddenly doth desolation, Thou knowest not.
texts.isa.47.12: Stand, I pray thee, in thy charms, And in the multitude of thy sorceries, In which thou hast laboured from thy youth, It may be thou art able to profit, It may be thou dost terrify!
texts.isa.47.13: Thou hast been wearied in the multitude of thy counsels, Stand up, I pray thee, and save thee, Let the charmers of the heavens, Those looking on the stars, Those teaching concerning the months, From those things that come on thee!
texts.isa.47.14: Lo, they have been as stubble! Fire hath burned them, They deliver not themselves from the power of the flame, There is not a coal to warm them, a light to sit before it.
texts.isa.47.15: So have they been to thee with whom thou hast laboured, Thy merchants from thy youth, Each to his passage they have wandered, Thy saviour is not!
texts.isa.48.1: Hear ye this, O house of Jacob, Who are called by the name of Israel, And from the waters of Judah came out, Who are swearing by the name of Jehovah, And of the God of Israel make mention, Not in truth nor in righteousness.
texts.isa.48.2: For from the Holy City they have been called, And on the God of Israel been supported, Jehovah of Hosts [is] His name.
texts.isa.48.3: The former things from that time I declared, And from my mouth they have gone forth, And I proclaim them, Suddenly I have done, and it cometh.
texts.isa.48.4: From my knowing that thou art obstinate, And a sinew of iron thy neck, And thy forehead brass,
texts.isa.48.5: And I declare to thee from that time, Before it cometh I have caused thee to hear, Lest thou say, `Mine idol hath done them, And my graven image, And my molten image did command them.
texts.isa.48.6: Thou hast heard, see the whole of it, And ye, do ye not declare? I have caused thee to hear new things from this time, And things reserved that ye knew not.
texts.isa.48.7: Now they have been produced and not from that time, Yea, before the day, and thou hast not heard them, Lest thou say, `Lo, I have known them.'
texts.isa.48.8: Yea, thou hast not heard, Yea, thou hast not known, Yea, from that time not opened hath thine ear, For I have known thou dealest treacherously, And `Transgressor from the belly,' One is crying to thee.
texts.isa.48.9: For My name's sake I defer Mine anger, And My praise I restrain for thee, So as not to cut thee off.
texts.isa.48.10: Lo, I have refined thee, and not with silver, I have chosen thee in a furnace of affliction.
texts.isa.48.11: For My sake, for Mine own sake, I do [it], For how is it polluted? And Mine honour to another I give not.
texts.isa.48.12: Hearken to me, O Jacob, and Israel, My called one, I [am] He, I [am] first, and I [am] last;
texts.isa.48.13: Also, My hand hath founded earth, And My right hand stretched out the heavens, I am calling unto them, they stand together.
texts.isa.48.14: Be gathered all of you, and hear, Who among them did declare these things? Jehovah hath loved him, He doth His pleasure on Babylon, And His arm [is on] the Chaldeans.
texts.isa.48.15: I -- I have spoken, yea, I have called him, I have brought him in, And he hath made prosperous his way.
texts.isa.48.16: Come ye near unto me, hear this, Not from the beginning in secret spake I, From the time of its being, there [am] I, And now the Lord Jehovah hath sent me, and His Spirit.
texts.isa.48.17: Thus said Jehovah, thy redeemer, The Holy One of Israel, `I [am] Jehovah thy God, teaching thee to profit, Causing thee to tread in the way thou goest.
texts.isa.48.18: O that thou hadst attended to My commands, Then as a river is thy peace, And thy righteousness as billows of the sea,
texts.isa.48.19: And as sand is thy seed, And the offspring of thy bowels as its gravel, Not cut off nor destroyed his name before Me.
texts.isa.48.20: Go out from Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans, With a voice of singing declare, Cause ye this to be heard, Bring it forth unto the end of the earth, Say, Redeemed hath Jehovah His servant Jacob.
texts.isa.48.21: And they have not thirsted in waste places, He hath caused them to go on, Waters from a rock he hath caused to flow to them, Yea, he cleaveth a rock, and flow do waters.
texts.isa.48.22: There is no peace, said Jehovah, to the wicked!
texts.isa.49.1: Hearken, O isles, unto me, And attend, O peoples, from afar, Jehovah from the womb hath called me, From the bowels of my mother He hath made mention of my name.
texts.isa.49.2: And he maketh my mouth as a sharp sword, In the shadow of His hand He hath hid me, And He maketh me for a clear arrow, In His quiver He hath hid me.
texts.isa.49.3: And He saith to me, `My servant Thou art, O Israel, In whom I beautify Myself.'
texts.isa.49.4: And I said, `For a vain thing I laboured, For emptiness and vanity my power I consumed, But my judgment [is] with Jehovah, And my wage with my God.
texts.isa.49.5: And now, said Jehovah, who is forming me from the belly for a servant to Him, To bring back Jacob unto Him, (Though Israel is not gathered, Yet I am honoured in the eyes of Jehovah, And my God hath been my strength.)
texts.isa.49.6: And He saith, `It hath been a light thing That thou art to Me for a servant To raise up the tribes of Jacob, And the preserved of Israel to bring back, And I have given thee for a light of nations, To be My salvation unto the end of the earth.'
texts.isa.49.7: Thus said Jehovah, Redeemer of Israel, His Holy One, To the despised in soul, To the abominated of a nation, To the servant of rulers: `Kings see, and have risen, princes, and worship, For the sake of Jehovah, who is faithful, The Holy of Israel, and He chooseth thee.'
texts.isa.49.8: Thus said Jehovah: `In a time of good pleasure I answered thee, And in a day of salvation I helped thee, And I keep thee, and give thee, For a covenant of the people, To establish the earth, To cause to inherit desolate inheritances.
texts.isa.49.9: To say to the bound, Go out, To those in darkness, Be uncovered. On the ways they feed, And in all high places is their pasture.
texts.isa.49.10: They do not hunger, nor thirst, Nor smite them doth mirage and sun, For He who is pitying them doth lead them, And by fountains of waters doth tend them.
texts.isa.49.11: And I have made all My mountains for a way, And My highways are lifted up.
texts.isa.49.12: Lo, these from afar come in, And lo, these from the north, and from the sea, And these from the land of Sinim.
texts.isa.49.13: Sing, O heavens, and joy, O earth, And break forth, O mountains, with singing, For comforted hath Jehovah His people, And His afflicted ones He doth pity.
texts.isa.49.14: And Zion saith, `Jehovah hath forsaken me, And my Lord hath forgotten me.'
texts.isa.49.15: Forget doth a woman her suckling, The loved one -- the son of her womb? Yea, these forget -- but I -- I forget not thee.
texts.isa.49.16: Lo, on the palms of the hand I have graven thee, Thy walls [are] before Me continually.
texts.isa.49.17: Hastened have those building thee, Those destroying thee, and laying thee waste, go out from thee.
texts.isa.49.18: Lift up round about thine eyes and see, All of them have been gathered, They have come to thee. I live, an affirmation of Jehovah! Surely all of them as an ornament thou puttest on, And thou bindest them on like a bride.
texts.isa.49.19: Because thy wastes, and thy desolate places, And the land of thy ruins, Surely now are straitened because of inhabitants, And far off have been those consuming thee.
texts.isa.49.20: Again do the sons of thy bereavement say in thine ears: `The place is too strait for me, Come nigh to me -- and I dwell.'
texts.isa.49.21: And thou hast said in thy heart: `Who hath begotten for me -- these? And I bereaved and gloomy, A captive, and turned aside, And these -- who hath nourished? Lo, I -- I was left by myself, these -- whence [are] they?
texts.isa.49.22: Thus said the Lord Jehovah: `Lo, I lift up unto nations My hand, And unto peoples I raise up Mine ensign, And they have brought thy sons in the bosom, And thy daughters on the shoulder are carried.
texts.isa.49.23: And kings have been thy nursing fathers, And their princesses thy nursing mothers; Face to the earth -- they bow down to thee, And the dust of thy feet they lick up, And thou hast known that I [am] Jehovah, That those expecting Me are not ashamed.
texts.isa.49.24: Is prey taken from the mighty? And the captive of the righteous delivered?
texts.isa.49.25: For thus said Jehovah: Even the captive of the mighty is taken, And the prey of the terrible is delivered, And with thy striver I strive, and thy sons I save.
texts.isa.49.26: And I have caused thine oppressors to eat their own flesh, And as new wine they drink their own blood, And known have all flesh that I, Jehovah, Thy saviour, and thy redeemer, [Am] the Mighty One of Jacob!'
texts.isa.50.1: Thus said Jehovah: `Where [is] this -- the bill of your mother's divorce, Whom I sent away? Or to which of My creditors have I sold you? Lo, for your iniquities ye have been sold, And for your transgressions Hath your mother been sent away.
texts.isa.50.2: Wherefore have I come, and there is no one? I called, and there is none answering, Hath My hand been at all short of redemption? And is there not in me power to deliver? Lo, by My rebuke I dry up a sea, I make rivers a wilderness, Their fish stinketh, for there is no water, And dieth with thirst.
texts.isa.50.3: I clothe the heavens [with] blackness, And sackcloth I make their covering.
texts.isa.50.4: The Lord Jehovah hath given to me The tongue of taught ones, To know to aid the weary [by] a word, He waketh morning by morning, He waketh for me an ear to hear as taught ones.
texts.isa.50.5: The Lord Jehovah opened for me the ear, And I rebelled not -- backward I moved not.
texts.isa.50.6: My back I have given to those smiting, And my cheeks to those plucking out, My face I hid not from shame and spitting.
texts.isa.50.7: And the Lord Jehovah giveth help to me, Therefore I have not been ashamed, Therefore I have set my face as a flint, And I know that I am not ashamed.
texts.isa.50.8: Near [is] He who is justifying me, Who doth contend with me? We stand together, who [is] mine opponent? Let him come nigh unto me.
texts.isa.50.9: Lo, the Lord Jehovah giveth help to me, Who [is] he that declareth me wicked? Lo, all of them as a garment wear out, A moth doth eat them.
texts.isa.50.10: Who [is] among you, fearing Jehovah, Hearkening to the voice of His servant, That hath walked in dark places, And there is no brightness for him? Let him trust in the name of Jehovah, And lean upon his God.
texts.isa.50.11: Lo, all ye kindling a fire, girding on sparks, Walk ye in the light of your fire, And in the sparks ye have caused to burn, From my hand hath this been to you, In grief ye lie down!
texts.isa.51.1: Hearken unto Me, ye pursuing righteousness, Seeking Jehovah, Look attentively unto the rock -- ye have been hewn, And unto the hole of the pit -- ye have been digged.
texts.isa.51.2: Look attentively unto Abraham your father, And unto Sarah -- she bringeth you forth, For -- one -- I have called him, And I bless him, and multiply him.
texts.isa.51.3: For Jehovah hath comforted Zion, He hath comforted all her wastes, And He setteth her wilderness as Eden, And her desert as a garden of Jehovah, Joy, yea, gladness is found in her, Confession, and the voice of song.
texts.isa.51.4: Attend unto Me, O My people, And, O My nation, unto Me give ear. For a law from Me goeth out, And My judgment to the light, Peoples I do cause to rest.
texts.isa.51.5: Near [is] My righteousness, Gone out hath My salvation and Mine arms, Peoples they judge, on Me isles do wait, Yea, on Mine arm they do wait with hope.
texts.isa.51.6: Lift ye up to the heavens your eyes, And look attentively unto the earth beneath, For the heavens as smoke have vanished, And the earth as a garment weareth out, And its inhabitants as gnats do die, And My salvation is to the age, And My righteousness is not broken.
texts.isa.51.7: Hearken unto Me, ye who know righteousness, A people, in whose heart [is] My law, Fear ye not the reproach of men, And for their reviling be not affrighted,
texts.isa.51.8: For as a garment eat them doth a moth, And as wool eat them doth a worm, And My righteousness is to the age, And My salvation to all generations.
texts.isa.51.9: Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of Jehovah, Awake, as [in] days of old, generations of the ages, Art not Thou it that is hewing down Rahab, Piercing a dragon!
texts.isa.51.10: Art not Thou it that is drying up a sea, Waters of a great deep? That hath made deep places of a sea A way for the passing of the redeemed?
texts.isa.51.11: And the ransomed of Jehovah turn back, And they have come to Zion with singing, And joy age-during [is] on their head, Gladness and joy they attain, Fled away have sorrow and sighing,
texts.isa.51.12: I -- I [am] He -- your comforter, Who [art] thou -- and thou art afraid of man? he dieth! And of the son of man -- grass he is made!
texts.isa.51.13: And thou dost forget Jehovah thy maker, Who is stretching out the heavens, and founding earth, And thou dost fear continually all the day, Because of the fury of the oppressor, As he hath prepared to destroy. And where [is] the fury of the oppressor?
texts.isa.51.14: Hastened hath a wanderer to be loosed, And he doth not die at the pit, And his bread is not lacking.
texts.isa.51.15: And I [am] Jehovah thy God, Quieting the sea, when its billows roar, Jehovah of Hosts [is] His name.
texts.isa.51.16: And I put My words in thy mouth, And with the shadow of My hand have covered thee, To plant the heavens, and to found earth, And to say to Zion, `My people [art] thou.'
texts.isa.51.17: Stir thyself, stir thyself, rise, Jerusalem, Who hast drunk from the hand of Jehovah The cup of His fury, The goblet, the cup of trembling, thou hast drunk, Thou hast wrung out.
texts.isa.51.18: There is not a leader to her Out of all the sons she hath borne, And there is none laying hold on her hand Out of all the sons she hath nourished.
texts.isa.51.19: These two are meeting thee, who is moved for thee? Spoiling and destruction -- Famine and sword, who -- I comfort thee?
texts.isa.51.20: Thy sons have been wrapt up, they have lain down, At the head of all out places, as a wild ox [in] a net, They are full of the fury of Jehovah, The rebuke of Thy God.
texts.isa.51.21: Therefore, hear, I pray thee, this, O afflicted and drunken one, and not with wine,
texts.isa.51.22: Thus said thy Lord Jehovah, and thy God, He pleadeth [for] his people: `Lo, I have taken out of thy hand the cup of trembling, The goblet, the cup of My fury, Thou dost not add to drink it any more.
texts.isa.51.23: And I have put it into the hand of those afflicting thee, Who have said to thy soul, Bow down, and we pass over, And thou makest as the earth thy body, And as the street to those passing by!'
texts.isa.52.1: Awake, awake, put on thy strength, O Zion, Put on the garments of thy beauty, Jerusalem -- the Holy City; For enter no more into thee again, Do the uncircumcised and unclean.
texts.isa.52.2: Shake thyself from dust, arise, sit, O Jerusalem, Bands of thy neck have loosed themselves, O captive, daughter of Zion.
texts.isa.52.3: For thus said Jehovah: `For nought ye have been sold, And not by money are ye redeemed.'
texts.isa.52.4: For thus said the Lord Jehovah: `To Egypt My people went down at first to sojourn there, And Asshur -- for nought he hath oppressed it.
texts.isa.52.5: And now, what -- to Me here, An affirmation of Jehovah, That taken is My people for nought? Its rulers cause howling, -- an affirmation of Jehovah, And continually all the day My name is despised.
texts.isa.52.6: Therefore doth My people know My name, Therefore, in that day, Surely I [am] He who is speaking, behold Me.'
texts.isa.52.7: How comely on the mountains, Have been the feet of one proclaiming tidings, Sounding peace, proclaiming good tidings, Sounding salvation, Saying to Zion, `Reigned hath thy God.'
texts.isa.52.8: The voice of thy watchmen! They have lifted up the voice, together they cry aloud, Because eye to eye they see, in Jehovah's turning back [to] Zion.
texts.isa.52.9: Break forth, sing together, O wastes of Jerusalem, For Jehovah hath comforted His people, He hath redeemed Jerusalem.
texts.isa.52.10: Jehovah hath made bare His holy arm Before the eyes of all the nations, And seen have all the ends of the earth, The salvation of our God.
texts.isa.52.11: Turn aside, turn aside, go out thence, The unclean touch not, go out from her midst, Be ye pure, who are bearing the weapons of Jehovah.
texts.isa.52.12: For not in haste do ye go out, Yea, with flight ye go not on, For going before you [is] Jehovah, And gathering you [is] the God of Israel!
texts.isa.52.13: Lo, My servant doth act wisely, He is high, and hath been lifted up, And hath been very high.
texts.isa.52.14: As astonished at thee have been many, (So marred by man his appearance, And his form by sons of men.)
texts.isa.52.15: So doth he sprinkle many nations. Concerning him kings shut their mouth, For that which was not recounted to them they have seen, And that which they had not heard they have understood!
texts.isa.53.1: Who hath given credence to that which we heard? And the arm of Jehovah, On whom hath it been revealed?
texts.isa.53.2: Yea, he cometh up as a tender plant before Him, And as a root out of a dry land, He hath no form, nor honour, when we observe him, Nor appearance, when we desire him.
texts.isa.53.3: He is despised, and left of men, A man of pains, and acquainted with sickness, And as one hiding the face from us, He is despised, and we esteemed him not.
texts.isa.53.4: Surely our sicknesses he hath borne, And our pains -- he hath carried them, And we -- we have esteemed him plagued, Smitten of God, and afflicted.
texts.isa.53.5: And he is pierced for our transgressions, Bruised for our iniquities, The chastisement of our peace [is] on him, And by his bruise there is healing to us.
texts.isa.53.6: All of us like sheep have wandered, Each to his own way we have turned, And Jehovah hath caused to meet on him, The punishment of us all.
texts.isa.53.7: It hath been exacted, and he hath answered, And he openeth not his mouth, As a lamb to the slaughter he is brought, And as a sheep before its shearers is dumb, And he openeth not his mouth.
texts.isa.53.8: By restraint and by judgment he hath been taken, And of his generation who doth meditate, That he hath been cut off from the land of the living? By the transgression of My people he is plagued,
texts.isa.53.9: And it appointeth with the wicked his grave, And with the rich [are] his high places, Because he hath done no violence, Nor [is] deceit in his mouth.
texts.isa.53.10: And Jehovah hath delighted to bruise him, He hath made him sick, If his soul doth make an offering for guilt, He seeth seed -- he prolongeth days, And the pleasure of Jehovah in his hand doth prosper.
texts.isa.53.11: Of the labour of his soul he seeth -- he is satisfied, Through his knowledge give righteousness Doth the righteous one, My servant, to many, And their iniquities he doth bear.
texts.isa.53.12: Therefore I give a portion to him among the many, And with the mighty he apportioneth spoil, Because that he exposed to death his soul, And with transgressors he was numbered, And he the sin of many hath borne, And for transgressors he intercedeth.
texts.isa.54.1: Sing, O barren, she hath not borne! Break forth with singing, and cry aloud, She hath not brought forth! For more [are] the sons of the desolate, Than the sons of the married one, said Jehovah.
texts.isa.54.2: Enlarge the place of thy tent, And the curtains of thy tabernacles they stretch out, Restrain not -- lengthen thy cords, And thy pins make strong.
texts.isa.54.3: For right and left thou breakest forth, And thy seed doth nations possess,
texts.isa.54.4: And desolate cities they cause to be inhabited. Fear not, for thou art not ashamed, Nor blush, for thou art not confounded, For the shame of thy youth thou forgettest, And the reproach of thy widowhood Thou dost not remember any more.
texts.isa.54.5: For thy Maker [is] thy husband, Jehovah of Hosts [is] His name, And thy Redeemer [is] the Holy One of Israel, `God of all the earth,' He is called.
texts.isa.54.6: For, as a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit, Called thee hath Jehovah, Even a youthful wife when she is refused, said thy God.
texts.isa.54.7: In a small moment I have forsaken thee, And in great mercies I do gather thee,
texts.isa.54.8: In overflowing wrath I hid my face [for] a moment from thee, And in kindness age-during I have loved thee, Said thy Redeemer -- Jehovah!
texts.isa.54.9: For, the waters of Noah [is] this to Me, In that I have sworn -- the waters of Noah Do not pass again over the earth -- So I have sworn, Wrath is not upon thee, Nor rebuke against thee.
texts.isa.54.10: For the mountains depart, and the hills remove, And My kindness from thee departeth not, And the covenant of My peace removeth not, Said hath thy loving one -- Jehovah.
texts.isa.54.11: O afflicted, storm-tossed, not comforted, Lo, I am laying with cement thy stones, And have founded thee with sapphires,
texts.isa.54.12: And have made of agate thy pinnacles, And thy gates of carbuncle stones, And all thy border of stones of delight,
texts.isa.54.13: And all thy sons are taught of Jehovah, And abundant [is] the peace of thy sons.
texts.isa.54.14: In righteousness thou establishest thyself, Be far from oppression, for thou fearest not, And from ruin, for it cometh not near unto thee.
texts.isa.54.15: Lo, he doth diligently assemble without My desire, Who hath assembled near thee? By thee he falleth!
texts.isa.54.16: Lo, I -- I have prepared an artizan, Blowing on a fire of coals, And bringing out an instrument for his work, And I have prepared a destroyer to destroy.
texts.isa.54.17: No weapon formed against thee prospereth, And every tongue rising against thee, In judgment thou condemnest. This [is] the inheritance of the servants of Jehovah, And their righteousness from me, an affirmation of Jehovah!
texts.isa.55.1: Ho, every thirsty one, come ye to the waters, And he who hath no money, Come ye, buy and eat, yea, come, buy Without money and without price, wine and milk.
texts.isa.55.2: Why do ye weigh money for that which is not bread? And your labour for that which is not for satiety? Hearken diligently unto me, and eat good, And your soul doth delight itself in fatness.
texts.isa.55.3: Incline your ear, and come unto me, Hear, and your soul doth live, And I make for you a covenant age-during, The kind acts of David -- that are stedfast.
texts.isa.55.4: Lo, a witness to peoples I have given him, A leader and commander to peoples.
texts.isa.55.5: Lo, a nation thou knowest not, thou callest, And a nation who know thee not unto thee do run, For the sake of Jehovah thy God, And for the Holy One of Israel, Because He hath beautified thee.
texts.isa.55.6: Seek ye Jehovah, while He is found, Call ye Him, while He is near,
texts.isa.55.7: Forsake doth the wicked his way, And the man of iniquity his thoughts, And he returneth to Jehovah, and He pitieth him, And unto our God for He multiplieth to pardon.
texts.isa.55.8: For not My thoughts [are] your thoughts, Nor your ways My ways, -- an affirmation of Jehovah,
texts.isa.55.9: For high have the heavens been above the earth, So high have been My ways above your ways, And My thoughts above your thoughts.
texts.isa.55.10: For, as come down doth the shower, And the snow from the heavens, And thither returneth not, But hath watered the earth, And hath caused it to yield, and to spring up, And hath given seed to the sower, and bread to the eater,
texts.isa.55.11: So is My word that goeth out of My mouth, It turneth not back unto Me empty, But hath done that which I desired, And prosperously effected that [for] which I sent it.
texts.isa.55.12: For with joy ye go forth, And with peace ye are brought in, The mountains and the hills Break forth before you [with] singing, And all trees of the field clap the hand.
texts.isa.55.13: Instead of the thorn come up doth fir, Instead of the brier come up doth myrtle, And it hath been to Jehovah for a name, For a sign age-during -- it is not cut off!
texts.isa.56.1: Thus said Jehovah: `Keep ye judgment, and do righteousness, For near [is] My salvation to come, And My righteousness to be revealed.'
texts.isa.56.2: O the happiness of a man who doth this, And of a son of man who keepeth hold on it, Keeping the sabbath from polluting it, And keeping his hand from doing any evil.
texts.isa.56.3: Nor speak let a son of the stranger, Who is joined unto Jehovah, saying: `Jehovah doth certainly separate me from His people.' Nor say let the eunuch, `Lo, I am a tree dried up,'
texts.isa.56.4: For thus said Jehovah of the eunuchs, Who do keep My sabbaths, And have fixed on that which I desired, And are keeping hold on My covenant:
texts.isa.56.5: I have given to them in My house, And within My walls a station and a name, Better than sons and than daughters, A name age-during I give to him That is not cut off.
texts.isa.56.6: And sons of the stranger, who are joined to Jehovah, To serve Him, and to love the name of Jehovah, To be to Him for servants, Every keeper of the sabbath from polluting it, And those keeping hold on My covenant.
texts.isa.56.7: I have brought them unto My holy mountain, And caused them to rejoice in My house of prayer, Their burnt-offerings and their sacrifices [Are] for a pleasing thing on Mine altar, For My house, `A house of prayer,' Is called for all the peoples.
texts.isa.56.8: An affirmation of the Lord Jehovah, Who is gathering the outcasts of Israel: `Again I gather to him -- to his gathered ones.'
texts.isa.56.9: Every beast of the field, Come to devour, every beast in the forest.
texts.isa.56.10: Blind [are] his watchmen -- all of them, They have not known, All of them [are] dumb dogs, they are not able to bark, Dozing, lying down, loving to slumber.
texts.isa.56.11: And the dogs [are] strong of desire, They have not known sufficiency, And they [are] shepherds! They have not known understanding, All of them to their own way they did turn, Each to his dishonest gain from his quarter:
texts.isa.56.12: `Come ye, I take wine, And we drink, quaff strong drink, And as this day hath been to-morrow, Great -- exceeding abundant!'
texts.isa.57.1: The righteous hath perished, And there is none laying [it] to heart, And men of kindness are gathered, Without any considering that from the face of evil Gathered is the righteous one.
texts.isa.57.2: He entereth into peace, they rest on their beds, [Each] is going straightforward.
texts.isa.57.3: And ye, come near hither, O sons of a sorceress, seed of an adulterer, Even thou dost commit whoredom.
texts.isa.57.4: Against whom do ye sport yourselves? Against whom enlarge ye the mouth? Prolong ye the tongue? Are not ye children of transgression? a false seed?
texts.isa.57.5: Who are inflamed among oaks, under every green tree, Slaughtering the children in valleys, Under clefts of the rocks.
texts.isa.57.6: Among the smooth things of a brook [is] thy portion, They -- they [are] thy lot, Also to them thou hast poured out an oblation, Thou hast caused a present to ascend, For these things am I comforted?
texts.isa.57.7: On a mountain, high and exalted, Thou hast set thy couch, Also thither thou hast gone up to make a sacrifice.
texts.isa.57.8: And behind the door, and the post, Thou hast set up thy memorial, For from Me thou hast removed, and goest up, Thou hast enlarged thy couch, And dost covenant for thyself among them, Thou hast loved their couch, the station thou sawest,
texts.isa.57.9: And goest joyfully to the king in ointment, And dost multiply thy perfumes, And sendest thine ambassadors afar off, And humblest thyself unto Sheol.
texts.isa.57.10: In the greatness of thy way thou hast laboured, Thou hast not said, `It is desperate.' The life of thy hand thou hast found, Therefore thou hast not been sick.
texts.isa.57.11: And of whom hast thou been afraid, and fearest, That thou liest, and Me hast not remembered? Thou hast not laid [it] to thy heart, Am not I silent, even from of old? And Me thou fearest not?
texts.isa.57.12: I declare thy righteousness, and thy works, And they do not profit thee.
texts.isa.57.13: When thou criest, let thy gatherings deliver thee, And all of them carry away doth wind, Take away doth vanity, And whoso is trusting in Me inheriteth the land, And doth possess My holy mountain.
texts.isa.57.14: And he hath said, `Raise up, raise up, prepare a way, Lift a stumbling-block out of the way of My people.'
texts.isa.57.15: For thus said the high and exalted One, Inhabiting eternity, and holy [is] His name: `In the high and holy place I dwell, And with the bruised and humble of spirit, To revive the spirit of the humble, And to revive the heart of bruised ones,'
texts.isa.57.16: For, not to the age do I strive, nor for ever am I wroth, For the spirit from before Me is feeble, And the souls I have made.
texts.isa.57.17: For the iniquity of his dishonest gain, I have been wroth, and I smite him, Hiding -- and am wroth, And he goeth on turning back in the way of his heart.
texts.isa.57.18: His ways I have seen, and I heal him, yea, I lead him, And recompense comforts to him and to his mourning ones.
texts.isa.57.19: Producing the fruit of the lips, `Peace, peace,' to the far off, and to the near, And I have healed him, said Jehovah.
texts.isa.57.20: And the wicked [are] as the driven out sea, For to rest it is not able, And its waters cast out filth and mire.
texts.isa.57.21: There is no peace, said my God, to the wicked!
texts.isa.58.1: Call with the throat, restrain not, As a trumpet lift up thy voice, And declare to My people their transgression, And to the house of Jacob their sins;
texts.isa.58.2: Seeing -- Me day by day they seek, And the knowledge of My ways they desire, As a nation that righteousness hath done, And the judgment of its God hath not forsaken, They ask of me judgments of righteousness, The drawing near of God they desire:
texts.isa.58.3: `Why have we fasted, and Thou hast not seen? We have afflicted our soul, and Thou knowest not.' Lo, in the day of your fast ye find pleasure, And all your labours ye exact.
texts.isa.58.4: Lo, for strife and debate ye fast, And to smite with the fist of wickedness, Ye fast not as [to]-day, To sound in the high place your voice.
texts.isa.58.5: Like this is the fast that I choose? The day of a man's afflicting his soul? To bow as a reed his head, And sackcloth and ashes spread out? This dost thou call a fast, And a desirable day -- to Jehovah?
texts.isa.58.6: Is not this the fast that I chose -- To loose the bands of wickedness, To shake off the burdens of the yoke, And to send out the oppressed free, And every yoke ye draw off?
texts.isa.58.7: Is it not to deal to the hungry thy bread, And the mourning poor bring home, That thou seest the naked and cover him, And from thine own flesh hide not thyself?
texts.isa.58.8: Then broken up as the dawn is thy light, And thy health in haste springeth up, Gone before thee hath thy righteousness, The honour of Jehovah doth gather thee.
texts.isa.58.9: Then thou callest, and Jehovah answereth, Thou criest, and He saith, `Behold Me.' If thou turn aside from thy midst the yoke, The sending forth of the finger, And the speaking of vanity,
texts.isa.58.10: And dost bring out to the hungry thy soul, And the afflicted soul dost satisfy, Then risen in the darkness hath thy light, And thy thick darkness [is] as noon.
texts.isa.58.11: And Jehovah doth lead thee continually, And hath satisfied in drought thy soul, And thy bones He armeth, And thou hast been as a watered garden, And as an outlet of waters, whose waters lie not.
texts.isa.58.12: And they have built out of thee the wastes of old, The foundations of many generations thou raisest up, And one calleth thee, `Repairer of the breach, Restorer of paths to rest in.'
texts.isa.58.13: If thou dost turn from the sabbath thy foot, Doing thine own pleasure on My holy day, And hast cried to the sabbath, `A delight,' To the holy of Jehovah, `Honoured,' And hast honoured it, without doing thine own ways, Without finding thine own pleasure, And speaking a word.
texts.isa.58.14: Then dost thou delight thyself on Jehovah, And I have caused thee to ride on high places of earth, And have caused thee to eat the inheritance of Jacob thy father, For the mouth of Jehovah hath spoken!
texts.isa.59.1: Lo, the hand of Jehovah Hath not been shortened from saving, Nor heavy his ear from hearing.
texts.isa.59.2: But your iniquities have been separating Between you and your God, And your sins have hidden The Presence from you -- from hearing.
texts.isa.59.3: For your hands have been polluted with blood, And your fingers with iniquity, Your lips have spoken falsehood, Your tongue perverseness doth mutter.
texts.isa.59.4: There is none calling in righteousness, And there is none pleading in faithfulness, Trusting on emptiness, and speaking falsehood, Conceiving perverseness, and bearing iniquity.
texts.isa.59.5: Eggs of a viper they have hatched, And webs of a spider they weave, Whoso is eating their eggs doth die, And the crushed hatcheth a viper.
texts.isa.59.6: Their webs become not a garment, Nor do they cover themselves with their works, Their works [are] works of iniquity, And a deed of violence [is] in their hands.
texts.isa.59.7: Their feet to evil do run, And they haste to shed innocent blood, Their thoughts [are] thoughts of iniquity, Spoiling and destruction [are] in their highways.
texts.isa.59.8: A way of peace they have not known, And there is no judgment in their paths, Their paths they have made perverse for themselves, No treader in it hath known peace.
texts.isa.59.9: Therefore hath judgment been far from us, And righteousness reacheth us not, We wait for light, and lo, darkness, For brightness -- in thick darkness we go,
texts.isa.59.10: We feel like the blind [for] the wall, Yea, as without eyes we feel, We have stumbled at noon as at twilight, In desolate places as the dead.
texts.isa.59.11: We make a noise as bears -- all of us, And as doves we coo sorely; We wait for judgment, and there is none, For salvation -- it hath been far from us.
texts.isa.59.12: For our transgressions have been multiplied before Thee, And our sins have testified against us, For our transgressions [are] with us, And our iniquities -- we have known them.
texts.isa.59.13: Transgressing, and lying against Jehovah, And removing from after our God, Speaking oppression and apostacy, Conceiving and uttering from the heart Words of falsehood.
texts.isa.59.14: And removed backward is judgment, And righteousness afar off standeth, For truth hath been feeble in the street, And straightforwardness is not able to enter,
texts.isa.59.15: And the truth is lacking, And whoso is turning aside from evil, Is making himself a spoil. And Jehovah seeth, and it is evil in His eyes, That there is no judgment.
texts.isa.59.16: And He seeth that there is no man, And is astonished that there is no intercessor, And His own arm giveth salvation to Him, And His righteousness -- it sustained Him.
texts.isa.59.17: And He putteth on righteousness as a breastplate, And an helmet of salvation on His head, And He putteth on garments of vengeance [for] clothing, And is covered, as [with] an upper-robe, [with] zeal.
texts.isa.59.18: According to deeds -- so He repayeth. Fury to His adversaries, [their] deed to His enemies, To the isles [their] deed He repayeth.
texts.isa.59.19: And they fear from the west the name of Jehovah, And from the rising of the sun -- His honour, When come in as a flood doth an adversary, The Spirit of Jehovah hath raised an ensign against him.
texts.isa.59.20: And come to Zion hath a redeemer, Even to captives of transgression in Jacob, An affirmation of Jehovah.
texts.isa.59.21: And I -- this [is] My covenant with them, said Jehovah, My Spirit that [is] on thee, And My words that I have put in thy mouth, Depart not from thy mouth, And from the mouth of thy seed, And from the mouth of thy seed's seed, said Jehovah, From henceforth unto the age!
texts.isa.60.1: Arise, be bright, for come hath thy light, And the honour of Jehovah hath risen on thee.
texts.isa.60.2: For, lo, the darkness doth cover the earth, And thick darkness the peoples, And on thee rise doth Jehovah, And His honour on thee is seen.
texts.isa.60.3: And come have nations to thy light, And kings to the brightness of thy rising.
texts.isa.60.4: Lift up round about thine eyes and see, All of them have been gathered, they have come to thee, Thy sons from afar do come, And thy daughters on the side are supported.
texts.isa.60.5: Then thou seest, and hast become bright, And thine heart hath been afraid and enlarged, For turn unto thee doth the multitude of the sea, The forces of nations do come to thee.
texts.isa.60.6: A company of camels covereth thee, Dromedaries of Midian and Ephah, All of them from Sheba do come, Gold and frankincense they bear, And of the praises of Jehovah they proclaim the tidings.
texts.isa.60.7: All the flock of Kedar are gathered to thee, The rams of Nebaioth do serve thee, They ascend for acceptance Mine altar, And the house of My beauty I beautify.
texts.isa.60.8: Who [are] these -- as a thick cloud they fly, And as doves unto their windows?
texts.isa.60.9: Surely for Me isles do wait, And ships of Tarshish first, To bring thy sons from afar, Their silver and their gold with them, To the name of Jehovah thy God, And to the Holy One of Israel, Because He hath beautified thee.
texts.isa.60.10: And sons of a stranger have built thy walls, And their kings do serve thee, For in My wrath I have smitten thee, And in My good pleasure I have pitied thee.
texts.isa.60.11: And opened have thy gates continually, By day and by night they are not shut, To bring unto thee the force of nations, Even their kings are led.
texts.isa.60.12: For the nation and the kingdom that do not serve thee perish, Yea, the nations are utterly wasted.
texts.isa.60.13: The honour of Lebanon unto thee doth come, Fir, pine, and box together, To beautify the place of My sanctuary, And the place of My feet I make honourable.
texts.isa.60.14: And come unto thee, bowing down, Have sons of those afflicting thee, And bowed themselves to the soles of thy feet Have all despising thee, And they have cried to thee: `City of Jehovah, Zion of the Holy One of Israel.'
texts.isa.60.15: Instead of thy being forsaken and hated, And none passing through, I have made thee for an excellency age-during, A joy of generation and generation.
texts.isa.60.16: And thou hast sucked the milk of nations, Yea, the breast of kings thou suckest, And thou hast known that I, Jehovah, Thy Saviour, and Thy Redeemer, [Am] the Mighty One of Jacob.
texts.isa.60.17: Instead of the brass I bring in gold, And instead of the iron I bring in silver, And instead of the wood brass, And instead of the stone iron, And I have made thy inspection peace, And thy exactors righteousness.
texts.isa.60.18: Violence is not heard any more in thy land, Spoiling and destruction in thy borders, And thou hast called `Salvation' thy walls, And thy gates, `Praise.'
texts.isa.60.19: To thee no more is the sun for a light by day, And for brightness the moon giveth not light to thee, And Jehovah hath become to thee A light age-during, and thy God thy beauty.
texts.isa.60.20: Thy sun goeth no more in, And thy moon is not removed, For Jehovah becometh to thee a light age-during. And the days of thy mourning have been completed.
texts.isa.60.21: And thy people [are] all of them righteous, To the age they possess the earth, A branch of My planting, A work of My hands, to be beautified.
texts.isa.60.22: The little one doth become a chief, And the small one a mighty nation, I, Jehovah, in its own time do hasten it!
texts.isa.61.1: The Spirit of the Lord Jehovah [is] on me, Because Jehovah did anoint me To proclaim tidings to the humble, He sent me to bind the broken of heart, To proclaim to captives liberty, And to bound ones an opening of bands.
texts.isa.61.2: To proclaim the year of the good pleasure of Jehovah, And the day of vengeance of our God, To comfort all mourners.
texts.isa.61.3: To appoint to mourners in Zion, To give to them beauty instead of ashes, The oil of joy instead of mourning, A covering of praise for a spirit of weakness, And He is calling to them, `Trees of righteousness, The planting of Jehovah -- to be beautified.'
texts.isa.61.4: And they have built the wastes of old, The desolations of the ancients they raise up, And they have renewed waste cities, The desolations of generation and generation.
texts.isa.61.5: And strangers have stood and fed your flock, Sons of a foreigner [are] your husbandmen, And your vine-dressers.
texts.isa.61.6: And ye are called `Priests of Jehovah,' `Ministers of our God,' is said of you, The strength of nations ye consume, And in their honour ye do boast yourselves.
texts.isa.61.7: Instead of your shame and confusion, A second time they sing of their portion, Therefore in their land A second time do they take possession, Joy age-during [is] for them.
texts.isa.61.8: For I [am] Jehovah, loving judgment, Hating plunder for a burnt-offering, And I have given their wage in truth, And a covenant age-during I make for them.
texts.isa.61.9: And known among nations hath been their seed, And their offspring in the midst of the peoples, All their beholders acknowledge them, For they [are] a seed Jehovah hath blessed.
texts.isa.61.10: I greatly rejoice in Jehovah, Joy doth my soul in my God, For He clothed me with garments of salvation, With a robe of righteousness covereth Me, As a bridegroom prepareth ornaments, And as a bride putteth on her jewels.
texts.isa.61.11: For, as the earth bringeth forth her shoots, And as a garden causeth its sown things to shoot up, So the Lord Jehovah causeth righteousness and praise To shoot up before all the nations!
texts.isa.62.1: For Zion's sake I am not silent, And for Jerusalem's sake I do not rest, Till her righteousness go out as brightness, And her salvation, as a torch that burneth.
texts.isa.62.2: And nations have seen thy righteousness, And all kings thine honour, And He is giving to thee a new name, That the mouth of Jehovah doth define.
texts.isa.62.3: And thou hast been a crown of beauty in the hand of Jehovah, And a diadem of royalty in the hand of thy God,
texts.isa.62.4: It is not said of thee any more, `Forsaken!' And of thy land it is not said any more, `Desolate,' For to thee is cried, `My delight [is] in her,' And to thy land, `Married,' For Jehovah hath delighted in thee, And thy land is married.
texts.isa.62.5: For a young man doth marry a virgin, Thy Builders do marry thee, With the joy of a bridegroom over a bride, Rejoice over thee doth thy God.
texts.isa.62.6: `On thy walls, O Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen, All the day, and all the night, Continually, they are not silent.' O ye remembrancers of Jehovah, Keep not silence for yourselves,
texts.isa.62.7: And give not silence to Him, Till He establish, and till He make Jerusalem A praise in the earth.
texts.isa.62.8: Sworn hath Jehovah by His right hand, Even by the arm of His strength: `I give not thy corn any more [as] food for thine enemies, Nor do sons of a stranger drink thy new wine, For which thou hast laboured.
texts.isa.62.9: For, those gathering it do eat it, and have praised Jehovah, And those collecting it do drink it in My holy courts.'
texts.isa.62.10: Pass ye on, pass on through the gates, Prepare ye the way of the people, Raise up, raise up the highway, clear it from stones, Lift up an ensign over the peoples.
texts.isa.62.11: Lo, Jehovah hath proclaimed unto the end of the earth: `Say ye to the daughter of Zion, Lo, thy salvation hath come,' Lo, his hire [is] with him, and his wage before him.
texts.isa.62.12: And they have cried to them, `People of the Holy One, Redeemed of Jehovah,' Yea, to thee is called, `Sought out one, a city not forsaken!'
texts.isa.63.1: `Who [is] this coming from Edom? With dyed garments from Bozrah? This that is honourable in his clothing, Travelling in the abundance of his power?' -- `I, speaking in righteousness, mighty to save.'
texts.isa.63.2: `Wherefore [is] thy clothing red? And thy garments as treading in a wine fat?'
texts.isa.63.3: -- `A wine-press I have trodden by myself, And of the peoples there is no one with me, And I tread them in mine anger, And I trample them in my fury, Sprinkled is their strength on my garments, And all my clothing I have polluted.
texts.isa.63.4: For the day of vengeance [is] in my heart, And the year of my redeemed hath come.
texts.isa.63.5: And I look attentively, and there is none helping, And I am astonished that there is none supporting, And give salvation to me doth mine own arm. And my wrath -- it hath supported me.
texts.isa.63.6: And I tread down peoples in mine anger, And I make them drunk in my fury, And I bring down to earth their strength.
texts.isa.63.7: The kind acts of Jehovah I make mention of, The praises of Jehovah, According to all that Jehovah hath done for us, And the abundance of the goodness to the house of Israel, That He hath done for them, According to His mercies, And according to the abundance of His kind acts.
texts.isa.63.8: And He saith, Only My people they [are], Sons -- they lie not, and He is to them for a saviour.
texts.isa.63.9: In all their distress [He is] no adversary, And the messenger of His presence saved them, In His love and in His pity He redeemed them, And He doth lift them up, And beareth them all the days of old.
