texts.isa.10.11: Shall I not as I have done to Samaria and her idols, so, do to Jerusalem and her images?
texts.isa.10.12: Wherefore it shall come to pass—When My Lord shall finish his whole work upon Mount Zion and upon Jerusalem, I will bring punishment—Upon the fruit of the greatness of heart of the king of Assyria. And upon the vainglory of his uplifted eyes,
texts.isa.10.13: For he hath said—By the strength of mine own hand, have I effectually wrought, And by my wisdom—for I have discernment,—That I might remove the bounds of peoples, Yea their treasures, have I plundered That I might lay prostrate as a mighty one the inhabitants;
texts.isa.10.14: And my hand hath found as a nest the wealth of the peoples, And as the gathering of eggs that are forsaken, all the earth, have, I, gathered,—And there was none to flap a wing, or open a mouth or chirp.
texts.isa.10.15: Shall the axe boast itself against him that heweth therewith? Or, the saw, magnify itself, against him that wieldeth it? As if a rod, could wield, them who lift it up! As if a staff, could raise, what is, not wood!
texts.isa.10.16: Therefore, shall the Lord, Yahweh of hosts, Send, among his fat ones, leanness, And under his glory, shall he kindle a kindling, like the kindling of fire;
texts.isa.10.17: So shall, the Light of Israel, become, a fire, And his Holy One, a flame, Which shall burn and consume his thorns and his briars, in one day;
texts.isa.10.18: And the glory of his forest and of his garden land, both soul and body, shall it bring to an end,—And it shall be like the wasting away of a consumptive.
texts.isa.10.19: And, the remnant of his forest-trees, few in number, shall become,—yea, a child, might describe them!
texts.isa.10.20: And it shall come to pass in that day, That the remnant of Israel. And the escaped of the house of Jacob Shall, no more again, lean upon him that smote them,—But shall lean upon Yahweh the Holy One of Israel, in truth.
texts.isa.10.21: A remnant, shall return, The remnant of Jacob,—unto the mighty GOD;
texts.isa.10.22: For though thy people, O Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, A [mere] remnant, shall return of them,—A full end decreed, bringeth in, justice, like a flood;
texts.isa.10.23: For, a full end and that a decreed one, is My Lord Yahweh of hosts executing in the midst of all the earth.
texts.isa.10.24: Therefore, thus, saith My Lord, Yahweh of hosts, Do not fear O my people dwelling in Zion, because of Assyria,—When with his rod, he would smite thee, And when his staff, he would lift up against thee in the manner of Egypt;
texts.isa.10.25: For, yet a very little while, and displeasure shall end, Yea, mine anger, over their destruction.
texts.isa.10.26: And Yahweh of hosts, will brandish over him, a scourge—Like the smiting of Midian at the rock Oreb,—And his staff being over the sea, He will lift it up in the manner of Egypt;
texts.isa.10.27: And it shall come to pass, in that day, That his burden shall remove from off thy shoulder, And his yoke from off thy neck,—Yea, the yoke shall be broken because of fatness.
texts.isa.10.28: He hath come in unto Ayyath, Hath passed through Migron,—At Michmash, storeth his baggage:
texts.isa.10.29: They have passed over the pass, Geba is his halting-place,—Terror-stricken is Ramah, Gibeah of Saul, hath fled!
texts.isa.10.30: Make shrill thy voice, O daughter of Gallim! Hearken, O Laishah, Answer, O Anathoth!
texts.isa.10.31: Madmenah, hath fled,—The inhabitants of Gebim, have gone into safety:
texts.isa.10.32: While yet to-day, in Nob, he tarrieth, He brandisheth his hand toward The mount of the daughter of Zion, The hill of Jerusalem.
texts.isa.10.33: Behold! the Lord, Yahweh of hosts, is about to lop off a tree-crown, with a crash,—Then shall, they who are lifted on high, be hewn down, And, the lofty, be laid low;
texts.isa.10.34: Then will he fell the thickets of the forest with iron,—And, Lebanon by a majestic one shall fall.
texts.isa.11.1: But there shall come forth a shoot from the stock of Jesse,—And, a sprout from his roots, shall bear fruit;
texts.isa.11.2: And the spirit of Yahweh shall rest upon him,—The spirit of wisdom and understanding, The spirit of counsel and might, The spirit of knowledge and reverence of Yahweh;
texts.isa.11.3: So will he find fragrance, in the reverence of Yahweh, And not, by the sight of his eyes, will he judge, Nor by the hearing of his ears, will he decide;
texts.isa.11.4: But he will judge with righteousness! them who are poor, And decide with equity! for the oppressed of the land,—And he will smite the land With the sceptre of his mouth, And with the breath of his lips, will he slay the lawless one;
texts.isa.11.5: And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins,—And faithfulness the girdle of his reins;
texts.isa.11.6: And the wolf shall dwell with the lamb, And, the leopard, with the kid, shall lie down,—And the calf and the young lion and the fatling—together, With, a little child, leading them;
texts.isa.11.7: And the cow, with the bear shall find pasture, Together, shall their young ones, lie down,—And, the lion, like the ox, shall eat straw;
texts.isa.11.8: And the sucking child shall caress over the hole of the asp, Yea over the viper’s den, hath the weaned child stretched out his hand:
texts.isa.11.9: They shall not hurt—nor destroy, in all my holy mountain,—For filled is the land with the knowledge of Yahweh, As the waters, to the sea, form a covering.
texts.isa.11.10: And there shall come to be, in that day, A root of Jesse, which shall be standing as an ensign of peoples, Unto him, shall nations seek,—And, his resting-place, shall be, glorious.
texts.isa.11.11: And it shall come to pass in that day, That My Lord will again a second time set his hand, to possess himself of the remnant of his people,—who shall be left—from Assyria and from Egypt and from Pathros and from Ethiopia and from Elam and from Shinar and from Hamath and from the Coastlands of the sea;
texts.isa.11.12: And he will lift up a standard to the nations, And will gather the outcasts of Israel,—And the dispersed of Judah, will he collect, From the four corners of the earth.
texts.isa.11.13: And the envy of Ephraim shall be removed, And the vexatious doings of Judah, shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah, shall not vex Ephraim;
texts.isa.11.14: But they shall fly on the wing of the Philistines in the west, Together, shall they make prey of the sons of the east,—On Edom and Moab, putting forth their hand, With the sons of Ammon hearkening unto them.
texts.isa.11.15: And Yahweh, will devote to destruction, the gulf of the Egyptian sea, And will brandish his hand against the River [="Euphrates"], in the full force of his spirit,—And will smite it in the seven streams And cause a marching through in sandals,
texts.isa.11.16: So shall there be a highway for the remnant of his people who shall be left out of Assyria,—Like as it was to Israel, in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt!
texts.isa.12.1: Thou shalt say, therefore, in that day, I will praise thee, O Yahweh! Though thou hast been angry with me, Thine anger turneth back. And thou dost comfort me.
texts.isa.12.2: Lo, GOD is my salvation! I will trust and not dread,—For, my might and melody, is Yah, Yahweh, And he hath become mine, by salvation.
texts.isa.12.3: Therefore shall ye draw water, with rejoicing,—out of the fountains of salvation.
texts.isa.12.4: And ye shall say in that day, Praise Yahweh. Call upon his Name, Make known among the peoples, his doings,—Bring to remembrance that, exalted, is his Name!
texts.isa.12.5: Praise in song Yahweh, For a splendid thing, hath he done,—Well known, is this in all the earth.
texts.isa.12.6: Make shrill thy voice and sing out thou inhabitress of Zion,—That great in the midst of thee, is the Holy One of Israel.
texts.isa.13.1: The oracle on Babylon,—of which Isaiah, son of Amoz had vision:—
texts.isa.13.2: Upon a bare mountain, lift ye up a standard, Raise high the voice to them, Wave the hand, That they may enter the doors of nobles.
texts.isa.13.3: I myself, have given charge to my hallowed ones,—Yea I have called My heroes in showing mine anger, My proudly exulting ones.
texts.isa.13.4: The noise of a multitude in the mountains, A resemblance of many people,—The noise of a tumult of kingdoms Nations gathered together, Yahweh of hosts, mustering a host for battle!
texts.isa.13.5: They are coming in From a land far away. From the utmost bound of the heavens,—Yahweh—with his weapons of indignation, To destroy the land.
texts.isa.13.6: Howl ye! for at hand is the day of Yahweh,—As a veritable destruction from the Almighty, shall it come.
texts.isa.13.7: For this cause—All hands, shall hang down,—and Every mortal heart, melt.
texts.isa.13.8: And they shall be in distress—Writhings and pains, shall lay hold, As a woman in childbirth, shall they be in pangs,—Everyone, at his neighbour, shall look in amazement, Faces of flames, their faces!
texts.isa.13.9: Lo! the day of Yahweh, coming in, Fierce and overflowing, and burning with anger,—To devote the earth to desolation, And her sinners, will he destroy out of it.
texts.isa.13.10: For the stars of the heavens and their constellations, shall not flash forth their light,—Obscured shall be the sun in his going forth, And the moon, shall not shed her light.
texts.isa.13.11: And I will visit, upon the inhabited earth, calamity!, And upon the lawless, their punishment, And will quiet the arrogance of the proud, And the loftiness of tyrants, will I lay low.
texts.isa.13.12: I will cause, a man, to be more precious than fine gold,—Even a son of earth than, the finest gold of Ophir.
texts.isa.13.13: For this cause, the heavens, will I disturb, And, the earth, shall tremble out of her place,—In the wrath of Yahweh of hosts, And in the day of the glow of his anger.
texts.isa.13.14: And it shall be—Like a gazelle that is chased, And like a sheep with none to lift it up,—Each, to his own people, will they turn, And, each, to his own land, will they flee:
texts.isa.13.15: Every one found, shall be thrust through,—And, every one taken, shall fall by the sword;
texts.isa.13.16: And, their infants, shall be dashed to the ground, before their eyes,—Plundered shall be, their houses, and their wives ravished.
texts.isa.13.17: Behold me! stirring up against them the Medes,—Who of silver, shall take no account, And as for gold, they shall not delight in it;
texts.isa.13.18: And, bows, shall dash the young to pieces,—And on the fruit of the womb, will they have no pity, Over children, will their eye throw no shield.
texts.isa.13.19: Thus shall Babylon—The most lovely of kingdoms, The majestic beauty of the Chaldees—Become as in the divine overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah.
texts.isa.13.20: It shall not be dwelt in for ever, Neither shall it be inhabited from generation to generation,—Neither shall encamp there, an Arab, Nor, shepherds, fold their flocks there.
texts.isa.13.21: Then shall lie down there, wild beasts, And filled shall be their houses with owls,—Then shall inhabit there, the ostrich, And shaggy creatures, shall dance there.
texts.isa.13.22: And jackals shall answer, in their citadels, And wild dogs, in their voluptuous palaces,—And near to come is her time, And, her days, shall not be delayed.
texts.isa.14.1: For Yahweh will have compassion on Jacob, And will yet choose Israel, And will give them rest upon their own soil,—And the sojourner, shall join himself, unto them, And they shall attach themselves unto the house of Jacob;
texts.isa.14.2: And peoples shall take them, and bring them into their own place, And the house of Israel shall possess themselves of them upon the soil of Yahweh for servants and for handmaids,—Thus shall they be taking captive their captors, And shall tread down their oppressors.
texts.isa.14.3: And it shall come to pass, in the day when Yahweh shall give thee rest from thy toil, and from thy disquiet,—and from the hard service which had been laid upon thee,
texts.isa.14.4: that thou shalt take up this taunt over the king of Babylon, and shalt say:—How hath ceased the oppressor! Ceased the exactress!
texts.isa.14.5: Broke hath Yahweh the staff of the lawless,—The sceptre of despots;
texts.isa.14.6: Smiting peoples in passion With stroke unremitting,—Trampling, in anger, on nations, Persecution unhindered.
texts.isa.14.7: Quiet, at rest, the whole earth,—Men have burst into shouting!
texts.isa.14.8: Yea the pine-trees, make mirth at thee, Cedars of Lebanon, Since thou wast laid low, No feller hath come up against us!
texts.isa.14.9: Hades beneath, is excited about thee To meet thine arrival,—Rousing up, for thee Shades, All the he-goats of earth! Maketh rise from their thrones, All the kings of the nations.
texts.isa.14.10: All of them, answer, and say to thee,—Thou too, made strengthless, as we! Unto us, art thou like!
texts.isa.14.11: Brought down to Hades, thy pride. The hum of thy harps, Beneath thee, is spread out corruption, And, thy coverlet—worms!
texts.isa.14.12: How hast thou fallen from heaven, O Shining One—Son of the Dawn! Hewn down to the earth, O crusher of nations!
texts.isa.14.13: Yet, thou, didst say in thy heart—The heavens, will I ascend, Above the stars of GOD, will I lift up my throne,—That I may sit in the Mount of Assembly In the Recesses of the North:
texts.isa.14.14: I will mount on the hills of the clouds, I will match the Most High!
texts.isa.14.15: Howbeit, to Hades, shalt thou be brought down,—To the Recesses of the Pit!
texts.isa.14.16: They who see thee, upon thee, will gaze, Upon thee, will thoughtfully muse,—Is this the man who startled the earth? Who terrified kingdoms?
texts.isa.14.17: Who made the world like a desert? And its cities, brake down? Its prisoners, he loosed not, Each one to his home?
texts.isa.14.18: All the kings of the nations—they all, are lying in state Each one in his crypt;
texts.isa.14.19: But, thou, art flung out from thy grave, Like a scion detested, Beshrouded with slain, the pierced of the sword, Like a carcase trod underfoot:
texts.isa.14.20: As for them who go down to the stones of the Pit, Thou shalt not be united with them in burial; For thy land, thou didst ruin Thy people, didst slay,—Unnamed to times age-abiding, Be the seed of the wicked!
texts.isa.14.21: Prepare—for his sons—shambles. For the iniquity of their fathers,—They shall not rise nor possess the earth, Nor fill the face of the world with cities.
texts.isa.14.22: I will rise. Then. against them, Declareth Yahweh of hosts,—And will cut off from Babylon Record and remnant And scion and seed, Declareth Yahweh.
texts.isa.14.23: And will make her a possession for the bittern, And marshes of water,—And will sweep it with the besom of destruction, Declareth Yahweh of hosts.
texts.isa.14.24: Yahweh of hosts, hath sworn, saying,—Surely as I intended, so, hath it come to pass, And as I purposed, the same, shall stand:—
texts.isa.14.25: That I will break in pieces the Assyrian in my land, Yea upon my mountains, will I tread him underfoot,—So shall be removed from off them his yoke, And his burden, from off their shoulder shall be removed.
texts.isa.14.26: This, is the purpose that is purposed upon all the earth,—And, this, the hand outstretched over all the nations;
texts.isa.14.27: For, Yahweh of hosts, hath purposed,—And who shall frustrate? And, his, is the hand outstretched, And who shall turn it back?
texts.isa.14.28: In the year that King Ahaz died, came this oracle:—
texts.isa.14.29: Do not rejoice, Philistia, any of thee, In that the rod of him that smote thee, is broken,—For, out of the root of the serpent, shall come forth, a viper, And his fruit be a fiery dragon that flieth.
texts.isa.14.30: Then shall feed the firstborn of the poor, And the needy, in confidence lie down,—And I will kill with famine thy root, And thy residue, shall be slain.
texts.isa.14.31: Howl—O gate, Make outcry—O city, Dispersed art thou Philistia, all of thee,—For out of the north, a smoke cometh in, With no straggler in his ranks.
texts.isa.14.32: What, then, shall one answer the messengers of a nation? That Yahweh, hath founded Zion, And in her, shall seek refuge the oppressed of his people.
texts.isa.15.1: The oracle on Moab: Because, in a night, was laid waste Ar of Moab—destroyed! Because, in a night, was laid waste Kir of Moab—destroyed,
texts.isa.15.2: He hath gone up to Bayith and Dibon, to the high places, to weep,—On Nebo and on Medeba, Moab is howling, On all their heads, a baldness, Every beard, clipped.
texts.isa.15.3: In their streets, have they girded them with sackcloth,—On their housetops, and in their broadways, every one is howling—melting in tears;
texts.isa.15.4: And Heshbon, hath made outcry, and Elealeh, Unto Jahaz, hath been heard their voice,—For this cause, do the armed men of Moab roar, Every man’s soul, quivereth to him.
texts.isa.15.5: Mine own heart, for Moab continueth to make outcry, Her fugitive, as far as Zoar, is like a heifer of three years; For the accent of Luhith, with weeping, they ascend, For by the way of Horonaim—an outcry of destruction, they excite;
texts.isa.15.6: For, the waters of Nimrim, shall become desolation,—For grass, hath dried up, Herbage hath failed, Green thing, hath not sprung up!
texts.isa.15.7: For this cause, the savings they had made and that which they had stored, Over the torrent-bed of the willows, shall they bear them.
texts.isa.15.8: For the outcry hath gone round the boundary of Moab,—As far as Eglaim, the howling thereof, And to Beer-elim, the howling thereof.
texts.isa.15.9: For the waters of Dimon, are full of blood, For I will lay upon Dimon new troubles,—To the escaped of Moab, the lions, Even to the survivors on the soil.
texts.isa.16.1: Send ye the lamb due to the ruler of the land, From Sela towards the desert,—Unto the mount of the daughter of Zion;
texts.isa.16.2: Yet shall it be that—Like wandering birds from a nest cast forth, Shall be the daughters of Moab, at the fords of Arnon.
texts.isa.16.3: Bring thou, in counsel, Execute thou judgment, Make as the night, thy shadow in the midst of high noon,—Hide thou the outcasts, The wanderer, do not thou reveal.
texts.isa.16.4: Let mine own outcasts, sojourn with thee, O Moab, become thou a covert to them from the face of the spoiler,—For vanished is the oppressor, At an end is extortion, They who tread down have ceased out of the land.
texts.isa.16.5: So shall be established, in lovingkindness, a throne, And one shall sit thereon, in truth, in the home of David,—Judging—and seeking justice and speeding righteousness.
texts.isa.16.6: We have heard of the arrogance of Moab, Proud exceedingly! His haughtiness and his arrogance and his passion, Not true, are his boastings.
texts.isa.16.7: Therefore shall, Moab, howl for, Moab, All that belong to her, shall wail,—For the ruins of Kir-hareseth, shall they moan out Utterly stricken!
texts.isa.16.8: For, the fields of Heshbon are withered—The vine of Sibmah, the owners of nations, have broken off ruddy branches, Unto Jazer, had they reached, They had spread abroad to the desert,—Her boughs, had stretched forth, had gone over to the sea.
texts.isa.16.9: For this cause, will I bewail, in the wailing of Jazer, The vine of Sibmah, I will drench thee with my tears, O Heshbon and Elealeh,—For, upon thy fruit-harvest, and upon thy grain-harvest, the battle-shout, hath fallen.
texts.isa.16.10: Now shall be withdrawn rejoicing and exultation out of the garden-land, And, in the vineyards, shall be neither singing nor shouting,—Wine in the winepress, the treader, shall not tread, The vintage-shout, have I made to cease.
texts.isa.16.11: For this cause, mine inward parts—for Moab, like a lyre, shall make a plaintive sound,—Yea what is within me, for Kir-heres.
texts.isa.16.12: And it shall be—When it is seen that Moab hath laboured in vain on the high place, He shall enter into his holy place to pray, and shall not prevail,
texts.isa.16.13: This, is the word which Yahweh spake concerning Moab in, time past;
texts.isa.16.14: But now, hath Yahweh spoken saying, In three years,—as the years of a hireling, shall the glory of Moab be diminished, with all the great multitude,—even a very small remnant, of no account.
texts.isa.17.1: The oracle on Damascus,—Lo! Damascus, is to be removed from being a city, And shall become a heap of ruins:
texts.isa.17.2: Forsaken, are the desolate cities,—For flocks, shall they serve, Which shall lie down and have none to make them afraid.
texts.isa.17.3: Then shall the fortress cease from Ephraim, And the kingdom from Damascus and the remnant of Syria,—Like the glory of the sons of Israel, shall they be,—Declareth Yahweh of hosts.
texts.isa.17.4: And it shall come to pass in that day, That the glory of Jacob, shall be diminished, And, the fatness of his flesh, shall be wasted;
texts.isa.17.5: And it shall come to pass—That, as the harvestman gathereth standing corn, And with his arm—the ears, he reapeth, Yea it shall come to pass—That, so, shall he be who gleaneth ears, in the vale of Rephaim;
texts.isa.17.6: Yet shall there be left therein, a gleaning. As in the beating of an olive-tree,—Two-three berries in the head of the tree-top,—Four—five, among her fruitful boughs, Declareth Yahweh God of Israel.
texts.isa.17.7: In that day, shall the son of earth look to him that made him,—And his eyes unto the Holy One of Israel, be turned;
texts.isa.17.8: And he shall not look unto the altars the work of his own hands,—Nor to what his own fingers have made, shall his eye be turned, Whether Sacred Stems or Sun-pillars.
texts.isa.17.9: In that day, shall his fortified cities become Like a neglected bough and a topmost branch, Which they neglected because of the sons of Israel,—So shall there be desolation.
texts.isa.17.10: Because thou didst forget the God of thy salvation, And thy Rock of refuge, thou didst not remember, For this cause, shalt thou plant very pleasant plants, And, the slip of a stranger, shalt thou set:
texts.isa.17.11: In the day when thou plantest, fence thou in, And in the morning, cause thou, thy slip, to blossom,—A harvest will have waved in the day of destiny, and mortal pain.
texts.isa.17.12: Alas! the booming of many peoples, Like the booming of the seas, shall they boom,—And the rushing of nations! Like the rushing of mighty waters, shall they rush.
texts.isa.17.13: Though nations like the rushing of many waters, shall rush, Yet shall one rebuke him, And he shall flee far away,—And be chased As the chaff of the mountains before a wind, And as whirling stubble before a storm!
texts.isa.17.14: At eventide, lo! terror, Before morning, he is not! This, is the portion of them who plunder us, And the lot of them who make of us a prey.
texts.isa.18.1: Ho! thou land of the buzzing of wings,—Which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia:
texts.isa.18.2: That sendeth by the sea, ambassadors Even in vessels of paper-reed, upon the face of the waters,—Go ye swift messengers Unto a nation drawn out and polished, Unto a people terrible from their beginning and onwards,—A nation most mighty and subduing, Whose land rivers have cut through.
texts.isa.18.3: All ye inhabitants of the world And ye, that dwell in the earth,—When there is lifted up an ensign on the mountains, Ye shall look, And when there is blown a horn, Ye shall hearken.
texts.isa.18.4: For, thus, said Yahweh unto me,—I must be quiet I must look on in my fixed place of abode,—Like a bright heat on the light, Like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.
texts.isa.18.5: For before harvest, when the bud is perfect, And, the blossom, becometh a ripening grape, Then will one cut down the twigs with pruning-hooks, And the tendrils, will he remove [and] cast down:
texts.isa.18.6: They shall be left together. To the ravenous birds, of the mountains, And to the beast of the earth,—Then shall the ravenous bird, summer upon them, And, every beast of the earth, upon them, shall winter.
texts.isa.18.7: In that time, shall there be borne along. As a present unto Yahweh of hosts A people drawn out and polished, Even from a people terrible from their beginning and onwards,—nation most mighty and subduing Whose land rivers, have cut through, Unto the place of the Name of Yahweh of hosts. Mount Zion.
texts.isa.19.1: The oracle on Egypt: Lo! Yahweh, riding upon a swift cloud, and he will enter Egypt, And the idols of Egypt shall shake at his presence, And, the heart of Egypt, shall melt within him;
texts.isa.19.2: And I will stir up Egyptians against Egyptians, And they shall fight—Every one against his brother and Every one against his neighbour,—City against city, and Kingdom against kingdom.
texts.isa.19.3: And the spirit of Egypt, shall vanish, within them, Yea the sagacity thereof, will I swallow up,—And they will seek Unto the idols and Unto them that mutter, and Unto them that have familiar spirits, and Unto the wizards;
texts.isa.19.4: And I will deliver the Egyptians into the hand of a cruel lord,—And a fierce king shall rule over them, Declareth the Lord, Yahweh of hosts.
texts.isa.19.5: And the waters shall be dried up from the great stream,—And the River, shall waste and be dry;
texts.isa.19.6: And rivers, shall stink, The canals of Egypt be shallow and waste, Reed and rush, be withered;
texts.isa.19.7: The meadows by the Nile, by the mouth of the Nile. And all that is sown in the Nile, Shall be dry, driven away, and not be!
texts.isa.19.8: Then shall the fishers, lament, And all shall mourn who cast in the Nile a hook,—And they who spread nets on the face of the waters shall languish;
texts.isa.19.9: Then shall turn pale The workers in combed flax,—and The weavers of white linen;
texts.isa.19.10: Then shall her pillars be crushed,—All who make wages, be bowed down in soul.
texts.isa.19.11: Surely, foolish, are the princes of Zoan, the wisest counsellors of Pharaoh, in counsel are brutish,—How can ye say unto Pharaoh, Son of the wise, am I Son of the kings of olden time?
texts.isa.19.12: Where then are thy wise men? Pray let them tell thee! And let them know what Yahweh of hosts hath purposed on Egypt!
texts.isa.19.13: Doting are the princes of Zoan, Deceived are the princes of Noph: They who are the corner-stone of her tribes, have led Egypt astray.
texts.isa.19.14: Yahweh, hath infused in her midst, a spirit of perverseness,—And they have led Egypt astray into all his own doings, As a drunken man staggereth into his own vomit;
texts.isa.19.15: And Egypt shall have nothing which can be done, Which head or tail, palm-top or rush, can do!
texts.isa.19.16: In that day, shall Egypt be like unto women,—And shall start and tremble because of the brandishing of the hand of Yahweh of hosts, which he is about to brandish over it.
texts.isa.19.17: Then shall the soil of Judah become, to Egypt, a terror; Every one to whom it is mentioned, will tremble,—Because of the purpose of Yahweh of hosts, which he is purposing against it.
texts.isa.19.18: In that day, shall there be five cities in the land of Egypt Speaking the language of Canaan, And swearing unto Yahweh of hosts,—The city of destruction, shall be the name of one!
texts.isa.19.19: In that day, shall there be An altar unto Yahweh, in the midst of the land of Egypt,—And a pillar near the boundary thereof unto Yahweh;
texts.isa.19.20: And it shall become a sign and a witness unto Yahweh of hosts in the land of Egypt,—For they will make outcry unto Yahweh, because of oppressors, That he would send them a saviour—and a great one Then will he deliver them.
texts.isa.19.21: Then will, Yahweh, make himself known, to the Egyptians, So shall the Egyptians know, Yahweh, in that day,—And they will offer a sacrifice and a present And will vow a vow unto Yahweh and will perform.
texts.isa.19.22: And Yahweh, will plague Egypt, plague and heal,—And they will turn unto Yahweh And he will be entreated of them and will heal them.
texts.isa.19.23: In that day, shall there be a highway. from Egypt to Assyria, And, the Assyrians, shall come into Egypt, And, the Egyptians, into Assyria; And, the Egyptians shall serve, with the Assyrians.
texts.isa.19.24: In that day, shall, Israel, be, a third, with Egypt and with Assyria,—A blessing in the midst of the earth:
texts.isa.19.25: Whom Yahweh of hosts hath blessed saying,—Blessed, be My people—the Egyptians, And the work of my hands—the Assyrians, And mine own inheritance—Israel.
texts.isa.20.1: In the year that Tartan entered Ashdod, when Sargon king of Assyria, sent him,—and he fought against Ashdod and captured it,—
texts.isa.20.2: At that time, spake Yahweh, through Isaiah son of Amoz, saying, Go, and loose the sackcloth from off thy loins, And thy sandal, draw thou off from thy foot,—And he did so, walking disrobed and barefoot.
texts.isa.20.3: Then said Yahweh,—As my servant Isaiah, hath walked, disrobed and barefoot three years as a sign and a wonder against Egypt and against Ethiopia,
texts.isa.20.4: So, shall the king of Assyria lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Ethiopia young and old disrobed and barefoot, with their persons behind Uncovered the shame of Egypt.
texts.isa.20.5: Thus shall they be confounded and turn pale,—For Ethiopia, their expectation, and For Egypt their boast;
texts.isa.20.6: And the inhabitant of this shore, shall exclaim, in that day, Lo! such, is our expectation, whereunto we fled for help, that we might be delivered from the presence of the king of Assyria! How then shall, we, escape?
texts.isa.21.1: The oracle on the desert of the sea: As storm-winds in the South which with a rush from the desert, do come from a terrible land,
texts.isa.21.2: [So] hath, a grievous vision, been told me:—the deceiver, is deceiving. And the spoiler, is spoiling, Go up, O Elam Besiege O Media, All the sighing she hath caused, have I made to cease.
texts.isa.21.3: For this cause, are my loins filled with anguish, Pangs, have seized me, as the pangs of her that is giving birth,—I writhe so that I cannot hear, I tremble, so that I cannot see:
texts.isa.21.4: My heart fluttereth, A horror, terrifieth me,—My twilight of pleasure, hath he turned for me into a time of trembling.
texts.isa.21.5: [Ye thought] to prepare the table—spread the mat—eat—drink! …Arise ye chieftains anoint the shield!
texts.isa.21.6: For, thus, hath My Lord said unto me,—Go, set the watchman, What he seeth, let him tell!
texts.isa.21.7: When he seeth A train of horsemen in double rank, A train of asses, A train of camels, Then shall he hearken attentively with diligent heed.
texts.isa.21.8: Then cried he. A lion! On the watch, O My Lord, had I been standing continually, by day, And at my post, had I been stationed whole nights;—
texts.isa.21.9: When lo! here was a train of men coming. With horsemen in double rank,—And one began and said, Fallen! fallen! is Babylon, And all the images of her gods, are smashed to the ground!
texts.isa.21.10: O thou My threshing! And the grain of my corn-floor! That which I have heard from Yahweh of hosts, the God of Israel, Have I declared, unto you.
texts.isa.21.11: The oracle on Dumah: Unto me, is one crying—out of Seir, Watchman! how far gone is the night? Watchman, how far gone is the night?
texts.isa.21.12: Said the watchman, There cometh a morning. But also a night,—If ye will enquire, enquire, ye—Come, again!
texts.isa.21.13: The oracle on Arabia,—Among the shrubs in Arabia, must ye lodge, Ye caravans of Dedanites.
texts.isa.21.14: To meet the thirsty, bring ye water,—Ye dwellers in the land of Tema; With bread for him, get in advance of him that is in flight!
texts.isa.21.15: For, before swords, have they fled: Before a sword that is drawn, Before a bow that is bent, And before the stress of war.
texts.isa.21.16: For, thus, hath My Lord said unto me,—Within a year according to the yearn of a hireling, shall fail all the glory of Kedar;
texts.isa.21.17: And, the remnant of the record of bowmen, The heroes of the sons of Kedar, shall become few; For Yahweh God of Israel, hath spoken.
texts.isa.22.1: The oracle on the valley of vision,—What aileth thee, then, That thou art wholly gone up to the house-tops?
texts.isa.22.2: With tumults, art thou filled, thou citadel in commotion! city exultant! Thy slain, are Not the slain, of the sword, Nor the dead in battle.
texts.isa.22.3: All thy ruler, having fled, together, by the bow, are taken captive: All found in thee have been taken captive, together, Far away, have they fled.
texts.isa.22.4: For this cause, I said—Look away from me, Bitterly, will I weep,—Do not press to comfort me, For the ruin of the daughter of my people.
texts.isa.22.5: For a day of confusion and downtreading and perplexity, pertaineth to My Lord, Yahweh of hosts, in the valley of vision, an undermining of walls, and a crying for help to the mountain.
texts.isa.22.6: Yea, Elam, beareth the quiver, With trains of men, [and] horsemen,—And, Kir, hath uncovered the shield.
texts.isa.22.7: And it hath come to pass that the choice of thy vales, are full of chariots; Yea, the horsemen, have set themselves, in array, at the gate.
texts.isa.22.8: Then removed he the veil of Judah,—Yea thou didst peer on that day, into the armoury of the forest-house;
texts.isa.22.9: And the breaches in the city of David, ye beheld for they were many,—So ye gathered together the waters of the lower pool;
texts.isa.22.10: And the houses of Jerusalem, ye counted,—And brake down the houses, to fortify the wall;
texts.isa.22.11: And a reservoir, ye made between the two walls, for the waters of the ancient pool,—And had no regard unto him that made it, Nor unto him that formed it long ago, had ye respect.
texts.isa.22.12: And, when My Lord Yahweh of hosts called in that day,—for weeping, and for lamentation, and for shaving bare and for girding with sackcloth,
texts.isa.22.13: Then lo! joy and rejoicing, killing oxen and slaughtering sheep, eating flesh and drinking wine,—Let us eat and drink, For to-morrow, we may die!
texts.isa.22.14: Therefore did Yahweh reveal himself in mine ears. Surely there shall be no propitiatory-covering put over this iniquity for you until ye die, Saith My Lord Yahweh of hosts.
texts.isa.22.15: Thus, said My Lord Yahweh, of hosts, Come go in unto this steward, Unto Shebna, who is over the house:
texts.isa.22.16: What doest thou here? And whom hast thou here? That thou hast hewn for thyself here a sepulchre,—As one hewing on high his sepulchre, Cutting out in the cliff a habitation for himself?
texts.isa.22.17: Lo! Yahweh, is about to hurl thee, with a hurl, O mighty man,—And roll thee with a roll;
texts.isa.22.18: He will, toss, thee, with a toss, like a ball, into a country wide on both hands,—There, shalt thou die, And there shall thy glorious chariots be the contempt of the house of thy lord.
texts.isa.22.19: Thus will I thrust thee out from thine office,—And from thy station, shall one tear thee down.
texts.isa.22.20: And it shall come to pass in that day, That I will call for my servant, for Eliakim son of Hilkiah,
texts.isa.22.21: And will clothe him with thy tunic And with thy girdle, will I gird him, And thine authority, will I deliver into his hand,—So shall he become a father To the inhabitant of Jerusalem and To the house of Judah.
texts.isa.22.22: And I will lay the key of the house of David upon his shoulder,—And he shall open and none shall shut, And shut and none shall open;
texts.isa.22.23: And I will fasten him as a peg in a sure place,—And he shall become a throne of glory, to the house of his father;
texts.isa.22.24: And they shall hang upon him all the weight of his father’s house—The offshoots and the side-twigs—All the small vessels, Both the cups and all the jugs
texts.isa.22.25: In that day,—Declareth Yahweh of hosts Shall the peg, give way, that was fastened in a sure place,—Yea it shall be cut off and fall And the burden that was upon it shall perish, For, Yahweh, hath spoken!
texts.isa.23.1: The oracle on Tyre,—Howl! ye ships of Tarshish, For it is laid too waste to be a haven to enter, From the land of Cyprus, hath it been unveiled to them.
texts.isa.23.2: Be dumb, ye inhabitants of the Coast,—Whom the merchants of Zidon, passing over the sea, once replenished;
texts.isa.23.3: Yea on mighty waters, was the grain of Shihor, The harvest of the Nile, was her increase,—And so she became a mart of nations.
texts.isa.23.4: Turn thou pale, O Zidon, For spoken hath the sea, the fortress of the sea saying,—I have neither been in pangs nor given birth I have neither brought up young men nor promoted virgins.
texts.isa.23.5: Like the report of Egypt, They shall be in pangs at the like report of Tyre.
texts.isa.23.6: Pass ye over to Tarshish,—Howl ye inhabitants of the Coast:
texts.isa.23.7: Is this to you an exultation? Though from ancient days, is her antiquity, Yet shall her own feet carry her away, far off to dwell.
texts.isa.23.8: Who hath purposed this, against Tyre, The bestower of crowns,—Whose merchants are princes, Her traders the honourable of the earth?
texts.isa.23.9: Yahweh of hosts, hath purposed it,—To humble the pride of all beauty, To make of little esteem all the honourable of the earth.
texts.isa.23.10: Pass through thy land as the Nile,—O daughter of Tarshish, there is no restraint any longer!
texts.isa.23.11: His hand, hath he stretched out over the sea, He hath shaken kingdoms,—Yahweh, hath given command against the Phoenician coast, To destroy her fortresses.
texts.isa.23.12: Therefore hath he said,—No more, again, do thou exult, Thou violated virgin daughter of Zidon,—To Cyprus, arise and pass over, Even there, shall one find thee no rest.
texts.isa.23.13: Lo! the land of the Chaldeans, This is the people that was not, Assyria, founded it for the inhabitants of the desert,—They set up its siege-towers, They demolished its palaces Made it a ruin!
texts.isa.23.14: Howl, ye ships of Tarshish,—For laid waste is your fortress.
texts.isa.23.15: So shall it be in that day, That Tyre shall be forgotten seventy years, According to the days of a certain king: At the end of seventy years, shall it befall Tyre according to the song of the harlot:
texts.isa.23.16: Take thou a lyre, Go round the city, O harlot forgotten,—Sweetly touch the strings Lengthen out the song, That thou mayest be called to mind.
texts.isa.23.17: So shall it be, at the end of seventy years, That Yahweh will visit Tyre, And she will return to her hire,—Yea she will play the harlot—with all the kingdoms of the earth, upon the face of the ground.
texts.isa.23.18: But her merchandise and her hire, shall be hallowed unto Yahweh, It shall not be stored up, nor hoarded,—For, to them who dwell before Yahweh, shall her merchandise belong, That they may eat to satisfaction And have stately apparel.
texts.isa.24.1: Lo! Yahweh emptying the earth and laying it waste,—And he will overturn the face thereof, And scatter them who dwell therein.
texts.isa.24.2: And it shall be—As the people, so, the priest, As the servant, so his lord, As the maid, so, her mistress,—As the buyer, so, the seller, As the lender, so, the borrower, As the debtor, so! his creditor.
texts.isa.24.3: Emptied—emptied—shall be the earth yea pillaged—pillaged,—For, Yahweh, hath spoken this word.
texts.isa.24.4: Mourneth, fadeth, the earth Languisheth, fadeth, the world,—Languished have the lofty of the people of the earth.
texts.isa.24.5: Yea the earth itself is profaned under them who dwell therein,—For they have Set aside laws, Gone beyond statute, Broken an age-abiding covenant.
texts.isa.24.6: For this cause, a curse, hath devoured the earth, And punished are the dwellers therein,—For this cause, are burned the inhabitants of the earth, And the men left remaining—are few.
texts.isa.24.7: Mourneth the new wine. Withereth the vine,—Sighing are all the merryhearted:
texts.isa.24.8: Ceased hath the mirth of timbrels, Ended is the noise of the uproarious,—Ceased hath the mirth of the lyre:
texts.isa.24.9: With a song, they drink not wine,—Bitter is strong drink, to them who drink it:
texts.isa.24.10: Broken down is the city of desolation,—Shut up every house that it cannot be entered.
texts.isa.24.11: There is an outcry concerning wine in the streets,—Darkened is all joy, Departed the gladness of the earth.
texts.isa.24.12: There is left in the city. desolation,—And to ruins, have been broken the gate.
texts.isa.24.13: When, thus, it shall be in the earth in the midst of the peoples, [There shall be] like the shaking of an olive-tree, like the going round to pick when closed is the harvest.
texts.isa.24.14: They, shall lift up their voice—shall raise a tremulous note,—On account of the splendour of Yahweh, have they made a shrill cry, on the West;
texts.isa.24.15: For this cause, In the Regions of Light, give ye glory to Yahweh,—In the Coastlands of the Sea, unto the Name of Yahweh. God of Israel,
texts.isa.24.16: From the uttermost part of the earth, melodies, have we heard—Beauty, to the righteous one! But I had said—Ruin to me! Ruin to me! Woe to me! Traitors, have betrayed, Yea traitorously, have traitors betrayed!
texts.isa.24.17: Terror and pit and snare,—are upon thee, O inhabitant of the earth!
texts.isa.24.18: So shall it be—He that fleeth from the sound of the terror! shall fall into the pit, And, he that getteth up out of the midst of the pit, shall be captured in the snare,—For, the windows on high, have opened, And shaken are the foundations of earth.
texts.isa.24.19: The earth breaketh, breaketh,—The earth crasheth, crasheth, The earth tottereth, tottereth;
texts.isa.24.20: The earth staggereth—staggereth like a drunken man, And rocketh to and fro like a night-hut,—So shall be heavy upon her, her transgression, And she shall fall and not again rise.
texts.isa.24.21: And it shall be in that day, That Yahweh will bring punishment Upon the host of the height in the height,—And upon the kings of the ground on the ground.
texts.isa.24.22: And they shall be swept together in a crowd, fettered for a pit, And shall be lowered into a dungeon,—And, after many days, shall they be punished.
texts.isa.24.23: Then shall blush the silvery moon, Then turn pale the glowing sun,—Because Yahweh of hosts hath become king In Mount Zion And in Jerusalem, And before his Elders in glory,
texts.isa.25.1: O Yahweh! my God, thou art, I will exalt thee, I will praise thy Name, For thou hast done a wonderful thing,—Purposes of long ago Faithfulness in truth.
texts.isa.25.2: For thou hast made, of a citadel, a mound, of a defenced city, a ruin,—palaces for foreigners to be no city, To times age-abiding, shall it not be built.
texts.isa.25.3: For this cause! shall glorify thee—a strong people, the city of tyrannous nations shall revere thee;
texts.isa.25.4: For thou didst become A refuge to the weak. A refuge to the needy, when distress was upon him,—A shelter from the storm. A shade from the heat, When the blast of tyrants was like a storm against a wall.
texts.isa.25.5: As heat in a desert, the pomp of foreigners, wilt thou subdue,—Heat—with the shade of a cloud, The song of tyrants! become low.
texts.isa.25.6: Then will Yahweh of hosts prepare for all the peoples in this mountain, A banquet of fat things, A banquet of old wines,—Of fat things full of marrow, Of old wines well refined;
texts.isa.25.7: And he will swallow up in this mountain, The mask of the veil, the veil that is upon all the peoples,—And the web that is woven over all the nations.
texts.isa.25.8: Having swallowed up death itself victoriously, My Lord, Yahweh, will wipe away, tears from off all faces,—And the reproach of his own people, will he remove from off all the earth, For, Yahweh, hath spoken.
texts.isa.25.9: So shall it be said, in that day, Lo! our God, is this! We waited for him, that he might save us,—This, is Yahweh! We waited for him, Let us exult and rejoice in his salvation.
texts.isa.25.10: For the hand of Yahweh will settle down in this mountain,—Then shall Moab be trodden down in its place, Like the treading down of a strawheap in the water of a dunghill;
texts.isa.25.11: Should he spread forth his hands in the midst thereof, As a swimmer spreadeth forth to swim, Then would be laid low his pride, together with the devices of his hands.
texts.isa.25.12: Yea, the lofty stronghold of thy walls, Hath he brought down—Laid low—Levelled to the ground even unto the dust.
texts.isa.26.1: In that day, shall be sung this song, in the land of Judah,—A strong city, have we! Salvation, will he set for walls and rampart,
texts.isa.26.2: Open ye the gates,—That there may enter in—a righteous nation preserving fidelity.
texts.isa.26.3: A purpose sustained, thou wilt guard, [saying], Prosper! Prosper! Because in thee, hath he been led to trust.
texts.isa.26.4: Trust ye in Yahweh, unto futurity,—For, in Yah, Yahweh, is a rock of ages.
texts.isa.26.5: For he hath brought down the inhabitants of the height the city exalted,—He layeth it low, Layeth it low even to the ground, Levelleth it, even to the dust:
texts.isa.26.6: The foot trampleth it,—The feet of the lowly, The steps of the weak,
texts.isa.26.7: The path of a righteous man, is, even,—O Upright One! the track of a righteous man, thou makest level.
texts.isa.26.8: Surely in the path of thy regulations, O Yahweh, we waited for thee,—Unto thy Name and unto thy Memorial, was there a longing of soul:
texts.isa.26.9: With my soul, longed I for thee in the night, Yea with my spirit within me, I kept on searching for thee,—For, when thy regulations [extend] to the earth, The inhabitants of the world will have learned, righteousness.
texts.isa.26.10: Let favour be shewed to the lawless, he hath not learned righteousness, In a land of honest dealings, he acteth perversely,—And seeth not the splendour of Yahweh.
texts.isa.26.11: O Yahweh though thy hand be lifted up,—yet do they not see, Would they might see—and turn pale at a people’s zeal,—Surely, the fire of thine enemies, must consume them!
texts.isa.26.12: O Yahweh, thou wilt ensure prosperity for us,—For even all our works, hast thou wrought for us,
texts.isa.26.13: O Yahweh, our God! Lords other than thee, have owned us,—By thyself alone, will we call upon thy Name.
texts.isa.26.14: The dead, come not to life again, The shades, do not arise,—Therefore, thou hast visited and destroyed them, And caused to perish every memorial of them.
texts.isa.26.15: Thou hast increased the nation, O Yahweh, Thou hast increased the nation thou hast gotten thyself glory, Thou hast extended far, all the ends of the land.
texts.isa.26.16: O Yahweh! in distress, they sought thee,—They poured out a whispered prayer, when thy chastening was upon them.
texts.isa.26.17: Like as a woman with child—Draweth near to giving birth, Is in pain, Crieth out in her pangs So, were we before thee, O Yahweh;—
texts.isa.26.18: We were with child—We were in pain, As it were we brought forth wind,—Salvation, we could not accomplish for the earth, Neither were born the inhabitants of the world.
texts.isa.26.19: Thy dead, shall come to life again, My dead body, they shall arise,—Awake and shout for joy, ye that dwell in the dust For, a dew of light, is thy dew, And, earth, to the shades shall give birth.
texts.isa.26.20: Come my people, enter into thy chambers, And shut thy doors behind thee,—Hide thee as it were a little moment Till the indignation pass over.
texts.isa.26.21: For lo! Yahweh, is coming forth out of his place, To visit the iniquity of earth’s inhabitant upon him,—Therefore shall the earth unveil her shed-blood, And throw a covering, no longer over her slain.
texts.isa.27.1: In that day, will Yahweh With his sword—the hard and the great and the strong, Bring punishment Upon Leviathan, the fleeing serpent, And upon Leviathan, the crooked serpent,—And will slay the monster which is in the sea.
texts.isa.27.2: In that day, A Wine-Vineyard! sing ye unto her:
texts.isa.27.3: I—Yahweh, am Watching over her, Every moment, will I water her,—Lest anyone injure her, Night and day, will I watch over her.
texts.isa.27.4: Fury, have I none,—Oh that there were delivered to me briars and thorns, in battle! I would march in among them I would set fire to them one and all.
texts.isa.27.5: Else, let one lay hold of my protection, Let him make peace with me,—Peace, let him make with me.
texts.isa.27.6: In coming times, shall Jacob strike root, Israel, shall blossom and bud,—Then shall they fill the face of the world with fruit.
texts.isa.27.7: Was it, with the smiting of his smiter, that he smote him? Or as with the slaying of his slayer, was he slain?
texts.isa.27.8: By driving her away—by dismissing her, wouldest thou contend with her? He removed her by his rough wind in, a day of east wind.
texts.isa.27.9: Therefore hereby, shall a propitiatory—covering be put over the iniquity of Jacob, And all, this, is the fruit of taking away his sin,—When he maketh all the stones of an altar like chalk-stones that soon crumble, Sacred Stems and Sun Images, shall not arise.
texts.isa.27.10: For the fortified city, is solitary, The dwelling forsaken and left as a wilderness,—There, shall the calf feed, And, there, lie down And shall consume the branches thereof:
texts.isa.27.11: When the cut-off boughs thereof are dry, they shall be broken to pieces, Women, coming, are kindling it! For it is not a people of understanding, For this cause, Will he that made him, not have compassion upon him, And, he that formed him, will shew him no favour.
texts.isa.27.12: And it shall come to pass, in that day, That Yahweh will beat off his fruit from the stream of the River [="Euphrates"], unto the torrent-valley of Egypt,—And, ye, shall be picked up, one by one O sons of Israel.
texts.isa.27.13: And it shall come to pass in that day, That there shall be a blowing with a great horn, Then shall come in Such as have wandered in the land of Assyria, And such as have been outcasts in the land of Egypt,—And they shall bow themselves down unto Yahweh In the holy mountain, In Jerusalem.
texts.isa.28.1: Alas! for the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim, And for his fading wreath of majestic beauty,—Which is on the head of the fertile valley, of them who are overcome with wine.
texts.isa.28.2: Lo! My Lord hath one who is, strong and bold, Like a storm of hail, a destroying tempest, Like a storm of mighty waters overflowing, Hath he thrust it down to the earth with force:
texts.isa.28.3: With the feet shall be trodden down, the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim,
texts.isa.28.4: So shall his fading wreath of majestic beauty, Which is on the head of the fertile valley, become—Like the first-ripe fig before fruit-harvest, Which when he that looketh upon it seeth while it is yet in his hand, he swalloweth it up.
texts.isa.28.5: In that day, will Yahweh of hosts become A crown of beauty, and A diadem of majesty,—Unto the remnant of his people:
texts.isa.28.6: Even a spirit of justice—to him that presideth over justice, And strength to them who would turn back the battle at the gate.
texts.isa.28.7: But as for these, With wine, do they reel, and With strong drink, do they stagger,—Priest and prophet, reel with strong drink They are swallowed up through wine They stagger through strong drink, They reel in prophetic vision, They totter in pronouncing judgment.
texts.isa.28.8: For, all tables, are full of filthy vomit,—There is no place!
texts.isa.28.9: Whom, would he teach knowledge? And, whom, would he cause to understand the message? Them who are weaned from the milk? taken from the breasts?
texts.isa.28.10: For it is—Precept upon precept, precept upon precept, Line upon line, line upon line,—A little here a little there.
texts.isa.28.11: For, with a jabbering lip, and with an alien tongue, must he speak unto this people!
texts.isa.28.12: To whom he said—This, is the rest—give ye rest to the weary, and This, is the quietness,—But they were unwilling to hear.
texts.isa.28.13: So the word of Yahweh must be to them—Precept upon precept, precept upon precept, Line upon line, line upon line, A little here, a little there,—That they may go and fall backward and be torn and snared and captured.
texts.isa.28.14: Wherefore, hear ye the word of Yahweh, Ye men who scoff,—Ye rulers of this people that is in Jerusalem.
texts.isa.28.15: Because ye have said—We have solemnised a covenant with death, And with hades, have we effected a vision,—The overflowing scourge when it sweepeth by, shall not reach unto us, For we have made lying our refuge. And in falsehood, have we hid ourselves,
texts.isa.28.16: Therefore, Thus, saith My Lord, Yahweh, Behold me! founding in Zion a stone, A stone of testing, The costly corner of a well-laid foundation, he that trusteth, shall not make haste!
texts.isa.28.17: But I will make—Justice the line, and Righteousness the plummet,—And the hail shall, sweep away, your refuge of lying, And your hiding-place, the waters shall overflow;
texts.isa.28.18: So shall be wiped out your covenant with death, And your vision with hades, not stand,—When the overflowing scourge, sweepeth past, then shall ye be thereby beaten down:
texts.isa.28.19: As often as it sweepeth past, it shall take you away, For morning by morning, shall it pass along. By day and by night,—And it shall be nothing less than a terror to make out the message;
texts.isa.28.20: For too short is the couch to stretch oneself out,—And, the coverlet, too narrow, when one draweth up his feet.
texts.isa.28.21: For as in Mount Perazim, will Yahweh, arise, As in the vale of Gibeon, will he be stirred,—To do his work—foreign is his work, And to perform his task—strange is his task.
texts.isa.28.22: Now, therefore do not show yourselves scoffers, Lest your fetters, be bound fast,—For, of a full end, and that a decreed one, have I heard from My Lord, Yahweh of hosts upon all the land
texts.isa.28.23: Give ear, and hear ye my voice,—Hearken, and hear ye my speech:—
texts.isa.28.24: All day long, doth the plowman plow for sowing? Doth he continue laying open and harrowing his soil?
texts.isa.28.25: Doth he not when he hath levelled the face thereof, Cast abroad the fennel? And, the cummin, doth he not scatter? And plant wheat in rows, And barley in a lot, And spelt in the border thereof?
texts.isa.28.26: Yea One hath trained him to good judgment, His God, directeth him.
texts.isa.28.27: For not with a sledge, must, black coriander be threshed, Nor must, the wheel of a cart, on cummin, be turned, But with a staff, must fennel be beaten, And cummin with a rod:
texts.isa.28.28: Bread-corn, must be crushed,—Yet would he not be evermore, threshing, it, So he hasteneth over it the wheel of his cart, with his horsemen, He crusheth it not!
texts.isa.28.29: Even this, from Yahweh of hosts, cometh forth,—Who hath bestowed distinction upon counsel, And magnified sound wisdom.
texts.isa.29.1: Alas for Ariel, Ariel, The city against which, David encamped,—Add ye a year to a year. Let the festivals, come round;
texts.isa.29.2: Yet will I bring Ariel into straits,—And she shall become a bewailing and wailing, Yea she shall become to me a veritable Hearth of God.
texts.isa.29.3: And I will encamp round about against thee,—And lay siege against thee with a fort, And raise against thee siege-works;
texts.isa.29.4: And thou shalt be brought low—Out of the earth, shalt thou speak, And out of the dust, shalt thou lower thine utterance,—And as one that hath a familiar spirit, Out of the earth, shall come thy voice, And out of the dust, thy speech shall chirp;
texts.isa.29.5: Then shall be as fine dust the multitude of thy foreigners,—And as chaff that passeth away, the multitude of tyrants; And it shall come to pass, in a twinkling, Suddenly,
texts.isa.29.6: From Yahweh of hosts, shalt thou be visited, With thunder, and with earthquake and a great noise, hurricane and storm and flame of fire devouring;
texts.isa.29.7: And it shall be like the dream of a night vision, With the multitude of all the nations who have been making war against Ariel,—Even with all who have been making war against her and her stronghold and who have been laying siege to her;
texts.isa.29.8: Yea it shall be As when the hungry man dreameth and lo! he is eating, But he awaketh, and his soul, is empty, Or as when the thirsty man dreameth and lo! he is drinking, But he awaketh and lo! he is faint and his soul, is craving, So, shall it be with the multitude of all the nations, that have come forth to war against Mount Zion.
texts.isa.29.9: Stand ye stock still and stare, Besmear your eyes and be blind,—They are drunken but not with wine, They reel, but not with strong drink;
texts.isa.29.10: For Yahweh, hath poured out upon you, a spirit of deep sleep, Yea hath tightly shut your eyes—the prophets,—And, your heads—the seers, hath he covered,
texts.isa.29.11: And so all vision hath become unto you as the words of a writing that is sealed, Which is delivered unto one acquainted with writing, saying, Pray thee read this, And he saith, I cannot, for it is sealed;
texts.isa.29.12: And then the writing is delivered to one unacquainted with writing, saying, Pray thee read this, And he saith I am not acquainted with writing.
texts.isa.29.13: Wherefore My Lord hath said,—Because this people, hath drawn near with their mouth, And with their lips, have honoured me, But their heart, have they moved far from me, And so their reverence of me hath become A commandment of men in which they have been schooled,
texts.isa.29.14: Therefore, behold me! again dealing wonderfully with this people, doing wonderfully a wonderful thing,—So shall perish, the wisdom of their wise men, And the intelligence of their intelligent men, shall vanish!
texts.isa.29.15: Alas! for them who would fain have been too deep for Yahweh by giving secret counsel,—and therefore in the dark, have been their doings, and they have said Who can see us? and—Who can understand us?
texts.isa.29.16: Your perverseness! As if like clay, the potter could be reckoned; For shall, the thing made say of him that made it, he made me not? Or hath the thing fashioned ever said of him that fashioned it, He hath no understanding.
texts.isa.29.17: Is it not yet a very little while, And Lebanon shall be turned, into garden land,—And garden land, for a forest, be reckoned?
texts.isa.29.18: Therefore, in that day, shall the deaf hear the words of a book,—And out of gloom and darkness, the eyes of the blind shall see;
texts.isa.29.19: And again shall the humbled in Yahweh, have joy,—And the needy of mankind in the Holy One of Israel, exult;
texts.isa.29.20: For the tyrant, hath vanished, And the scoffer, is no more, Yea cut off are all who watch for iniquity:—
texts.isa.29.21: Who bring a man into condemnation with a rumour, And for him that decideth in the gate, lay a snare,—And have driven away, for a thing of nought, one who was righteous.
texts.isa.29.22: Therefore, Thus, saith Yahweh, concerning the house of Jacob, [even he saith it] who redeemed Abraham,—Not now, shall, Jacob turn pale, And, not now, shall their faces whiten;
texts.isa.29.23: For, when he seeth his children the work of my hands, in his midst, They will hallow my Name,—Yea they will hallow the Holy One of Jacob, And the God of Israel, will they regard with awe.
texts.isa.29.24: Then will they who erred in spirit comprehend, And the murmurers, accept instruction.
texts.isa.30.1: Alas! for sons who are rebellious, Declareth Yahweh. Executing a purpose, but not from me, And pouring out a libation but not from my spirit,—That they may add sin to sin:
texts.isa.30.2: Who are setting out to go down to Egypt, But at my mouth, have not asked,—Betaking them to the protection of Pharaoh And seeking refuge under the shadow of Egypt.
texts.isa.30.3: Therefore shall the protection of Pharaoh become to you a shame, And, the refuge in the shadow of Egypt, an insult;
texts.isa.30.4: For their princes have been, in Zoan,—And, their messengers unto Hanes, would draw near.
texts.isa.30.5: Every one, hath felt ashamed of a people that could not serve them,—Neither with help, nor with service, But they are a shame, yea even a reproach.
texts.isa.30.6: The Oracle on the Beasts of the South,—Through a land of distress and oppression—Lioness and lion coming therefrom, Viper and fiery flying serpent, They would carry, on the shoulders of young asses their wealth And on the humps of camels their treasures Unto a people that cannot serve them.
texts.isa.30.7: But, the Egyptians, with vanity and emptiness, would help,—Therefore have I proclaimed concerning this, Insolent, they sit still!
texts.isa.30.8: Now, enter—Write it upon a tablet before them And upon a scroll, inscribe it,—That it may serve for a later day, For futurity, unto times age-abiding:—
texts.isa.30.9: That it is, a rebellious people, Sons apt at deceiving,—Sons unwilling to hear the law of Yahweh:
texts.isa.30.10: Who have said to the seers, Ye must not see! To the prophets, Ye must not prophesy to us reproofs! Speak to us smooth things, Prophesy delusions:
texts.isa.30.11: Depart ye from the way, Turn aside from the path,—Desist from setting before us the Holy One of Israel.
texts.isa.30.12: Therefore—Thus, saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye have rejected this word,—And have trusted in oppression and perverseness, And have relied thereon,
texts.isa.30.13: Therefore, shall this iniquity become to you As a breach ready to fall, A bulging in a high wall,—Whose breaking down cometh, suddenly in a twinkling.
texts.isa.30.14: Yea he will break it—as the breaking of the pitcher of a potter, crushed, he will not spare; So that there shall not be found when it is smashed, A sherd wherewith to snatch fire from a hearth, Or to skim off water out of a cistern.
texts.isa.30.15: For thus, said my Lord Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel—By returning and resting, shall ye be saved, In keeping quiet and trusting, shall be your strength,—Howbeit ye would not!
texts.isa.30.16: But ye said,—Nay! but on horses, will we flee For this cause, shall ye indeed flee,—And on the swift, will we ride, For this cause, swift, shall be your pursuers:
texts.isa.30.17: One thousand, before the war-cry of one—before the war-cry of five, shall ye flee,—Until ye have been left, As a pole on the top of a mountain, And as an ensign upon a hill.
texts.isa.30.18: And, therefore, will Yahweh wait, That he may grant you favour, And, therefore, will he lift himself up, That he may show you compassion,—For A God of justice, is, Yahweh, How happy all they who are waiting for him
texts.isa.30.19: For, a people, In Zion, shall dwell, In Jerusalem,—As for weeping, thou shalt not weep! As for favour, he will grant thee favour, at the sound of thine outcry,—As soon as he heareth, he hath answered thee!
texts.isa.30.20: Though My Lord, should give you bread in short measure and water in scant allowance Yet will thy Teacher not hide himself any more, But thine eyes shall ever be looking on thy Teacher.
texts.isa.30.21: So shall, thine own ears, hear a word from behind thee saying,—This, is the way, walk ye therein, When ye would turn to the right hand Or when ye would turn to the left.
texts.isa.30.22: Then will ye defile—The overlaying of thy graven images of silver, And the coating of thy molten image, of gold,—Thou wilt cash them away, as a woman the token of her sickness, Begone! shalt thou say thereto,
texts.isa.30.23: Then will he give—Rain for thy seed—wherewith thou shalt sow thy ground and Bread as the increase of thy ground, which shall be fertile and fat,—Thy cattle, in that day, shall feed in broad pasture:
texts.isa.30.24: And the oxen and the young asses that till the ground, salted provender, shall eat, which hath been winnowed with shovel or fan.
texts.isa.30.25: Then shall there be, On every lofty mountain and On every lifted hill, Channels, Conduits of water,—In the great day of slaughter, When the towers fall.
texts.isa.30.26: Then shall the light of the moon, be as the light of the sun, And, the light of the sun, shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days,—In the day—When Yahweh, bindeth up, the laceration of his people, and When the severe wound caused by smiting them, he healeth.
texts.isa.30.27: Lo! the Name of Yahweh, coming in from afar, His anger kindling, A heavy storm,—His lips, are full of indignation, And, his tongue, is like a fire that devoureth;
texts.isa.30.28: And, his breath like an overflowing torrent, even unto the neck, doth reach, To sift nations with a sieve of calamity,—A bridle leading to ruin, being upon the jaws of the peoples.
texts.isa.30.29: A song, shall ye have, As in the night of hallowing a festival,—And gladness of heart, As when one goeth with the flute to enter Into the mountain of Yahweh Unto the Rock of Israel.
texts.isa.30.30: Then will Yahweh cause to be heard—the resounding of his voice And the bringing down of his arm, shall be seen, In a rage of anger, And with the flame of a devouring fire,—A burst and a downpour, and a hailstone!
texts.isa.30.31: For at the voice of Yahweh, shall Assyria be crushed,—With his rod, will he smite.
texts.isa.30.32: And it shall come to pass,—that, every stroke of the staff of doom which Yahweh shall lay upon him, shall be with timbrels and with lyres,—when, with battles of brandished weapons, he hath fought against them.
texts.isa.30.33: For there hath been set in order, beforehand a Topheth, Yea, the same, for the king, hath been prepared He hath made it deep—made it large,—The circumference thereof is for fire and wood in abundance, the breath of Yahweh, like a torrent of brimstone, is ready to kindle it.
texts.isa.31.1: Alas! for them who are going down to Egypt for help, On horses, would rely,—And have trusted—In chariots—because they are many, and In horsemen, because they are very bold, But have not looked unto the Holy One of Israel, And onto Yahweh, have not sought.
texts.isa.31.2: But, he also, is wise, and hath brought in calamity, And his own words, hath he not set aside,—Therefore will he rise up, Against the house of evil-doers, and Against the help of the workers of iniquity.
texts.isa.31.3: Now, the Egyptians, are, men, and not, GOD, And, their horses, flesh, and not, spirit; When, Yahweh, shall stretch out his hand, Then, he that is giving help, shall stumble And, he that is receiving help, shall fall, And, together, shall, all of them, vanish!
texts.isa.31.4: For Thus, hath Yahweh said unto me—Like as a lion or a young lion growleth over his prey. Who—though there be called out against him a multitude of shepherds—Will not at their voice, be dismayed, Nor, at their noise, be daunted, So, will Yahweh of hosts come down, to make war over Mount Zion, and over the hill thereof.
texts.isa.31.5: As little mother-birds hovering, so, will Yahweh of hosts throw a covering over Jerusalem,—Covering, so will he rescue, Passing over, so will he deliver!
texts.isa.31.6: Return ye unto him against whom the sons of Israel have deeply revolted,
texts.isa.31.7: For in that day, will every man reject his idols of silver, and his idols of gold,—Which your hands had made for you as a sin!
texts.isa.31.8: Then shall the Assyrian fall, by the sword, not of a great man, And the sword, not of a mean man, shall devour him,—Howbeit he shall take his flight from the face of a sword, And his young men, shall come under tribute;
texts.isa.31.9: And his own Cliff, through terror, shall he pass by, And his princes shall be dismayed at an ensign,—Declareth Yahweh. Who hath a flame in Zion, And hath a furnace in Jerusalem.
texts.isa.32.1: Lo! in righteousness, shall reign a king, Yea even princes, with equity, shall bear rule.
texts.isa.32.2: So shall each one become As a hiding-place from the wind And a covert from the storm,—As channels of water in a dry place, As the shadow of a massive cliff in a weary land.
texts.isa.32.3: And the eyes of them who are ready to see, shall not be closed,—And, the ears of them who are ready to hear, shall hearken;
texts.isa.32.4: And the heart of the hurried, shall take note of knowledge, And the tongue of stammerers, shall make haste to speak plainly.
texts.isa.32.5: A base man, shall no longer be called, noble,—Nor, a knave, be named, liberal;
texts.isa.32.6: For, a base man, with baseness, will speak, And, his heart, will practise iniquity,—Practising profanity, And speaking, against Yahweh that which misleadeth, Emptying the soul of the hungry, And the drink of the thirsty, he causeth to fail;
texts.isa.32.7: Yea, a knave, his weapons are wicked,—He, base schemes, hath devised To ruin the oppressed with speeches of falsehood Even when the needy pleadeth, for justice.
texts.isa.32.8: But, a noble man, noble things, hath devised,—And, he, upon noble things, will stand,
texts.isa.32.9: Ye women in comfort! arise hear my voice, Ye daughters so confident give ear to my speech:—
texts.isa.32.10: Some days beyond a year, ye shall be troubled ye confident ones,—For failed hath the vintage, No, gathering, cometh in.
texts.isa.32.11: Tremble, ye women in comfort, Be troubled ye daughters so confident,—Strip! and bare yourselves, and gird somewhat on your loins:
texts.isa.32.12: Upon your breasts, continue smiting: For desirable fields, For fruitful vine.
texts.isa.32.13: Over the soil of my people, thorns and briars shall grow,—Yea over all houses of joy, thou city exultant!
texts.isa.32.14: For the palace, is abandoned, the tumult of the city, hath ceased—Hill and watch-tower, serve as caves, unto times age-abiding, The joy of wild-asses, The pasture of flocks:—
texts.isa.32.15: Until there be poured out upon us the spirit, from on high,—Then shall the wilderness become, garden-land, And the garden-land, for a forest, be reckoned;
texts.isa.32.16: Then shall, justice inhabit, the wilderness, And righteousness, in the garden-land, shall abide;
texts.isa.32.17: And the yield of righteousness, shall be, peace,—And the tillage of righteousness, quietness, and confidence! to times age-abiding;
texts.isa.32.18: And my people shall dwell, In a borne of peace,—and In habitations of security, and In resting-places of comfort.
texts.isa.32.19: But it shall hail during the felling of the forest, And in a sunken place, shall, the city, sink.
texts.isa.32.20: How happy are ye who sow beside all waters,—Who send forth the foot of the ox and the ass.
texts.isa.33.1: Alas! thou plunderer when, thou, hadst not been plundered, And thou traitor when they had not betrayed thee: When thou hast ceased plundering, thou shalt be plundered, When thou hast left off betraying, they shall betray thee.
texts.isa.33.2: O Yahweh! shew us favour,—For thee, have we waited,—Be thou their arm every morning, Yea our salvation in the time of distress.
texts.isa.33.3: At the noise of a tumult, the peoples retreated,—When thou didst lift thyself up, nations were scattered.
texts.isa.33.4: Then shall your spoil be gathered as the gathering of the caterpillar,—As the swift running of locusts, is he about to run upon them.
texts.isa.33.5: Exalted is Yahweh, for he inhabiteth a height,—He hath filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
texts.isa.33.6: So shall a wealth of deliverances, wisdom and knowledge, become the stability of thy times,—the reverence of Yahweh, the same is his treasure.
texts.isa.33.7: Lo! their heroes, have cried out openly,—the messengers of peace, in bitterness, continue weeping [they say]:
texts.isa.33.8: The highways are deserted, The passer-by on the path, hath ceased,—He hath broken covenant, He hath despised cities, He hath made no account of men.
texts.isa.33.9: The land mourneth, languisheth, Lebanon, displayeth shame, is withered,—Sharon, hath become, as the waste plain, And Bashan and Carmel are shaking off their leaves.
texts.isa.33.10: Now, will I arise, Saith Yahweh, Now, will I lift myself up, Now, will I be exalted!
texts.isa.33.11: Ye shall conceive chaff Ye shall bring forth stubble,—Your own breath, like fire, shall devour you.
texts.isa.33.12: So shall peoples, become, as the burnings of lime,—As thorns lopped off, with fire, shall they be burned.
texts.isa.33.13: Hear—ye that are far off. what I have done, And know—ye that are near my might:
texts.isa.33.14: Terror-stricken in Zion,—are sinners, Shuddering hath seized the impious,—Who among us can sojourn with a fire that devoureth? Who among us can sojourn with burnings age-abiding?
texts.isa.33.15: He that walketh righteously, And speaketh uprightly,—He that refuseth the gain of exactions That shaketh his hands free from holding a bribe, That stoppeth his ear from hearkening to deeds of blood, And shutteth his eyes from giving countenance to wrong,
texts.isa.33.16: He, the heights, shall inhabit, A stronghold of crags, shall be his refuge,—His bread, hath been delivered, His waters, have been made sure,
texts.isa.33.17: Of a king, in his beauty, shall thine eyes have vision: They shall see a land that stretcheth afar.
texts.isa.33.18: Thy heart, may murmur in terror,—Where is the scribe? Where—the receiver? Where—he that maketh a list of the towers?
texts.isa.33.19: The fierce people, shalt thou not see,—The people of too deep a lip to be understood, of too barbarous a tongue for thee to comprehend.
texts.isa.33.20: Look thou on Zion, the city of our appointed feast,—Thine own eyes, shall see Jerusalem—A home of comfort A tent which shall not be packed up—Whose pins shall not be pulled out, for ever, And none of, whose cords, shall be broken.
texts.isa.33.21: But, there shall Yahweh be our majestic one, A place of rivers—streams broad on both hands, Wherein shall go no galley with oars, Neither shall majestic ship traverse it;
texts.isa.33.22: For, Yahweh is our judge, Yahweh, is our lawgiver,—Yahweh, is our king, He will save us!
texts.isa.33.23: Loosed are thy ropes,—They cannot strengthen the socket of their mast They have not unfurled a sail Now, can be apportioned spoil, in abundance, The lame, have captured prey!
texts.isa.33.24: Neither shall the inhabitant say. I am sick,—the people who dwell therein, have been forgiven iniquity.
texts.isa.34.1: Come near ye nations to hear, And, ye races, attend,—Let the earth hear, and the fulness thereof, The world and all things produced therefrom:
texts.isa.34.2: That Yahweh hath wrath against all the nations, and indignation against all their host,—He hath devoted them to destruction He hath delivered them to slaughter;
texts.isa.34.3: And their slain shall be cast out, And their carcases, the stench of them shall ascend,—And, the mountains, shall melt away with their blood.
texts.isa.34.4: Then shall be dissolved all the host of the heavens, And the heavens shall roll up as a scroll,—Yea, all their host, shall fade—Like the fading and falling of a leaf from a vine, and Like what fadeth and falleth from a fig-tree.
texts.isa.34.5: For my sword hath been sated in the heavens,—Lo! upon Edom, shall it descend, Even on the people whom I have devoted to justice.
texts.isa.34.6: A sword, hath Yahweh—Glutted with blood Sated with fat,—With the blood of well-fed lambs and he-goats, With the fat of the kidneys of rams,—For, a sacrifice, hath Yahweh in Bozrah, Yea a great slaughter in the land of Edom;
texts.isa.34.7: Then shall buffaloes come down with them, And bullocks with bulls,—So shall their land be soaked with blood, And, their dust, with fat, shall be enriched.
texts.isa.34.8: For a day of avenging, hath Yahweh,—A year of requitals for the quarrel of Zion.
texts.isa.34.9: Then shall the torrents thereof be turned into pitch, And the dust thereof, into brimstone,—So shall her land become burning pitch:
texts.isa.34.10: Neither night nor day, shall it be quenched, To times age-abiding, shall ascend the smoke thereof,—From generation to generation, shall it be waste, Never, never, shall any pass through it:
texts.isa.34.11: That the vomiting pelican and the bittern may possess it: And the great owl and the raven, dwell therein; Then will he stretch out over it The line of desolation, and The plummet of emptiness.
texts.isa.34.12: Her nobles (but none, are, there)! unto royalty, will call,—All, all her princes, shall become nought.
texts.isa.34.13: Then shall come up, in her palaces thorns Nettles and thistles in her fortresses,—And she shall become A home for wild dogs, An enclosure for ostriches;
texts.isa.34.14: Then shall criers meet with howlers, And, the shaggy creature, unto his fellow, shall call,—Only, there, shall, the night-spectre, Make her settlement, And find for herself a place of rest:
texts.isa.34.15: There, shall, the arrow-snake, Make her nest and lay, And hatch and gather under her shadow,—Only, there, shall be gathered the falcons, every one with her mate.
texts.isa.34.16: Seek ye out of the scroll of Yahweh, and read, Not, one from among them, is lacking, None, hath missed, her mate,—For, a mouth, hath, itself commanded, And, his spirit, hath itself gathered them:
texts.isa.34.17: Yea he himself, hath cast for them a lot, And his own hand, hath given to them a portion by line,—Unto times age-abiding, shall they possess it, To generation after generation, shall they dwell therein.
texts.isa.35.1: Wilderness and parched land, shall be glad for them,—And the waste plain, shall exult, and blossom as the lily:
texts.isa.35.2: It shall, blossom abundantly, and exult, Yea with exultation and shouts of triumph, The glory of Lebanon, hath been given to it, The splendour of Carmel, and Sharon,—They, shall see the glory of Yahweh, the splendour of our God.
texts.isa.35.3: Strengthen ye the weak hands,—The trembling knees, make ye firm:
texts.isa.35.4: Say to the hurried in heart, Be strong, Do not fear,—Lo! your God, with avenging, doth come, With the recompence of God, He, doth come to save you.
texts.isa.35.5: Then, shall be opened the eyes of the blind,—And, the ears of the deaf, be unstopped:
texts.isa.35.6: Then, shall leap as a hart the lame, Then shall shout the tongue of the dumb, For, there have broken forth—In the desert—waters, And streams, in the waste plain:
texts.isa.35.7: Then shall the glowing sand, become a lake, And thirsty ground—springs of water,—In the home of the wild dog—its lair, Shall be an enclosure for cane and paper—reed.
texts.isa.35.8: And there shall be there, a raised way—even a high road, And the Highroad of Holiness, shall it be called, There shall not pass over it one who is unclean; But He Himself, shall be one of them travelling the road, And the perverse, shall not stray [thereinto].
texts.isa.35.9: There shall be, there, no lion, Nor shall ravenous beast, go up thereon, It shall not be found, there,—Thus, shall travel the redeemed;
texts.isa.35.10: And the ransomed of Yahweh! shall return, And shall enter Zion with shouting, With gladness age-abiding, upon their head, Joy and gladness shall overtake them, And sorrow and sighing, shall flee away.
texts.isa.36.1: Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up, against all the fortified cities of Judah and took them.
texts.isa.36.2: Then did the king of Assyria send Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem unto King Hezekiah with a heavy force,—and he took his stand by the upper channel of the pool, in the highway of the fuller’s field.
texts.isa.36.3: And there went out to him—Eliakim son of Hilkiah who was over the household,—and Shebna, the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder.
texts.isa.36.4: And Rabshakeh said unto them, Pray you say unto Hezekiah,—Thus, saith the great king, the king of Assyria, What is this trust, wherewith thou dost trust?
texts.isa.36.5: I have said [sayest thou] —they are only words of the lips—Counsel and might have I for the war,—Now, upon whom dost thou trust, that thou hast rebelled against me?
